Sustituir `backend/app/api/v1/realm_settings.py` entero por (el nombre del archivo se queda: lo importan `main.py:306`
y las pruebas; la fase 4 puede renombrarlo):

```python
"""Settings -> Email: how this organization sends its account email.

Design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-autenticacion-propia-design.md` §7
("Correo de cuentas"); the surface itself is from
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-invisible-identity-layer-design.md` §2.1.

    GET  /api/v1/settings/email        orgs.manage
    PUT  /api/v1/settings/email        orgs.manage, on every client
    POST /api/v1/settings/email/test   orgs.manage, on every client

WHAT CHANGED ON 2026-11-04. These settings used to be written into the
identity provider's realm, which held the relay password and did the sending.
The platform now has its own sign-in and sends its own invitations and resets,
so the settings are one `account_mail_settings` row per organization and the
relay's password or Microsoft client secret is a vault credential
(`app/core/mail.py`, invariant 3). The wire shape is unchanged.

THIS ROUTE IS THIN ON PURPOSE. `app/core/mail.py` owns the storage, the vault
and the sending. What is here is the part that has to be here: the
permission, the tenant session, the audit record, and the body rules that
must not be field constraints.

THE PASSWORD (invariant 3)
--------------------------
It arrives in the PUT body, goes to the vault, and is never logged or
returned. `EmailSettingsOut` has no field that can carry it -- there is no key
to forget to strip -- and `tests/test_realm_settings_api.py` scans the RAW body
of all three routes for the literal rather than for the absence of a key,
because a renamed field would satisfy the weaker assertion while still
shipping the value.

`password` is OPTIONAL on the way in, and that is not a convenience. The
console cannot send back a value it never received, so "absent" has to mean
"leave the stored one alone" -- otherwise the first operator to correct a
display name writes an empty string over a working credential and finds out
when the next invitation fails.

THE MICROSOFT SIGN-IN (`auth_type="token"`) follows the same rules for its
client secret. The platform now performs the client-credentials exchange
itself, so the token URL is PINNED to Microsoft's own endpoint
(`mail.microsoft_tenant`): a configurable URL would be a place to send the
client secret to anyone. Switching modes CLEARS the other mode's credential in
the same write (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-mail-oauth-design.md` §3).

ONE ORGANIZATION'S SETTINGS. The realm was shared by every tenant; this row is
not. Writing it still needs `orgs.manage` on every client: one relay serves
every client of the organization (MSP clients spec §1.4).

AUDIT (invariant 4). One `email.settings_updated` per accepted save, recording
WHICH fields were supplied and none of their values (the log is append-only;
a value written into it can never be redacted, and one of these fields is a
password); one `email.test_requested` per test message; and one
`email.credential_used` for every vault checkout (`app/core/mail.py`). The save
and its record are one transaction.
"""

from typing import Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from app.api.deps import AuthContext, require_permission, require_permission_on_every_client
from app.core import rate_limit
from app.core.audit import audit_service
from app.core.i18n import tr
from app.core.identity.policy import resolve_console_domain
from app.core.mail import (
    MailNotConfigured,
    MailRecipientRefused,
    MailSendFailed,
    MailSettingsInput,
    failure_message,
    microsoft_tenant,
    pick_test_recipient,
    read_settings,
    save_settings,
    send_account_mail,
)
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.models.auth import AccountMailSettings

router = APIRouter(prefix="/settings", tags=["settings"])

MAX_HOST = 253
MAX_ADDRESS = 320
MAX_DISPLAY_NAME = 200
#: Long enough for any relay credential, short enough that the body is bounded.
MAX_PASSWORD = 512
#: Same bound and reasoning as MAX_PASSWORD, for an Azure client secret.
MAX_CLIENT_SECRET = 512
MAX_TOKEN_URL = 2048
#: Test messages one organization may send in a minute: enough to retry after
#: fixing a setting, too few to make this button a way to send mail in bulk --
#: the figure and the reason of `notification/api.py`'s test send.
TEST_SENDS_PER_MINUTE = 5

#: No control character in a field that reaches a mail header:
#: `email.policy.default` refuses a CR or LF by raising deep inside the send
#: (`app/modules/email_intake/identity.py` tells that story). None of these
#: fields is a secret, so a field failure echoing its input is acceptable.
_NO_CONTROL = r"^[^\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$"
#: The same, and no whitespace at all: a hostname or an address has none.
_NO_SPACE = r"^[^\s\x00-\x1f\x7f]*$"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# models
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


class EmailSettingsOut(BaseModel):
    """How this organization sends mail: the relay, the sender, and whether it
    is set up at all.

    NO FIELD HERE CAN CARRY A CREDENTIAL, and that is structural rather than
    careful: there is no password key to forget to strip. `authenticated` says
    only that a sign-in is configured.
    """

    configured: bool = Field(
        description=(
            "False when no relay is set, which is how a new organization starts. While it "
            "is false no invitation can be delivered, and the Users tab says so."
        )
    )
    host: str = Field(description="The relay's hostname. Empty when nothing is set.")
    port: str = Field(description="The relay's port. Empty when nothing is set.")
    from_address: str = Field(
        description="The address invitations and password-reset mails are sent from."
    )
    from_display_name: str = Field(description="The sender name a recipient sees.")
    reply_to: str = Field(description="Where replies go, if that differs from the sender.")
    encryption: str = Field(
        description="`none`, `starttls` or `ssl` -- how the connection to the relay is secured."
    )
    username: str = Field(description="The account this platform signs in to the relay as.")
    authenticated: bool = Field(
        description=(
            "True when the relay requires a sign-in and one is saved. The stored secret "
            "itself is never returned by this API."
        )
    )
    auth_type: str = Field(
        description=(
            "`password` or `token`. `token` means the relay sign-in uses a Microsoft 365 "
            "application; this platform obtains a token for each message and never stores it."
        )
    )
    # Named `microsoft_*`, not `token_*`: a response field whose name reads
    # as a secret is refused by the AI layer's scrubber (`core/secrets.py`).
    microsoft_client_id: str = Field(
        description=(
            "The application (client id) the Microsoft sign-in uses. Its secret is never "
            "returned by this API and has no field here."
        )
    )
    microsoft_sign_in_url: str = Field(
        description="Microsoft's token address the sign-in uses. Not a secret."
    )
    microsoft_scope: str = Field(
        description="What the Microsoft sign-in asks for access to. Not a secret."
    )
    suggested_test_recipient: str = Field(
        default="",
        description=(
            "Where the console proposes sending a test: the caller's own address with "
            "`+itms-test` before the @, which reaches the same inbox on Microsoft 365 and "
            "Gmail and is easy to find there. Empty when the caller's sign-in carries no "
            "usable address."
        ),
    )


class TestSendOut(BaseModel):
    """What came of sending a test message."""

    sent: bool = Field(
        description=(
            "True when the relay accepted the message for delivery. ACCEPTANCE IS NOT "
            "DELIVERY: a relay can accept a message and drop it silently, so the console "
            "names the mailbox to check rather than showing a tick."
        )
    )
    recipient: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "The mailbox the test went to: the address asked for, or the saved sending "
            "address when none was."
        ),
    )


class TestSendIn(BaseModel):
    """Where to send the test. `extra="forbid"`, and the body is optional: an
    empty POST still sends to the saved sending address."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    recipient: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        max_length=254,
        description=(
            "The sending address, the caller's own address (a `+tag` is fine), or an "
            "address in the organization's console sign-in domain. Anything else is "
            "refused: this is not a way to send mail to arbitrary addresses."
        ),
    )


def suggested_test_recipient(email: str) -> str:
    """`name+itms-test@domain` for the caller's own address, or "" if it is not
    one plausible address. An existing tag is replaced, not stacked."""
    if email.count("@") != 1:
        return ""
    local, domain = email.strip().split("@")
    local = local.split("+", 1)[0]
    if not local or "." not in domain:
        return ""
    return f"{local}+itms-test@{domain.lower()}"


class EmailSettingsIn(BaseModel):
    """`extra="forbid"`: a body carrying `smtpServer`, `org_id` or a stray key is
    a 422, not a silent no-op."""

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    host: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=MAX_HOST, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    port: int = Field(ge=1, le=65535)
    from_address: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=MAX_ADDRESS, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    from_display_name: str = Field(default="", max_length=MAX_DISPLAY_NAME, pattern=_NO_CONTROL)
    reply_to: str = Field(default="", max_length=MAX_ADDRESS, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    encryption: Literal["none", "starttls", "ssl"]
    username: str = Field(default="", max_length=MAX_ADDRESS, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    # NO `max_length` OR `pattern` HERE, AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. A
    # field-level constraint failure is reported by FastAPI with the offending
    # INPUT echoed into the 422 body -- which for this field would be the
    # password. The bound is enforced in `_refuse_unusable` instead, where the
    # refusal can name the rule without repeating the value.
    password: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Stored in the vault and never logged or returned by this platform. OMIT IT to "
            "keep the one already saved -- the console cannot send back a value it was never "
            "given, so an absent field must not clear a working credential."
        ),
    )
    auth_type: Literal["password", "token"] = Field(
        default="password",
        description="How the relay sign-in works. Defaults to `password`.",
    )
    token_url: str = Field(default="", max_length=MAX_TOKEN_URL, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    token_scope: str = Field(default="", max_length=500, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    token_client_id: str = Field(default="", max_length=200, pattern=_NO_SPACE)
    # No `max_length`, for the same reason `password` has none. Bounded in
    # `_refuse_unusable`.
    token_client_secret: str | None = Field(
        default=None,
        description=(
            "Stored in the vault and never logged or returned by this platform. OMIT IT to "
            "keep the one already saved."
        ),
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# body rules and translation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def _refuse_unusable(body: EmailSettingsIn) -> None:
    """The body checks that are NOT expressed as field constraints, because a
    model-level Pydantic failure echoes the WHOLE body, password included.

    1. A password with no username is REFUSED, not quietly dropped: no username
       means no sign-in and the save CLEARS the stored credential, so accepting
       a typed password would answer 200 to a request whose most sensitive
       field was discarded.
    2. The length bounds, which would otherwise put the secret in the 422.
    3. A Microsoft sign-in's required fields, and its token URL pinned to
       Microsoft's own endpoint (the platform presents the secret there).
    """
    if body.password is not None:
        if not body.username:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "a relay password needs a sign-in username; leave both blank for a relay "
                    "that needs no sign-in",
                ),
            )
        if len(body.password) > MAX_PASSWORD:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "the relay password may be at most {max_password} characters",
                    max_password=MAX_PASSWORD,
                ),
            )
    if body.auth_type == "token":
        if not body.username:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr("a Microsoft sign-in needs a username: the mailbox the relay sends as"),
            )
        if not body.token_client_id:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "a Microsoft sign-in needs an application (client id); choose Password "
                    "instead for a relay that signs in with one",
                ),
            )
        if not body.token_url:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr("a Microsoft sign-in needs a token URL"),
            )
        if microsoft_tenant(body.token_url) is None:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "a Microsoft sign-in's token URL must be Microsoft's own: "
                    "https://login.microsoftonline.com/<directory>/oauth2/v2.0/token"
                ),
            )
        if body.password is not None:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "a Microsoft sign-in does not use a relay password; the saved one is "
                    "removed when this is saved",
                ),
            )
    if body.token_client_secret is not None:
        if body.auth_type != "token" or not body.token_client_id:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "a client secret is only used by a Microsoft sign-in, and needs an "
                    "application (client id)",
                ),
            )
        if len(body.token_client_secret) > MAX_CLIENT_SECRET:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT,
                tr(
                    "the client secret may be at most {max_client_secret} characters",
                    max_client_secret=MAX_CLIENT_SECRET,
                ),
            )


def _values(body: EmailSettingsIn) -> MailSettingsInput:
    return MailSettingsInput(
        host=body.host,
        port=body.port,
        from_address=body.from_address,
        from_display_name=body.from_display_name,
        reply_to=body.reply_to,
        encryption=body.encryption,
        username=body.username,
        auth_type=body.auth_type,
        token_url=body.token_url,
        token_scope=body.token_scope,
        token_client_id=body.token_client_id,
    )


def _as_settings(row: AccountMailSettings | None, caller_email: str = "") -> EmailSettingsOut:
    suggestion = suggested_test_recipient(caller_email)
    if row is None:
        return EmailSettingsOut(
            configured=False,
            host="",
            port="",
            from_address="",
            from_display_name="",
            reply_to="",
            encryption="none",
            username="",
            authenticated=False,
            auth_type="password",
            microsoft_client_id="",
            microsoft_sign_in_url="",
            microsoft_scope="",
            suggested_test_recipient=suggestion,
        )
    return EmailSettingsOut(
        configured=bool(row.host),
        host=row.host,
        port=str(row.port),
        from_address=row.from_address,
        from_display_name=row.from_display_name,
        reply_to=row.reply_to,
        encryption=row.encryption,
        username=row.username,
        authenticated=bool(row.username) and row.credential_id is not None,
        auth_type="token" if row.auth_type == "token" else "password",
        microsoft_client_id=row.token_client_id,
        microsoft_sign_in_url=row.token_url,
        microsoft_scope=row.token_scope,
        suggested_test_recipient=suggestion,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# routes
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@router.get("/email", response_model=EmailSettingsOut)
async def read_email_settings(
    request: Request,
    ctx: AuthContext = Depends(require_permission("orgs.manage")),
) -> EmailSettingsOut:
    """How this organization sends mail today.

    `configured: false` for an organization that has not set it up -- a state,
    not a 404. Never opens the vault: `authenticated` is read off the row.
    """
    async with org_session(
        ctx.org_id, engine=request.app.state.app_engine, clients=ctx.clients
    ) as session:
        return _as_settings(await read_settings(session, ctx.org_id), ctx.claims.email)


@router.put("/email", response_model=EmailSettingsOut)
async def write_email_settings(
    body: EmailSettingsIn,
    request: Request,
    ctx: AuthContext = Depends(require_permission_on_every_client("orgs.manage")),
) -> EmailSettingsOut:
    """Save the relay settings, and answer with what is stored afterwards --
    never with what was typed (a fresh read, in its own session)."""
    _refuse_unusable(body)
    state = request.app.state
    supplied = sorted(body.model_fields_set)
    async with org_session(ctx.org_id, engine=state.app_engine, clients=ctx.clients) as session:
        await save_settings(
            session,
            state.vault,
            org_id=ctx.org_id,
            actor_id=ctx.user_id,
            values=_values(body),
            password=body.password,
            client_secret=body.token_client_secret,
        )
        await audit_service.record(
            session,
            org_id=ctx.org_id,
            actor_type="user",
            actor_id=ctx.user_id,
            action="email.settings_updated",
            target_type="email_settings",
            target_id="account_mail",
            # FIELD NAMES ONLY. `password` appearing here is a record that the
            # credential was rotated; its value never can be.
            metadata={"fields": supplied},
        )
        await session.flush()

    async with org_session(ctx.org_id, engine=state.app_engine, clients=ctx.clients) as session:
        return _as_settings(await read_settings(session, ctx.org_id), ctx.claims.email)


@router.post("/email/test", response_model=TestSendOut)
async def send_test_message(
    request: Request,
    body: TestSendIn | None = None,
    ctx: AuthContext = Depends(require_permission_on_every_client("orgs.manage")),
) -> TestSendOut:
    """Send a test message through the saved relay to the address asked for, or
    to the saved SENDING address when the body names none.

    The address must be the sending address, the caller's own (a `+tag` is
    fine), or one in the organization's console sign-in domain
    (`mail.pick_test_recipient`), so this route cannot become a way to send the
    organization's mail to anyone.

    A FAILED SEND IS CAUGHT INSIDE THE SESSION and refused after it: the vault
    checkout that signed in to the relay has already been audited in this
    session, and that record must survive the refusal (`app/core/mail.py`).

    A success means the relay ACCEPTED the message, not that it arrived.
    """
    state = request.app.state
    if not await rate_limit.hit(
        state.redis, f"email-test:org:{ctx.org_id}", limit=TEST_SENDS_PER_MINUTE, window_s=60
    ):
        raise HTTPException(
            status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
            tr("too many test messages for this organization; try again in a minute"),
        )
    failure: MailSendFailed | None = None
    async with org_session(ctx.org_id, engine=state.app_engine, clients=ctx.clients) as session:
        saved = await read_settings(session, ctx.org_id)
        if saved is None or not saved.host:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
                tr("no email settings are saved yet, so there is nothing to test"),
            )
        try:
            recipient = pick_test_recipient(
                body.recipient if body else None,
                sender=saved.from_address,
                caller_email=ctx.claims.email,
                org_domain=await resolve_console_domain(session, ctx.org_id, state.settings),
            )
        except MailRecipientRefused as exc:
            raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT, str(exc)) from exc
        try:
            await send_account_mail(
                session,
                org_id=ctx.org_id,
                to=recipient,
                subject=tr("ITMS test message"),
                text=tr(
                    "This is a test message from ITMS. It reached you, so this organization's "
                    "account email (invitations and password resets) is working."
                ),
                vault=state.vault,
                actor_id=ctx.user_id,
            )
        except MailNotConfigured as exc:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
                tr("no email settings are saved yet, so there is nothing to test"),
            ) from exc
        except MailSendFailed as exc:
            failure = exc
        else:
            await audit_service.record(
                session,
                org_id=ctx.org_id,
                actor_type="user",
                actor_id=ctx.user_id,
                action="email.test_requested",
                target_type="email_settings",
                target_id="account_mail",
                metadata={"recipient": recipient},
            )
        await session.flush()
    if failure is not None:
        raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_502_BAD_GATEWAY, failure_message(failure.reason))
    return TestSendOut(sent=True, recipient=recipient)
```

**Cómo se componen (para la Task 7).** Cada verificación de un factor va entre `check_allowed` y
`record_success`/`record_failure`, en una sesión que **confirma** (`commit`) aunque la respuesta sea un rechazo:

```python
async with org_session(org_id, engine=engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
    state = await failures.check_allowed(session, user_id, "totp", now=now)
    accepted = state.allowed and await totp.verify_totp(
        session, user_id, code, vault=vault, now=now
    )
    if state.allowed:
        if accepted:
            await failures.record_success(session, user_id, "totp")
        else:
            await failures.record_failure(
                session, org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id, factor="totp", now=now
            )
# The block has COMMITTED here. Refuse AFTER it: an HTTPException raised inside
# would roll the failure count back, and the counter would never reach 100.
if not accepted:
    raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, ...)  # generic message (§2.3)
```

**Decisión del plan (1): la bóveda y la organización se pasan como argumentos.** El Apéndice A escribía
`verify_totp(session, user_id, code, *, now)`, `replace_codes(session, user_id)` y `record_failure(...)`. Abrir el
secreto necesita la bóveda (`app.state.vault`, como en todo el árbol: `backup/repository.py:72`,
`email_intake/oauth.py:109`), e insertar una fila necesita su `org_id`. Se añaden como argumentos con nombre; el orden
posicional de la interfaz se conserva.

**Decisión del plan (2): un TOTP «pendiente» es una fila con `last_step` NULL.** La tabla de la Task 1 no tiene columna
de confirmación, y el alta del primer factor (Task 7: `enroll/totp/start` y `enroll/totp/confirm`) necesita guardar el
secreto entre las dos llamadas. Una fila cuyo `last_step` es NULL nunca aceptó un código: no es un factor
(`verify_totp` y `has_totp` la ignoran); `confirm_secret` es lo único que acepta contra ella, y al aceptar escribe
`last_step`, que es lo que la convierte en factor. `stage_secret` nunca sustituye una fila confirmada
(`TotpAlreadyEnrolled`): quitar un factor es otro acto (`remove_totp`), con su confirmación reciente arriba (§2.5).

**Decisión del plan (3): los códigos de recuperación se guardan con argon2id al mínimo de OWASP, sin pepper.** Un
código son 10 símbolos Crockford: 50 bits. NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.2.2, leído el 2026-11-04 en
https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html: *«Look-up secrets that are shorter than the minimum security strength
specified in the latest revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication) SHALL be stored
in a salted and hashed form using a suitable password hashing scheme, as described in [Sec. 3.1.1.2]. The salt value
SHALL be at least 32 bits in length … Both the salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored for each look-up
secret.»* Un SHA-256 a secas no lo cumple. Se usa argon2id con sal aleatoria de 16 bytes por código y los parámetros
mínimos de OWASP, *«m=19456 (19 MiB), t=2, p=1»* [S4], no los de las contraseñas (64 MiB, t=3, p=4): un intento con
código de recuperación se compara con hasta diez hashes. Sin pepper: necesitaría una versión de clave por fila que
`auth_recovery_codes` no tiene, y el hash con sal es lo que §3.1.2.2 pide.

**Decisión del plan (4): la espera.** «Desde el 5.º fallo, espera creciente: 1 s, duplicando hasta 15 min»: tras el
fallo consecutivo número `n`, el siguiente intento espera `min(2 ** (n - 5), 900)` segundos desde ese fallo, para
`n ≥ 5`. Del 1.º al 4.º no hay espera; el 5.º da 1 s, el 6.º 2 s, …, el 14.º 512 s y del 15.º en adelante 900 s
(2¹⁰ = 1024 > 900). Es la forma de NIST §3.2.2 (*«wait after a failed attempt for a period of time that increases as
the subscriber account approaches its maximum allowance»*) y de OWASP [S5] (*«starts as a very short period (e.g., one
second), but doubles after each failed login attempt»*). Un intento durante la espera no se verifica ni se cuenta.

**Decisión del plan (5): esta tarea audita el bloqueo, dentro de `record_failure`.** El paso a «desactivado» solo es
visible allí (el `RETURNING` del contador). D16: los fallos no entran en la cadena (no la inundan); el bloqueo sí.
El Apéndice A pone `auth.factor_disabled` en la lista de la Task 8: la entrada del vocabulario la añade esta tarea
y la Task 8 no la repite.

**Decisión del plan (6): `secret_sealed` es `BYTEA` (Task 1) y `seal_bytes` devuelve un `str` ASCII**
(`vault.py:203`); se guarda como `sealed.encode("ascii")`. Los precedentes del árbol usan `Text`
(`licenses/models.py:83`, `email_intake/models.py:174`); si la Task 1 lo deja en `Text`, sobran el `.encode` y el
`.decode` de `totp.py` y nada más cambia.

**Decisión del plan (7): un acierto no revive un factor desactivado, y renovar el secreto no borra los fallos.**
`record_success` solo borra filas sin `disabled_at` (*«Authenticators that have been disabled SHALL be required to
rebind»*, NIST §3.2.2); `reset_factor` es el acto del administrador. `replace_codes` y `stage_secret` no tocan
`auth_failures` (NIST §3.1.3, de los secretos fuera de banda, aplicado por analogía: *«Generating a new authentication
secret SHALL NOT reset the failed authentication count»*).

#### Parte A — fallos, espera y bloqueo

- [ ] **Step 2: Escribir las pruebas de los fallos**

Crear `backend/tests/test_auth_failures.py` (la siembra copia `tests/test_backup_repository.py:17-24`):

```python
"""Failed attempts per person and per factor: `app/core/auth/failures.py`.

Design §2.3 and falsifier §10.3: counted per account and per factor, never per
address alone [S5]; from the 5th consecutive failure a wait of 1 s that
doubles up to 15 min; at 100 the factor is disabled until an administrator
restores it [S1 §3.2.2]; a success clears that factor's failures.
"""

import asyncio
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession

from app.core.auth import failures
from app.core.auth.failures import Factor, FactorState
from app.core.client_scope import ClientScope
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.models import AuditEvent, Organization, User
from app.models.auth import AuthFailure

NOW = datetime(2026, 11, 4, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


@dataclass
class _World:
    org_id: UUID
    user_id: UUID
    app_engine: AsyncEngine
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine


async def _person(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, org_id: UUID | None = None) -> tuple[UUID, UUID]:
    async with AsyncSession(admin_engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        if org_id is None:
            slug = f"fail-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"
            org = Organization(name=slug, slug=slug)
            session.add(org)
            await session.flush()
            org_id = org.id
        user = User(
            org_id=org_id,
            external_subject=f"sub-{uuid4().hex[:10]}",
            email=f"{uuid4().hex[:8]}@toeshee.com",
        )
        session.add(user)
        await session.commit()
        return org_id, user.id


@pytest.fixture()
async def world(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine) -> _World:
    org_id, user_id = await _person(admin_engine)
    return _World(org_id, user_id, app_engine, admin_engine)


async def _fail(
    w: _World,
    factor: Factor = "totp",
    *,
    times: int = 1,
    at: datetime = NOW,
    user_id: UUID | None = None,
) -> FactorState:
    state: FactorState | None = None
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        for _ in range(times):
            state = await failures.record_failure(
                session, org_id=w.org_id, user_id=user_id or w.user_id, factor=factor, now=at
            )
    assert state is not None
    return state


async def _check(
    w: _World, factor: Factor = "totp", *, at: datetime = NOW, user_id: UUID | None = None
) -> FactorState:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await failures.check_allowed(session, user_id or w.user_id, factor, now=at)


async def _succeed(w: _World, factor: Factor = "totp") -> None:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        await failures.record_success(session, w.user_id, factor)


async def _consecutive(w: _World, factor: Factor = "totp") -> int | None:
    async with AsyncSession(w.admin_engine) as session:
        value: int | None = await session.scalar(
            select(AuthFailure.consecutive).where(
                AuthFailure.user_id == w.user_id, AuthFailure.factor == factor
            )
        )
        return value


async def _audit(w: _World) -> list[AuditEvent]:
    async with AsyncSession(w.admin_engine) as session:
        return list(
            (
                await session.execute(
                    select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.org_id == w.org_id).order_by(AuditEvent.id)
                )
            ).scalars()
        )


ALLOWED = FactorState(allowed=True, wait_s=0, disabled=False)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("consecutive", "wait"),
    [(0, 0), (4, 0), (5, 1), (6, 2), (7, 4), (14, 512), (15, 900), (99, 900)],
)
def test_the_wait_starts_at_the_fifth_failure_and_doubles_to_fifteen_minutes(
    consecutive: int, wait: int
) -> None:
    assert failures.backoff_s(consecutive) == wait


async def test_a_factor_with_no_failures_is_allowed(world: _World) -> None:
    assert await _check(world) == ALLOWED


async def test_four_failures_do_not_wait(world: _World) -> None:
    await _fail(world, times=4)

    assert await _check(world) == ALLOWED


async def test_the_fifth_failure_waits_one_second(world: _World) -> None:
    """`backoff_s` and `_state`'s comparison with `last_failed_at`: remove
    either and the attempt at NOW is allowed."""
    state = await _fail(world, times=5)

    assert state == FactorState(allowed=False, wait_s=1, disabled=False)
    assert await _check(world) == FactorState(allowed=False, wait_s=1, disabled=False)
    assert await _check(world, at=NOW + timedelta(seconds=1)) == ALLOWED


async def test_the_wait_doubles(world: _World) -> None:
    await _fail(world, times=7)

    assert await _check(world, at=NOW + timedelta(seconds=1)) == FactorState(
        allowed=False, wait_s=3, disabled=False
    )
    assert await _check(world, at=NOW + timedelta(seconds=4)) == ALLOWED


async def test_the_wait_stops_at_fifteen_minutes(world: _World) -> None:
    await _fail(world, times=30)

    assert await _check(world) == FactorState(allowed=False, wait_s=900, disabled=False)
    assert await _check(world, at=NOW + timedelta(minutes=15)) == ALLOWED


async def test_the_hundredth_failure_disables_the_factor_and_audits_it_once(world: _World) -> None:
    """Falsifier §10.3, first half. `DISABLE_AT` and the `case(...)` in the
    upsert: remove it and the factor is never disabled; and the audit fires on
    the transition only, not on the 101st."""
    assert not (await _fail(world, times=99)).disabled

    assert await _fail(world) == FactorState(allowed=False, wait_s=0, disabled=True)
    await _fail(world)

    assert await _check(world, at=NOW + timedelta(days=365)) == FactorState(
        allowed=False, wait_s=0, disabled=True
    )
    (event,) = [e for e in await _audit(world) if e.action == "auth.factor_disabled"]
    assert (event.actor_type, event.actor_id) == ("system", None)
    assert (event.target_type, event.target_id) == ("user", str(world.user_id))
    assert event.meta["factor"] == "totp"
    assert event.meta["consecutive"] == failures.DISABLE_AT


async def test_a_success_clears_that_factors_failures(world: _World) -> None:
    await _fail(world, times=6)

    await _succeed(world)

    assert await _check(world) == ALLOWED
    assert await _consecutive(world) is None


async def test_a_success_does_not_revive_a_disabled_factor(world: _World) -> None:
    """Decisión del plan 7: only an administrator restores it."""
    await _fail(world, times=failures.DISABLE_AT)

    await _succeed(world)

    assert (await _check(world)).disabled


async def test_an_administrator_reset_restores_the_factor(world: _World) -> None:
    await _fail(world, times=failures.DISABLE_AT)

    async with org_session(
        world.org_id, engine=world.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()
    ) as session:
        await failures.reset_factor(session, world.user_id, "totp")

    assert await _check(world) == ALLOWED


async def test_factors_and_people_are_counted_apart(world: _World) -> None:
    """Per account AND per factor [S5]: a wall of TOTP failures says nothing
    about the password, nor about a colleague."""
    _org, colleague = await _person(world.admin_engine, world.org_id)
    await _fail(world, "totp", times=20)

    assert await _check(world, "password") == ALLOWED
    assert await _check(world, "totp", user_id=colleague) == ALLOWED


async def test_concurrent_failures_are_all_counted(world: _World) -> None:
    """The single-statement upsert: a read-then-write counter would lose
    increments to concurrent attempts, and an attacker could run attempts in
    parallel to stay under 100."""
    await asyncio.gather(*[_fail(world) for _ in range(10)])

    assert await _consecutive(world) == 10
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Escribir `failures.py`**

Crear `backend/app/core/auth/failures.py`:

```python
"""Failed attempts per person and per factor: the wait, and the stop at 100.

Design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-autenticacion-propia-design.md` §2.3.

* COUNTED PER ACCOUNT AND PER FACTOR, never per address alone. OWASP: "The
  counter of failed logins should be associated with the account itself,
  rather than the source IP address" [S5]. Per-address limits are a second
  layer (`app/core/rate_limit.py`), not this one.
* THE WAIT. From the `BACKOFF_FROM`-th consecutive failure the next attempt
  waits `2 ** (n - BACKOFF_FROM)` seconds after the n-th, capped at
  `BACKOFF_CAP_S`: 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... 15 min. NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.2.2 names the
  technique ("wait after a failed attempt for a period of time that increases
  as the subscriber account approaches its maximum allowance") and OWASP its
  shape ("starts as a very short period (e.g., one second), but doubles after
  each failed login attempt"). An attempt during the wait is not verified and
  not counted: the caller asks `check_allowed` first.
* THE STOP. NIST §3.2.2: "the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed
  authentication attempts using a specific authenticator on a single
  subscriber account to no more than 100 by disabling that authenticator."
  At `DISABLE_AT` the row gets `disabled_at`, and that is audited -- once, on
  the transition. A success does NOT clear a disabled factor ("Authenticators
  that have been disabled SHALL be required to rebind"); `reset_factor` is the
  administrator's act.
* A SUCCESS CLEARS THE COUNT (NIST: "the verifier SHOULD disregard any
  previous failed attempts for the authenticators used in the successful
  authentication").

THE FAILURES THEMSELVES ARE NOT AUDITED (D16): a failed attempt for an account
that may not exist has no organization to chain to, and one row per wrong
code would flood the chain. The lockout is.

ONE STATEMENT PER FAILURE. `record_failure` is an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO
UPDATE ... RETURNING: concurrent attempts each add one, so running attempts in
parallel does not stay under 100.

THE CALLER'S SESSION MUST COMMIT. Verify, record, close the session block,
and refuse AFTER it: an HTTPException raised inside the block rolls the
failure back, and the counter never reaches 100.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from math import ceil
from typing import Literal
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import case, delete, func, select
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core.audit import audit_service
from app.models import User
from app.models.auth import AuthFailure

__all__ = [
    "BACKOFF_CAP_S",
    "BACKOFF_FROM",
    "DISABLE_AT",
    "Factor",
    "FactorState",
    "backoff_s",
    "check_allowed",
    "record_failure",
    "record_success",
    "reset_factor",
]

Factor = Literal["password", "totp", "passkey", "recovery"]

#: The consecutive failure from which the next attempt waits.
BACKOFF_FROM = 5
#: The longest wait, in seconds: 15 minutes.
BACKOFF_CAP_S = 900
#: Consecutive failures that disable the factor (NIST's upper bound).
DISABLE_AT = 100


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FactorState:
    """May the person try this factor now? `wait_s` is how long until they may,
    when they may not yet; `disabled` means only an administrator can say yes."""

    allowed: bool
    wait_s: int
    disabled: bool


def backoff_s(consecutive: int) -> int:
    """Seconds the next attempt waits after `consecutive` failures in a row."""
    if consecutive < BACKOFF_FROM:
        return 0
    return min(2 ** (consecutive - BACKOFF_FROM), BACKOFF_CAP_S)


def _state(
    consecutive: int, last_failed_at: datetime, disabled_at: datetime | None, now: datetime
) -> FactorState:
    if disabled_at is not None:
        return FactorState(allowed=False, wait_s=0, disabled=True)
    wait = backoff_s(consecutive)
    remaining = (last_failed_at + timedelta(seconds=wait) - now).total_seconds()
    if wait == 0 or remaining <= 0:
        return FactorState(allowed=True, wait_s=0, disabled=False)
    return FactorState(allowed=False, wait_s=ceil(remaining), disabled=False)


async def check_allowed(
    session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID, factor: Factor, *, now: datetime | None = None
) -> FactorState:
    row = (
        await session.execute(
            select(AuthFailure).where(AuthFailure.user_id == user_id, AuthFailure.factor == factor)
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if row is None:
        return FactorState(allowed=True, wait_s=0, disabled=False)
    return _state(row.consecutive, row.last_failed_at, row.disabled_at, now or datetime.now(UTC))


async def record_failure(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    user_id: UUID,
    factor: Factor,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> FactorState:
    """Count one failure and answer the state it leaves. At `DISABLE_AT` the
    factor is disabled and the lockout is audited, exactly once."""
    at = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    upsert = (
        pg_insert(AuthFailure)
        .values(
            org_id=org_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            factor=factor,
            consecutive=1,
            last_failed_at=at,
            disabled_at=None,
        )
        .on_conflict_do_update(
            index_elements=["user_id", "factor"],
            set_={
                "consecutive": AuthFailure.consecutive + 1,
                "last_failed_at": at,
                "disabled_at": case(
                    (
                        AuthFailure.consecutive + 1 >= DISABLE_AT,
                        func.coalesce(AuthFailure.disabled_at, at),
                    ),
                    else_=AuthFailure.disabled_at,
                ),
            },
        )
        .returning(AuthFailure.consecutive, AuthFailure.disabled_at)
    )
    consecutive, disabled_at = (await session.execute(upsert)).one()
    if consecutive == DISABLE_AT:
        await audit_service.record(
            session,
            org_id=org_id,
            actor_type="system",
            actor_id=None,
            action="auth.factor_disabled",
            target_type="user",
            target_id=str(user_id),
            metadata={"factor": factor, "consecutive": consecutive},
            # Informative: a contact's own client, NULL for a technician.
            client_id=await session.scalar(select(User.client_id).where(User.id == user_id)),
        )
    return _state(consecutive, at, disabled_at, at)


async def record_success(session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID, factor: Factor) -> None:
    """Clear the factor's failures -- unless it is disabled, which only
    `reset_factor` undoes."""
    await session.execute(
        delete(AuthFailure).where(
            AuthFailure.user_id == user_id,
            AuthFailure.factor == factor,
            AuthFailure.disabled_at.is_(None),
        )
    )


async def reset_factor(session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID, factor: Factor) -> None:
    """An administrator's act (design §7, "Restablecer factores"), audited by
    the caller: the factor's count and its disabled state go."""
    await session.execute(
        delete(AuthFailure).where(AuthFailure.user_id == user_id, AuthFailure.factor == factor)
    )
```

#### Parte B — TOTP

- [ ] **Step 8: Escribir las pruebas de TOTP**

Crear `backend/tests/test_auth_totp.py`:

```python
"""TOTP: `app/core/auth/totp.py` (design §2.2, falsifier §10.3).

RFC 6238 with a 30-second step, six digits and one step of tolerance either
way; a code accepted once is never accepted again, which `pyotp` 2.10.0 does
not do for us [S43]; the secret is sealed by the vault and bound to its
person. The expected codes are computed with `pyotp`; the RFC 6238 Appendix B
vectors pin the algorithm independently of it.
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pyotp
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession

from app.core.auth import totp
from app.core.client_scope import ClientScope
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.core.vault import LocalVaultService
from app.models import Organization, User
from app.models.auth import AuthTotp

NOW = datetime(2026, 11, 4, 12, 0, 15, tzinfo=UTC)
STEP = int(NOW.timestamp()) // 30
FIXED = bytes(range(20))


def _code(secret: bytes, step: int) -> str:
    return pyotp.TOTP(base64.b32encode(secret).decode("ascii")).generate_otp(step)


@dataclass
class _World:
    org_id: UUID
    user_id: UUID
    vault: LocalVaultService
    app_engine: AsyncEngine
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine


async def _person(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, org_id: UUID | None = None) -> tuple[UUID, UUID]:
    async with AsyncSession(admin_engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        if org_id is None:
            slug = f"totp-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"
            org = Organization(name=slug, slug=slug)
            session.add(org)
            await session.flush()
            org_id = org.id
        user = User(
            org_id=org_id,
            external_subject=f"sub-{uuid4().hex[:10]}",
            email=f"{uuid4().hex[:8]}@toeshee.com",
        )
        session.add(user)
        await session.commit()
        return org_id, user.id


@pytest.fixture()
async def world(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine, tmp_path: Path) -> _World:
    org_id, user_id = await _person(admin_engine)
    vault = LocalVaultService(tmp_path / "root.key")
    return _World(org_id, user_id, vault, app_engine, admin_engine)


async def _stage(w: _World, secret: bytes, *, user_id: UUID | None = None) -> None:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        await totp.stage_secret(
            session, org_id=w.org_id, user_id=user_id or w.user_id, secret=secret, vault=w.vault
        )


async def _confirm(
    w: _World, code: str, *, at: datetime = NOW, user_id: UUID | None = None
) -> bool:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await totp.confirm_secret(
            session, user_id or w.user_id, code, vault=w.vault, now=at
        )


async def _verify(
    w: _World, code: str, *, at: datetime = NOW, user_id: UUID | None = None
) -> bool:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await totp.verify_totp(session, user_id or w.user_id, code, vault=w.vault, now=at)


async def _has(w: _World) -> bool:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await totp.has_totp(session, w.user_id)


async def _enrolled(
    w: _World, secret: bytes | None = None, *, user_id: UUID | None = None
) -> bytes:
    """A confirmed factor whose last accepted step is ten minutes before NOW, so
    the tests at NOW start from a clean window."""
    secret = secret or totp.new_secret()
    await _stage(w, secret, user_id=user_id)
    earlier = NOW - timedelta(minutes=10)
    assert await _confirm(w, _code(secret, totp.step_of(earlier)), at=earlier, user_id=user_id)
    return secret


async def _last_step(w: _World) -> int | None:
    async with AsyncSession(w.admin_engine) as session:
        value: int | None = await session.scalar(
            select(AuthTotp.last_step).where(AuthTotp.user_id == w.user_id)
        )
        return value


async def _sealed(w: _World, user_id: UUID) -> bytes:
    """The stored column, read on the ADMIN engine: what a database dump holds."""
    async with AsyncSession(w.admin_engine) as session:
        sealed: bytes = (
            await session.execute(select(AuthTotp.secret_sealed).where(AuthTotp.user_id == user_id))
        ).scalar_one()
        return sealed


def test_a_new_secret_is_160_random_bits() -> None:
    first, second = totp.new_secret(), totp.new_secret()

    assert len(first) == 20 and len(second) == 20
    assert first != second


def test_the_uri_is_the_key_uri_format_an_authenticator_reads() -> None:
    """No `digits`, `period` or `algorithm` parameter: the Key Uri Format's
    defaults are 6, 30 and SHA-1, which is exactly what this module verifies."""
    uri = totp.otpauth_uri(FIXED, account="alice@toeshee.com", issuer="ITMS")

    parts = urlsplit(uri)
    assert (parts.scheme, parts.netloc) == ("otpauth", "totp")
    assert parts.path == "/ITMS:alice%40toeshee.com"
    assert parse_qs(parts.query) == {
        "secret": [base64.b32encode(FIXED).decode("ascii")],
        "issuer": ["ITMS"],
    }
    parsed = pyotp.parse_uri(uri)
    assert isinstance(parsed, pyotp.TOTP)
    assert (parsed.digits, parsed.interval) == (6, 30)


async def test_the_rfc_6238_vectors_are_accepted(world: _World) -> None:
    """RFC 6238 Appendix B, SHA-1, secret "12345678901234567890": T=59 is
    94287082, T=1111111109 is 07081804, T=1234567890 is 89005924 at eight
    digits; six digits are the last six. Pins the step, the digits and the
    hash without trusting `pyotp` to agree with itself."""
    await _stage(world, b"12345678901234567890")

    assert await _confirm(world, "287082", at=datetime.fromtimestamp(59, UTC))
    assert await _verify(world, "081804", at=datetime.fromtimestamp(1111111109, UTC))
    assert await _verify(world, "005924", at=datetime.fromtimestamp(1234567890, UTC))


async def test_a_code_is_accepted_once(world: _World) -> None:
    """Falsifier §10.3, second half. NIST §3.1.4: "Verifiers SHALL accept a
    given OTP only once while it is valid". The `step > after` test and the
    conditional UPDATE: remove either and the second call answers True."""
    secret = await _enrolled(world)
    code = _code(secret, STEP)

    assert await _verify(world, code)
    assert not await _verify(world, code)
    # Still inside the window at the next step, and still refused.
    assert not await _verify(world, code, at=NOW + timedelta(seconds=20))
    assert await _verify(world, _code(secret, STEP + 1), at=NOW + timedelta(seconds=30))


async def test_an_older_code_is_refused_once_a_newer_one_was_accepted(world: _World) -> None:
    secret = await _enrolled(world)

    assert await _verify(world, _code(secret, STEP + 1))
    assert not await _verify(world, _code(secret, STEP))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("offset", "accepted"), [(-2, False), (-1, True), (0, True), (1, True), (2, False)]
)
async def test_one_step_of_tolerance_either_way(world: _World, offset: int, accepted: bool) -> None:
    await _enrolled(world, FIXED)

    assert await _verify(world, _code(FIXED, STEP + offset)) is accepted


@pytest.mark.parametrize("code", ["", "12345", "1234567", "12a456", "１２３４５６", "123456\n"])
async def test_a_malformed_code_is_refused_and_changes_nothing(world: _World, code: str) -> None:
    await _enrolled(world, FIXED)
    before = await _last_step(world)

    assert not await _verify(world, code)
    assert await _last_step(world) == before


async def test_spaces_inside_a_code_are_ignored(world: _World) -> None:
    secret = await _enrolled(world)
    code = _code(secret, STEP)

    assert await _verify(world, f" {code[:3]} {code[3:]} ")


async def test_a_staged_secret_is_not_a_factor_until_confirmed(world: _World) -> None:
    """Decisión del plan 2: `last_step IS NULL` is an enrolment in progress."""
    secret = totp.new_secret()
    await _stage(world, secret)

    assert not await _has(world)
    assert not await _verify(world, _code(secret, STEP))
    assert await _confirm(world, _code(secret, STEP))
    assert await _has(world)
    # And once it is a factor, `confirm_secret` no longer accepts against it.
    assert not await _confirm(world, _code(secret, STEP + 1), at=NOW + timedelta(seconds=30))


async def test_staging_never_replaces_a_confirmed_secret(world: _World) -> None:
    secret = await _enrolled(world)

    with pytest.raises(totp.TotpAlreadyEnrolled):
        await _stage(world, totp.new_secret())

    assert await _verify(world, _code(secret, STEP))


async def test_staging_again_replaces_a_pending_secret(world: _World) -> None:
    first, second = totp.new_secret(), totp.new_secret()
    await _stage(world, first)
    await _stage(world, second)

    assert not await _confirm(world, _code(first, STEP))
    assert await _confirm(world, _code(second, STEP))


async def test_the_secret_is_sealed_not_stored(world: _World) -> None:
    secret = await _enrolled(world)

    sealed = await _sealed(world, world.user_id)

    assert secret not in sealed
    assert base64.b32encode(secret) not in sealed
    assert set(json.loads(base64.b64decode(sealed))) == {"wrapped_dek", "key_version", "ct_b64"}


async def test_a_sealed_secret_moved_to_another_person_does_not_open(world: _World) -> None:
    """The seal is bound to the user id (`key_id=user_id`, AAD `org|user`):
    copying one person's secret onto another's row is an integrity failure,
    not a working factor."""
    secret = await _enrolled(world)
    _org, colleague = await _person(world.admin_engine, world.org_id)
    await _enrolled(world, user_id=colleague)
    sealed = await _sealed(world, world.user_id)
    async with AsyncSession(world.admin_engine) as session:
        await session.execute(
            update(AuthTotp).where(AuthTotp.user_id == colleague).values(secret_sealed=sealed)
        )
        await session.commit()
    code = _code(secret, STEP)

    assert not await _verify(world, code, user_id=colleague)
    assert await _verify(world, code)


async def test_two_requests_with_one_code_cannot_both_win(world: _World) -> None:
    """The conditional UPDATE (`last_step < step`): with a read-then-write the
    two would both see the old step and both answer True."""
    secret = await _enrolled(world)
    code = _code(secret, STEP)

    results = await asyncio.gather(_verify(world, code), _verify(world, code))

    assert sorted(results) == [False, True]


async def test_removing_the_factor(world: _World) -> None:
    await _enrolled(world)

    async with org_session(
        world.org_id, engine=world.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()
    ) as session:
        assert await totp.remove_totp(session, world.user_id)
    async with org_session(
        world.org_id, engine=world.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()
    ) as session:
        assert not await totp.remove_totp(session, world.user_id)
    assert not await _has(world)


def test_a_naive_time_is_refused() -> None:
    """A naive datetime is read as local time by `timestamp()`: a server in
    another zone would accept codes hours away."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        totp.step_of(datetime(2026, 11, 4, 12, 0, 0))
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Escribir `totp.py`**

Crear `backend/app/core/auth/totp.py`:

```python
"""TOTP (RFC 6238): the app factor, and the one rule pyotp does not keep for us.

Design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-autenticacion-propia-design.md` §2.2:
30-second step, 6 digits, one step of tolerance either way, a 160-bit secret
[S12, S13]; a code accepted once is never accepted again; the secret is sealed
by the vault.

WHAT PYOTP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. `pyotp` 2.10.0 computes the code
(`OTP.generate_otp`, the RFC 4226 truncation) and builds the `otpauth://` URI
(`TOTP.provisioning_uri`). It keeps no state, so it cannot refuse a code it
has already accepted: its README tells the application to store "the most
recently authenticated timestamp" and reject what is not newer, and the helper
for that (`verify_and_get_timecode`) is on its development branch, not in the
release [S43]. NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.4: "Verifiers SHALL accept a given OTP
only once while it is valid". So this module does not call `TOTP.verify`: it
computes the three candidate steps itself, compares each in constant time,
and accepts a match only for a step strictly greater than
`auth_totp.last_step` -- written with a conditional UPDATE, so two requests
racing with one code cannot both win.

PENDING AND CONFIRMED. A row whose `last_step` is NULL has never accepted a
code: it is an enrolment in progress, not a factor. `verify_totp` and
`has_totp` ignore it; `confirm_secret` is the only thing that accepts against
it, and accepting writes `last_step`, which is what turns it into a factor.
`stage_secret` never replaces a confirmed row: removing a factor is its own
act (`remove_totp`), with its own recent confirmation upstream (§2.5).

THE SECRET. 20 random bytes, sealed with `VaultService.seal_bytes` bound to
the person's id (AAD `org|user_id`, `app/core/vault.py:190-212`), so a sealed
secret copied onto another person's row does not open. It is opened for one
comparison and dropped; never logged, never returned (the URI is shown once,
at enrolment, by the caller).

FAILURES ARE NOT COUNTED HERE: the caller wraps every call in
`app/core/auth/failures.py`; see that module.
"""

import base64
import hmac
import logging
import re
import secrets
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import UUID

import pyotp
from cryptography.exceptions import InvalidTag
from sqlalchemy import delete, select, update
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core.vault import VaultService
from app.models.auth import AuthTotp

__all__ = [
    "DIGITS",
    "SECRET_BYTES",
    "STEP_S",
    "WINDOW",
    "TotpAlreadyEnrolled",
    "confirm_secret",
    "has_totp",
    "new_secret",
    "otpauth_uri",
    "remove_totp",
    "stage_secret",
    "step_of",
    "verify_totp",
]

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

STEP_S = 30
DIGITS = 6
#: Steps of tolerance either side of the current one.
WINDOW = 1
#: 160 bits, RFC 4226's recommended key length.
SECRET_BYTES = 20

_CODE = re.compile(r"[0-9]{6}")


class TotpAlreadyEnrolled(Exception):
    """A confirmed TOTP exists; it is removed first, never overwritten."""


def new_secret() -> bytes:
    return secrets.token_bytes(SECRET_BYTES)


def _b32(secret: bytes) -> str:
    # 20 bytes are 32 base32 characters exactly: there is no padding to strip.
    return base64.b32encode(secret).decode("ascii")


def otpauth_uri(secret: bytes, *, account: str, issuer: str) -> str:
    """The Key Uri Format string an authenticator app scans. 6 digits, 30 s and
    SHA-1 are its defaults, so pyotp leaves them out."""
    return pyotp.TOTP(
        _b32(secret), digits=DIGITS, interval=STEP_S, name=account, issuer=issuer
    ).provisioning_uri()


def step_of(now: datetime) -> int:
    """The RFC 6238 time step `now` falls in. A naive datetime is refused: its
    `timestamp()` is local time."""
    if now.tzinfo is None:
        raise ValueError(  # i18n-exempt: programming error, never reaches a person
            "a TOTP check needs a timezone-aware time"
        )
    return int(now.timestamp()) // STEP_S


def _matching_step(secret: bytes, code: str, now: datetime, after: int | None) -> int | None:
    """The newest step within the window whose code is `code` and that is newer
    than `after`; None otherwise. Every candidate is compared, so the time taken
    does not say which step matched."""
    otp = pyotp.TOTP(_b32(secret), digits=DIGITS, interval=STEP_S)
    current = step_of(now)
    accepted: int | None = None
    for step in range(current - WINDOW, current + WINDOW + 1):
        if step < 0:
            continue
        matches = hmac.compare_digest(otp.generate_otp(step), code)
        if matches and (after is None or step > after):
            accepted = step
    return accepted


async def stage_secret(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    user_id: UUID,
    secret: bytes,
    vault: VaultService,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Keep `secret` as the person's PENDING TOTP until `confirm_secret` accepts
    a code from it. Replaces a pending one; raises `TotpAlreadyEnrolled` when a
    confirmed one exists (the upsert's `where`: no row comes back)."""
    sealed = (
        await vault.seal_bytes(session, org_id=org_id, key_id=user_id, plaintext=secret)
    ).encode("ascii")
    at = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    upsert = (
        pg_insert(AuthTotp)
        .values(user_id=user_id, org_id=org_id, secret_sealed=sealed, last_step=None, created_at=at)
        .on_conflict_do_update(
            index_elements=["user_id"],
            set_={"secret_sealed": sealed, "created_at": at},
            where=AuthTotp.last_step.is_(None),
        )
        .returning(AuthTotp.user_id)
    )
    if (await session.execute(upsert)).scalar_one_or_none() is None:
        raise TotpAlreadyEnrolled()


async def _open(session: AsyncSession, vault: VaultService, row: AuthTotp) -> bytes | None:
    try:
        return await vault.open_bytes(
            session, org_id=row.org_id, key_id=row.user_id, sealed=row.secret_sealed.decode("ascii")
        )
    except (InvalidTag, ValueError):
        # A seal that does not open for THIS person: moved from another row,
        # or damaged. Refused, never a 500, and never the seal in a log.
        logger.warning("totp secret did not open for its row; the code is refused")
        return None


async def _accept(
    session: AsyncSession,
    user_id: UUID,
    code: str,
    *,
    vault: VaultService,
    now: datetime,
    confirmed: bool,
) -> bool:
    typed = code.replace(" ", "")
    if not _CODE.fullmatch(typed):
        return False
    row = (
        await session.execute(select(AuthTotp).where(AuthTotp.user_id == user_id))
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if row is None or (row.last_step is not None) != confirmed:
        return False
    secret = await _open(session, vault, row)
    if secret is None:
        return False
    step = _matching_step(secret, typed, now, row.last_step)
    del secret
    if step is None:
        return False
    # THE GUARD IS THE REPLAY PROTECTION. Pending: still pending, and still the
    # secret the code was checked against. Confirmed: no newer step accepted
    # in between.
    guard = (
        AuthTotp.last_step < step
        if confirmed
        else (AuthTotp.last_step.is_(None)) & (AuthTotp.secret_sealed == row.secret_sealed)
    )
    won = (
        await session.execute(
            update(AuthTotp)
            .where(AuthTotp.user_id == user_id, guard)
            .values(last_step=step)
            .returning(AuthTotp.user_id)
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    return won is not None


async def confirm_secret(
    session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID, code: str, *, vault: VaultService, now: datetime
) -> bool:
    """Accept `code` against the PENDING secret; on success it is a factor."""
    return await _accept(session, user_id, code, vault=vault, now=now, confirmed=False)


async def verify_totp(
    session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID, code: str, *, vault: VaultService, now: datetime
) -> bool:
    """Accept `code` against the CONFIRMED secret: ±`WINDOW` steps, and only a
    step newer than the last one accepted."""
    return await _accept(session, user_id, code, vault=vault, now=now, confirmed=True)


async def has_totp(session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID) -> bool:
    found = await session.scalar(
        select(AuthTotp.user_id).where(AuthTotp.user_id == user_id, AuthTotp.last_step.is_not(None))
    )
    return found is not None


async def remove_totp(session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID) -> bool:
    """Drop the person's TOTP, pending or confirmed. True if there was one."""
    removed = (
        await session.execute(
            delete(AuthTotp).where(AuthTotp.user_id == user_id).returning(AuthTotp.user_id)
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    return removed is not None
```

```python
"""Recovery codes: `app/core/auth/recovery.py` (design §2.2).

Ten single-use look-up secrets, shown once, stored salted and hashed with a
password hashing scheme -- NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.2.2 for a secret shorter
than 112 bits.
"""

import asyncio
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession

from app.core.auth import failures, recovery
from app.core.client_scope import ClientScope
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.models import Organization, User
from app.models.auth import AuthFailure, AuthRecoveryCode

SHAPE = re.compile(r"[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{5}-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{5}")


@dataclass
class _World:
    org_id: UUID
    user_id: UUID
    app_engine: AsyncEngine
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine


async def _person(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, org_id: UUID | None = None) -> tuple[UUID, UUID]:
    async with AsyncSession(admin_engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        if org_id is None:
            slug = f"rec-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"
            org = Organization(name=slug, slug=slug)
            session.add(org)
            await session.flush()
            org_id = org.id
        user = User(
            org_id=org_id,
            external_subject=f"sub-{uuid4().hex[:10]}",
            email=f"{uuid4().hex[:8]}@toeshee.com",
        )
        session.add(user)
        await session.commit()
        return org_id, user.id


@pytest.fixture()
async def world(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine) -> _World:
    org_id, user_id = await _person(admin_engine)
    return _World(org_id, user_id, app_engine, admin_engine)


async def _replace(w: _World, user_id: UUID | None = None) -> list[str]:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await recovery.replace_codes(session, org_id=w.org_id, user_id=user_id or w.user_id)


async def _use(w: _World, code: str, user_id: UUID | None = None) -> bool:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await recovery.use_code(session, user_id or w.user_id, code)


async def _remaining(w: _World) -> int:
    async with org_session(w.org_id, engine=w.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
        return await recovery.remaining(session, w.user_id)


async def _stored(w: _World) -> list[bytes]:
    async with AsyncSession(w.admin_engine) as session:
        return list(
            (
                await session.execute(
                    select(AuthRecoveryCode.code_hash).where(AuthRecoveryCode.user_id == w.user_id)
                )
            ).scalars()
        )


def test_ten_codes_in_the_shown_format() -> None:
    codes = recovery.new_codes()

    assert len(codes) == 10 and len(set(codes)) == 10
    assert all(SHAPE.fullmatch(code) for code in codes)


async def test_codes_are_stored_salted_and_hashed_with_argon2id(world: _World) -> None:
    """NIST §3.1.2.2, Decisión del plan 3: argon2id at OWASP's minimum, one
    random salt per code, and the code itself nowhere."""
    codes = await _replace(world)

    stored = await _stored(world)
    assert len(stored) == 10
    assert all(h.startswith(b"$argon2id$v=19$m=19456,t=2,p=1$") for h in stored)
    assert len({h.split(b"$")[4] for h in stored}) == 10  # ten distinct salts
    for code in codes:
        assert all(code.replace("-", "").encode() not in h for h in stored)


async def test_each_code_works_once(world: _World) -> None:
    codes = await _replace(world)

    assert await _use(world, codes[3])
    assert not await _use(world, codes[3])
    assert await _remaining(world) == 9


async def test_typing_is_forgiving(world: _World) -> None:
    """Case, spaces and the hyphen do not matter; O reads as 0 and I or L as 1,
    as Crockford's alphabet says."""
    codes = await _replace(world)
    typed = codes[0].replace("-", " ").lower().replace("0", "o").replace("1", "l")

    assert await _use(world, f"  {typed} ")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("code", ["", "AAAAA-AAAAU", "AAAAA-AAAA", "AAAAA-AAAAAA", "ÄAAAA-AAAAA"])
async def test_a_malformed_code_is_refused_and_spends_nothing(world: _World, code: str) -> None:
    await _replace(world)

    assert not await _use(world, code)
    assert await _remaining(world) == 10


async def test_a_code_never_issued_is_refused(world: _World) -> None:
    codes = await _replace(world)
    stranger = next(c for c in recovery.new_codes() if c not in codes)

    assert not await _use(world, stranger)
    assert await _remaining(world) == 10


async def test_new_codes_replace_the_old_ones(world: _World) -> None:
    old = await _replace(world)
    new = await _replace(world)

    assert not await _use(world, old[0])
    assert await _use(world, new[0])
    assert len(await _stored(world)) == 10


async def test_another_persons_code_is_refused(world: _World) -> None:
    _org, colleague = await _person(world.admin_engine, world.org_id)
    theirs = await _replace(world, colleague)
    await _replace(world)

    assert not await _use(world, theirs[0])


async def test_replacing_the_codes_keeps_the_failure_count(world: _World) -> None:
    """Decisión del plan 7: new codes are not a way to reset the counter."""
    await _replace(world)
    async with org_session(
        world.org_id, engine=world.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()
    ) as session:
        for _ in range(3):
            await failures.record_failure(
                session, org_id=world.org_id, user_id=world.user_id, factor="recovery"
            )

    await _replace(world)

    async with AsyncSession(world.admin_engine) as session:
        assert (
            await session.scalar(
                select(AuthFailure.consecutive).where(
                    AuthFailure.user_id == world.user_id, AuthFailure.factor == "recovery"
                )
            )
        ) == 3


async def test_two_requests_with_one_code_cannot_both_win(world: _World) -> None:
    """The conditional UPDATE (`used_at IS NULL`): NIST §3.1.2.2, "SHALL be
    used successfully only once"."""
    codes = await _replace(world)

    results = await asyncio.gather(_use(world, codes[0]), _use(world, codes[0]))

    assert sorted(results) == [False, True]
```

- [ ] **Step 15: Escribir `recovery.py`**

Crear `backend/app/core/auth/recovery.py`:

```python
"""Recovery codes: ten look-up secrets, shown once, stored salted and hashed.

Design `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-autenticacion-propia-design.md` §2.2
("10 códigos de recuperación de un solo uso, mostrados una vez y guardados
como hash" [S7]).

THE HASH IS A PASSWORD HASH, AND NIST SAYS WHY. A code is ten symbols of
Crockford base32: 50 bits. NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.2.2: "Look-up secrets that
are shorter than the minimum security strength specified in the latest
revision of [SP800-131A] (i.e., 112 bits as of the date of this publication)
SHALL be stored in a salted and hashed form using a suitable password hashing
scheme ... The salt value SHALL be at least 32 bits in length". A bare SHA-256
of 50 bits is hours of GPU time from the database dump it was meant to
survive. So: argon2id with a 16-byte random salt per code (argon2-cffi's
`PasswordHasher`, whose encoded string carries salt and parameters together).

AT OWASP'S MINIMUM, NOT THE PASSWORD DEFAULT. A sign-in with a recovery code
checks the attempt against up to ten stored hashes; at argon2-cffi's default
(64 MiB, t=3, p=4, what `passwords.py` uses) that is ten password checks in one
request. OWASP's minimum, "m=19456 (19 MiB), t=2, p=1" [S4], is the documented
floor for a guessable human password; a random 50-bit code behind it is far
out of reach offline, and online attempts are bounded by `failures.py`. No
pepper: it would need a key version per row that `auth_recovery_codes` does
not carry, and the salted argon2id hash is what §3.1.2.2 asks for.

SINGLE USE (§3.1.2.2: "SHALL be used successfully only once"): a conditional
UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL, so two requests with one code cannot both
win.

THE FORMAT. `XXXXX-XXXXX` in Crockford's alphabet (no I, L, O, U): read aloud
and typed by hand. On the way in, case, spaces and the hyphen are ignored and
the confusable letters are read the way Crockford says (O as 0, I and L as 1).

Replacing the codes does not touch the recovery factor's failure count
(`failures.py`, Decisión del plan 7 of the plan that built this).
"""

import asyncio
import secrets
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import UUID

from argon2 import PasswordHasher
from argon2.exceptions import InvalidHashError, VerificationError
from sqlalchemy import delete, func, select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.models.auth import AuthRecoveryCode

__all__ = [
    "ALPHABET",
    "CODE_COUNT",
    "new_codes",
    "normalise",
    "remaining",
    "replace_codes",
    "use_code",
]

CODE_COUNT = 10
ALPHABET = "0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ"
_LENGTH = 10
_ALIASES = str.maketrans({"O": "0", "I": "1", "L": "1"})
_HASHER = PasswordHasher(time_cost=2, memory_cost=19456, parallelism=1, hash_len=32, salt_len=16)


def new_codes() -> list[str]:
    """`CODE_COUNT` distinct codes, `XXXXX-XXXXX`."""
    codes: list[str] = []
    while len(codes) < CODE_COUNT:
        raw = "".join(secrets.choice(ALPHABET) for _ in range(_LENGTH))
        code = f"{raw[:5]}-{raw[5:]}"
        if code not in codes:
            codes.append(code)
    return codes


def normalise(code: str) -> str | None:
    """The ten symbols a typed code means, or None if it cannot be one."""
    cleaned = code.upper().replace("-", "").replace(" ", "").translate(_ALIASES)
    if len(cleaned) != _LENGTH or any(ch not in ALPHABET for ch in cleaned):
        return None
    return cleaned


def _hash_all(normalised: list[str]) -> list[bytes]:
    return [_HASHER.hash(code).encode("ascii") for code in normalised]


def _find(rows: list[tuple[UUID, bytes]], wanted: str) -> UUID | None:
    for row_id, stored in rows:
        try:
            if _HASHER.verify(stored, wanted):
                return row_id
        except (VerificationError, InvalidHashError):
            continue
    return None


async def replace_codes(session: AsyncSession, *, org_id: UUID, user_id: UUID) -> list[str]:
    """Issue a fresh set and forget the old one, used codes included. The
    plaintext codes are returned ONCE, for the caller to show."""
    codes = new_codes()
    hashes = await asyncio.to_thread(_hash_all, [code.replace("-", "") for code in codes])
    await session.execute(delete(AuthRecoveryCode).where(AuthRecoveryCode.user_id == user_id))
    session.add_all(
        [AuthRecoveryCode(org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id, code_hash=h) for h in hashes]
    )
    await session.flush()
    return codes


async def use_code(
    session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID, code: str, *, now: datetime | None = None
) -> bool:
    """Spend `code` if it is one of the person's unused codes. True once."""
    wanted = normalise(code)
    if wanted is None:
        return False
    rows = (
        await session.execute(
            select(AuthRecoveryCode.id, AuthRecoveryCode.code_hash).where(
                AuthRecoveryCode.user_id == user_id, AuthRecoveryCode.used_at.is_(None)
            )
        )
    ).all()
    match = await asyncio.to_thread(_find, [(row.id, row.code_hash) for row in rows], wanted)
    if match is None:
        return False
    won = (
        await session.execute(
            update(AuthRecoveryCode)
            .where(AuthRecoveryCode.id == match, AuthRecoveryCode.used_at.is_(None))
            .values(used_at=now or datetime.now(UTC))
            .returning(AuthRecoveryCode.id)
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    return won is not None


async def remaining(session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID) -> int:
    """Unused codes left, for `GET /me/security`."""
    count = await session.scalar(
        select(func.count())
        .select_from(AuthRecoveryCode)
        .where(AuthRecoveryCode.user_id == user_id, AuthRecoveryCode.used_at.is_(None))
    )
    return int(count or 0)
```
