### Task 5: Claves de acceso (WebAuthn)

Diseño §2.2 («Llave de acceso … se ofrece primero. Verificación del usuario **requerida** (y comprobada en el
servidor); sin atestación; varias por cuenta; las sincronizadas valen. Desafíos aleatorios de al menos 16 bytes, de un
solo uso y con caducidad») y §10, falsificador 4. Oleada 2, en paralelo con las Tasks 3, 4, 6 y 10. Solo backend: esta
tarea no añade rutas (son de la Task 7), ni textos para personas, ni auditoría (la escriben quienes llaman).

Hoy la plataforma no tiene WebAuthn: lo hacía Keycloak. Esta tarea escribe las cuatro mitades de las dos ceremonias
(opciones y verificación de registro y de autenticación) sobre **py_webauthn 3.0.1**, que añade la Task 2, y sobre
las tablas `auth_passkeys` y `auth_webauthn_challenges` de la Task 1.

**La API de py_webauthn 3.0.1, leída en su código.** El wheel publicado
(`https://files.pythonhosted.org/…/webauthn-3.0.1-py3-none-any.whl`, `webauthn/__init__.py`: `__version__ = "3.0.1"`)
se descargó y se leyó; cada llamada de esta tarea se ejecutó contra él (Python 3.12.3, cryptography 50.0.2, cbor2 6.2.0):

- `webauthn/registration/generate_registration_options.py`: `generate_registration_options(*, rp_id, rp_name,
  user_name, user_id: bytes | None, user_display_name, challenge: bytes | None, timeout: int = 60000, attestation =
  AttestationConveyancePreference.NONE, authenticator_selection: AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria | None,
  exclude_credentials: list[PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor] | None, supported_pub_key_algs, hints)`. Algoritmos por
  defecto `[EDDSA (-8), ECDSA_SHA_256 (-7), RSASSA_PKCS1_v1_5_SHA_256 (-257)]`, los que W3C recomienda [S14].
- `webauthn/registration/verify_registration_response.py`: `verify_registration_response(*, credential: str | dict |
  RegistrationCredential, expected_challenge: bytes, expected_rp_id: str, expected_origin: str | list[str],
  require_user_presence: bool = True, require_user_verification: bool = False, …) -> VerifiedRegistration`
  (`credential_id`, `credential_public_key`, `sign_count`, `user_verified`, `credential_device_type`,
  `credential_backed_up`, `fmt`, `aaguid`). **`require_user_verification` es `False` por defecto** (D22).
- `webauthn/authentication/generate_authentication_options.py`: `generate_authentication_options(*, rp_id, challenge,
  timeout, allow_credentials, user_verification = UserVerificationRequirement.PREFERRED)`.
- `webauthn/authentication/verify_authentication_response.py`: `verify_authentication_response(*, credential,
  expected_challenge, expected_rp_id, expected_origin, credential_public_key: bytes, credential_current_sign_count:
  int, require_user_verification: bool = False) -> VerifiedAuthentication` (`credential_id`, `new_sign_count`,
  `credential_device_type`, `credential_backed_up`, `user_verified`). Rechaza un contador que no supera el guardado
  salvo que ambos sean 0, y comprueba los flags antes que la firma.
- `webauthn/helpers/`: `options_to_json(options) -> str` (claves camelCase del W3C, bytes en base64url sin relleno,
  `alg` como entero), `parse_client_data_json(bytes) -> CollectedClientData` (`.challenge: bytes`),
  `base64url_to_bytes(str) -> bytes`; `webauthn/helpers/exceptions.py`: toda excepción propia deriva de
  `WebAuthnException`; `webauthn/helpers/structs.py`: `CredentialDeviceType.MULTI_DEVICE` / `SINGLE_DEVICE`,
  `AuthenticatorTransport` (`usb`, `nfc`, `ble`, `smart-card`, `internal`, `cable`, `hybrid`). El paquete trae
  `webauthn/py.typed`: no hace falta ninguna excepción de mypy en `backend/pyproject.toml`.

**El emparejamiento con `@simplewebauthn/browser` 14.0.0** (D22: sin verificar) se fija aquí hasta donde se puede sin
navegador: `startRegistration({ optionsJSON })` y `startAuthentication({ optionsJSON })` reciben los diccionarios
`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` / `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` del W3C
(`packages/browser/src/types/index.ts:69-83`) y devuelven `RegistrationResponseJSON` /
`AuthenticationResponseJSON`, que `verify_*_response` acepta como `dict`. Las pruebas lo fijan con (1) una respuesta
de un navegador real — Firefox para Android, atestación `none` — tomada de las pruebas del propio SimpleWebAuthn
(`packages/server/src/registration/verifyRegistrationResponse.test.ts`, `attestationNone`, licencia MIT, Copyright (c)
2020 Matthew Miller; https://github.com/MasterKale/SimpleWebAuthn), que verifica con `require_user_verification=True`;
(2) respuestas grabadas del autenticador simulado, con los miembros que añade la librería del navegador
(`publicKey`, `publicKeyAlgorithm`, `authenticatorData`, `clientExtensionResults`, `authenticatorAttachment`), y
(3) la forma de las opciones. La prueba con Chromium y su autenticador virtual es la del falsificador 4 en la Task 13.

**Files:**
- Create: `backend/app/core/auth/passkeys.py`
- Create: `backend/tests/webauthn_authenticator.py` (autenticador simulado, ayudante de pruebas)
- Create: `backend/tests/test_auth_passkey_vectors.py` (vectores fijos, sin base de datos)
- Create: `backend/tests/test_auth_passkeys.py` (las cuatro funciones contra la base de datos real)
- Test: `backend/tests/test_auth_passkey_vectors.py`, `backend/tests/test_auth_passkeys.py`,
  `backend/tests/test_i18n_catalog.py`, `backend/tests/test_client_catalog.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes:
  - Task 1: `AuthPasskey` y `AuthWebauthnChallenge` (`backend/app/models/auth.py`) con las columnas de
    el Apéndice A; las dos tablas con RLS y en `CATALOG` como `O("users","user_id")`: una fila de un técnico no
    tiene cliente y solo una sesión de todos los clientes la escribe (migración 0231, `NULL_ALL`).
  - Task 2: la dependencia `webauthn==3.0.1` (y `cbor2`, que trae) en `backend/pyproject.toml`, y el paquete
    `backend/app/core/auth/` (`__init__.py`).
  - `app.models.User` (`backend/app/models/core.py:41-82`): `id` (UUIDv7, `uuid7_pk`), `org_id`, `email`,
    `display_name`.
  - En las pruebas: `org_session(org_id, engine=…, clients=ClientScope.all())` (`backend/app/core/tenancy.py:24-48`),
    y los fixtures `admin_engine` / `app_engine` (`backend/tests/conftest.py:170-182`), con la siembra
    de `tests/test_bcp_findings.py:32-41`.
- Produces (`backend/app/core/auth/passkeys.py`; nombres del Apéndice A y los **nuevos**, marcados):
  - `async def registration_options(session: AsyncSession, user: User, *, rp_id: str, rp_name: str) -> dict[str, Any]`
    — `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON`; **`authenticatorSelection.userVerification == "required"`**
    (requisito del coordinador), `attestation == "none"`, `residentKey == "preferred"`, las ya registradas en
    `excludeCredentials`.
  - `async def verify_registration(session, user, credential: dict[str, Any], *, name: str, expected_origin: str,
    rp_id: str) -> AuthPasskey`.
  - `async def authentication_options(session, user_id: UUID | None, *, org_id: UUID, rp_id: str, purpose:
    Literal["authenticate", "step_up"]) -> dict[str, Any]` — **`org_id` es nuevo** (Decisión del plan 2);
    `userVerification == "required"`.
  - `async def verify_authentication(session, credential: dict[str, Any], *, expected_origin: str, rp_id: str,
    purpose: Literal["authenticate", "step_up"]) -> AuthPasskey` — comprueba UV, contador, BE y desafío de un solo uso.
  - **Nuevos:** `class PasskeyRejected(Exception)` con `reason: Literal["challenge", "credential", "verification",
    "name"]`; `def user_handle(user_id: UUID) -> bytes`; `CHALLENGE_BYTES = 32`; `CHALLENGE_TTL =
    timedelta(minutes=5)`; `CEREMONY_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000`; `NAME_MAX = 100`.
  - `verify_registration_response` y `verify_authentication_response` se importan **a nivel de módulo** en
    `app.core.auth.passkeys` (requisito del coordinador: las pruebas los espían con `monkeypatch.setattr(passkeys,
    …)`).
  - Para la Task 7 (quien llama): `rp_id = app.core.auth.csrf.console_host(settings)`, `expected_origin =
    app.core.auth.csrf.console_origin(settings)` (Task 6); `None` en cualquiera de los dos → 503. Cada
    `PasskeyRejected` se responde con el mismo mensaje genérico y cuenta un fallo del factor `passkey`
    (`failures.record_failure`, Task 4); `reason` es solo para el log. La sesión que se pasa es de todos los clientes.

**Decisión del plan (1): el *user handle* es un SHA-256 del id de la persona, no el id.** W3C pide que el handle no
lleve datos personales y recomienda 64 bytes aleatorios guardados en la cuenta; la Task 1 no tiene columna para eso, y
`users.id` es un UUIDv7 cuyos primeros 48 bits son la fecha de alta. `user_handle(user_id) =
sha256(b"itms.webauthn.user-handle\x00" + user_id.bytes)`: estable (el autenticador sustituye la credencial de la
misma cuenta en vez de duplicarla), sin fecha y comprobable al autenticar (`userHandle` contra la persona del passkey).

**Decisión del plan (2): `authentication_options` recibe `org_id`.** La fila del desafío necesita organización, y sin
persona (credencial descubrible, contactos de la fase 2) no hay de dónde sacarla. Con persona, la Task 7 pasa la de su
sesión.

**Decisión del plan (3): el desafío se busca por el que trae la respuesta y se gasta antes de verificar.** La interfaz
no lleva un id de desafío; el `clientDataJSON` de la respuesta lo contiene. Un solo `UPDATE … SET used_at = now()
WHERE challenge = … AND purpose = … AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING …` lo gasta: de dos respuestas
que compiten, una sola obtiene fila, y una respuesta que luego falla ya lo gastó (no se reintenta con el mismo).

**Decisión del plan (4): un desafío vivo por persona y propósito.** Emitir otro retira el anterior y barre los gastados
o caducados de esa persona; los anónimos solo se barren gastados o caducados, para que dos personas que entran a la vez
no se retiren el desafío una a otra.

**Decisión del plan (5): si el flag BE cambia, se rechaza.** S14: «Backup eligibility is a credential property and is
permanent for a given public key credential source». Una credencial registrada de un solo dispositivo que ahora dice
ser sincronizable no es la que se registró.

**Decisión del plan (6): `verified.user_verified` se comprueba también en el código, además del argumento.** La
propiedad no descansa en un solo argumento; la prueba que espía la llamada (`test_both_verify_calls_ask…`) fija el
argumento por separado, para que quitar cualquiera de los dos ponga una prueba en rojo.

- [ ] **Step 1: El autenticador simulado**

Crear `backend/tests/webauthn_authenticator.py`. Responde a las opciones como el navegador entrega el resultado a
`@simplewebauthn/browser`: ES256, atestación `none`, y los flags a elección de la prueba (`uv=False` es un toque sin
verificación del usuario).

```python
"""A software WebAuthn authenticator for tests (P2 phase 1 Task 5).

It answers `navigator.credentials.create()` and `.get()` the way a browser
hands the result to `@simplewebauthn/browser` 14's `startRegistration` /
`startAuthentication`, which return the W3C `RegistrationResponseJSON` /
`AuthenticationResponseJSON` dictionaries
(https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-3/#dictdef-registrationresponsejson): bytes as
base64url without padding, plus the convenience members the browser library
adds (`publicKey`, `publicKeyAlgorithm`, `authenticatorData`,
`clientExtensionResults`). py_webauthn 3.0.1 reads the first and ignores the
second, which `test_auth_passkey_vectors.py` pins.

ES256 only (COSE -7): the algorithm every platform authenticator offers and the
one `cryptography` signs without extra dependencies. The FLAGS are the point:
`uv=False` is an authenticator that only checked presence -- the touch that
OWASP says "alone is not a second factor" -- and a test can also clear `up`,
set `be`/`bs`, or replay a counter.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import base64
import hashlib
import json
import secrets
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes, serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec
from webauthn.helpers import encode_cbor

FLAG_UP = 0x01
FLAG_UV = 0x04
FLAG_BE = 0x08
FLAG_BS = 0x10
FLAG_AT = 0x40

#: The AAGUID of an authenticator that does not name its model ("none"
#: attestation zeroes it in practice); 16 bytes.
ZERO_AAGUID = bytes(16)


def b64url(data: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")


def unb64url(text: str) -> bytes:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(text + "===")


def _flags(*, up: bool, uv: bool, be: bool, bs: bool, at: bool) -> int:
    return (
        (FLAG_UP if up else 0)
        | (FLAG_UV if uv else 0)
        | (FLAG_BE if be else 0)
        | (FLAG_BS if bs else 0)
        | (FLAG_AT if at else 0)
    )


@dataclass
class SoftPasskey:
    """One credential: its id, its P-256 key, its counter and its user handle."""

    rp_id: str
    user_handle: bytes
    credential_id: bytes = field(default_factory=lambda: secrets.token_bytes(32))
    private_key: ec.EllipticCurvePrivateKey = field(
        default_factory=lambda: ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())
    )
    sign_count: int = 0
    backup_eligible: bool = True
    backed_up: bool = True

    def cose_public_key(self) -> bytes:
        numbers = self.private_key.public_key().public_numbers()
        return encode_cbor(
            {
                1: 2,  # kty: EC2
                3: -7,  # alg: ES256
                -1: 1,  # crv: P-256
                -2: numbers.x.to_bytes(32, "big"),
                -3: numbers.y.to_bytes(32, "big"),
            }
        )

    def _auth_data(self, *, up: bool, uv: bool, attested: bool) -> bytes:
        rp_id_hash = hashlib.sha256(self.rp_id.encode("utf-8")).digest()
        flags = _flags(
            up=up, uv=uv, be=self.backup_eligible, bs=self.backed_up, at=attested
        )
        data = rp_id_hash + bytes([flags]) + struct.pack(">I", self.sign_count)
        if attested:
            data += (
                ZERO_AAGUID
                + struct.pack(">H", len(self.credential_id))
                + self.credential_id
                + self.cose_public_key()
            )
        return data

    def create(
        self,
        options: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        origin: str,
        uv: bool = True,
        up: bool = True,
        challenge: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The `RegistrationResponseJSON` for `options` (a creation-options
        JSON dict, as the server sent it). `challenge` overrides the one in
        `options`, to answer a challenge the server never issued."""
        client_data = json.dumps(
            {
                "type": "webauthn.create",
                "challenge": challenge or options["challenge"],
                "origin": origin,
                "crossOrigin": False,
            },
            separators=(",", ":"),
        ).encode("utf-8")
        auth_data = self._auth_data(up=up, uv=uv, attested=True)
        attestation = encode_cbor({"fmt": "none", "attStmt": {}, "authData": auth_data})
        public_der = self.private_key.public_key().public_bytes(
            serialization.Encoding.DER, serialization.PublicFormat.SubjectPublicKeyInfo
        )
        return {
            "id": b64url(self.credential_id),
            "rawId": b64url(self.credential_id),
            "type": "public-key",
            "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
            "clientExtensionResults": {},
            "response": {
                "clientDataJSON": b64url(client_data),
                "attestationObject": b64url(attestation),
                "transports": ["hybrid", "internal"],
                "publicKeyAlgorithm": -7,
                "publicKey": b64url(public_der),
                "authenticatorData": b64url(auth_data),
            },
        }

    def get(
        self,
        options: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        origin: str,
        uv: bool = True,
        up: bool = True,
        advance: int = 1,
        challenge: str | None = None,
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """The `AuthenticationResponseJSON` for request options `options`.
        `advance` is how far the counter moves (0 replays the last value)."""
        self.sign_count += advance
        client_data = json.dumps(
            {
                "type": "webauthn.get",
                "challenge": challenge or options["challenge"],
                "origin": origin,
                "crossOrigin": False,
            },
            separators=(",", ":"),
        ).encode("utf-8")
        auth_data = self._auth_data(up=up, uv=uv, attested=False)
        signature = self.private_key.sign(
            auth_data + hashlib.sha256(client_data).digest(), ec.ECDSA(hashes.SHA256())
        )
        return {
            "id": b64url(self.credential_id),
            "rawId": b64url(self.credential_id),
            "type": "public-key",
            "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
            "clientExtensionResults": {},
            "response": {
                "clientDataJSON": b64url(client_data),
                "authenticatorData": b64url(auth_data),
                "signature": b64url(signature),
                "userHandle": b64url(self.user_handle),
            },
        }
```

```python
    "MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAEvXxzuIsum0ztpiAistqL4TGTpbVu3Cbn33hC4kzQtesGBa2nva"
    "g6xqK4DX4xQED6R_8WuDushc7bAURRu3znGg"
)


def _registration(flags_and_tail: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The recorded `RegistrationResponseJSON`; only the flags byte differs
    between the two recordings (0x5D = UP|UV|BE|BS|AT, 0x59 = the same without
    UV), and it sits inside both `attestationObject` and `authenticatorData`."""
    auth_data = "RVFWvDTxPt9J0_YPMVi_ZBcnbUEsML5rJxPcpXHQqC" + flags_and_tail
    return {
        "id": "oaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoQ",
        "rawId": "oaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoQ",
        "type": "public-key",
        "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
        "clientExtensionResults": {},
        "response": {
            "clientDataJSON": _CLIENT_DATA_CREATE,
            "attestationObject": "o2NmbXRkbm9uZWdhdHRTdG10oGhhdXRoRGF0YViU" + auth_data,
            "transports": ["hybrid", "internal"],
            "publicKeyAlgorithm": -7,
            "publicKey": _PUBLIC_KEY_DER,
            "authenticatorData": auth_data,
        },
    }


REGISTRATION_WITH_UV = _registration("pd" + _ATTESTED_TAIL)
REGISTRATION_WITHOUT_UV = _registration("pZ" + _ATTESTED_TAIL)

ASSERTION_WITH_UV: dict[str, Any] = {
    "id": "oaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoQ",
    "rawId": "oaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoaGhoQ",
    "type": "public-key",
    "authenticatorAttachment": "platform",
    "clientExtensionResults": {},
    "response": {
        "clientDataJSON": (
            "eyJ0eXBlIjoid2ViYXV0aG4uZ2V0IiwiY2hhbGxlbmdlIjoiSUNFaUl5UWxKaWNvS1NvckxDMHVMekF4"
            "TWpNME5UWTNPRGs2T3p3OVBqOCIsIm9yaWdpbiI6Imh0dHBzOi8vaXRtcy5leGFtcGxlLmNvbSIsImNy"
            "b3NzT3JpZ2luIjpmYWxzZX0"
        ),
        "authenticatorData": "RVFWvDTxPt9J0_YPMVi_ZBcnbUEsML5rJxPcpXHQqCodAAAAAQ",
        "signature": (
            "MEQCIGdzOLrBwpeSoonVqUaSa6xRTcBjZh9MRn_Z7WNU_66jAiANaXumLLLgbEvYoSwHg-cdX5B40XLU"
            "RiA1ACVIEp1thQ"
        ),
        "userHandle": "xfp41Bp8Kky6sfYZdTO8TVev15Tft9Qi8CEN_FXfYJY",
    },
}


def _verify_registration(credential: dict[str, Any], **overrides: Any) -> Any:
    arguments: dict[str, Any] = {
        "credential": credential,
        "expected_challenge": REGISTRATION_CHALLENGE,
        "expected_rp_id": RP_ID,
        "expected_origin": ORIGIN,
        "require_user_verification": True,
    }
    arguments.update(overrides)
    return verify_registration_response(**arguments)


def _verify_assertion(**overrides: Any) -> Any:
    arguments: dict[str, Any] = {
        "credential": ASSERTION_WITH_UV,
        "expected_challenge": ASSERTION_CHALLENGE,
        "expected_rp_id": RP_ID,
        "expected_origin": ORIGIN,
        "credential_public_key": COSE_PUBLIC_KEY,
        "credential_current_sign_count": 0,
        "require_user_verification": True,
    }
    arguments.update(overrides)
    return verify_authentication_response(**arguments)


def test_a_real_browsers_registration_verifies_with_user_verification_required() -> None:
    verified = verify_registration_response(
        credential=FIREFOX_ANDROID_NONE,
        expected_challenge=FIREFOX_CHALLENGE,
        expected_rp_id=FIREFOX_RP_ID,
        expected_origin=FIREFOX_ORIGIN,
        require_user_verification=True,
    )
    assert verified.fmt == "none"
    assert verified.user_verified is True
    assert verified.sign_count == 0
    assert bytes_to_base64url(verified.credential_public_key) == FIREFOX_PUBLIC_KEY
    assert bytes_to_base64url(verified.credential_id) == FIREFOX_ANDROID_NONE["id"]
    # A security key or a platform credential that is not synced.
    assert verified.credential_device_type == CredentialDeviceType.SINGLE_DEVICE
    assert verified.credential_backed_up is False


def test_the_recorded_registration_verifies_and_yields_the_recorded_key() -> None:
    verified = _verify_registration(REGISTRATION_WITH_UV)
    assert verified.credential_id == CREDENTIAL_ID
    assert verified.credential_public_key == COSE_PUBLIC_KEY
    assert verified.user_verified is True
    assert verified.sign_count == 0
    assert verified.credential_device_type == CredentialDeviceType.MULTI_DEVICE
    assert verified.credential_backed_up is True


def test_the_library_default_accepts_an_unverified_user_which_is_why_it_is_never_used() -> None:
    """D22. The same response with UV cleared PASSES the library's default
    (`require_user_verification=False`) and fails the argument passkeys.py
    always passes. If this test's first half ever fails, the default changed
    upstream -- the second half is the one that protects the platform."""
    lenient = verify_registration_response(
        credential=REGISTRATION_WITHOUT_UV,
        expected_challenge=REGISTRATION_CHALLENGE,
        expected_rp_id=RP_ID,
        expected_origin=ORIGIN,
    )
    assert lenient.user_verified is False
    with pytest.raises(InvalidRegistrationResponse, match="User verification is required"):
        _verify_registration(REGISTRATION_WITHOUT_UV)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "overrides",
    [
        {"expected_rp_id": "itms.example.org"},
        {"expected_origin": "https://itms.example.org"},
        {"expected_challenge": bytes(32)},
    ],
    ids=["rp", "origin", "challenge"],
)
def test_the_recorded_registration_is_refused_for_anything_else(overrides: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(InvalidRegistrationResponse):
        _verify_registration(REGISTRATION_WITH_UV, **overrides)


def test_the_recorded_assertion_verifies_and_advances_the_counter_to_one() -> None:
    verified = _verify_assertion()
    assert verified.credential_id == CREDENTIAL_ID
    assert verified.new_sign_count == 1
    assert verified.user_verified is True
    assert verified.credential_device_type == CredentialDeviceType.MULTI_DEVICE


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "overrides",
    [
        {"expected_rp_id": "itms.example.org"},
        {"expected_origin": "https://itms.example.org"},
        {"expected_challenge": bytes(32)},
        # The counter already stands at 1: the same assertion again is a replay.
        {"credential_current_sign_count": 1},
    ],
    ids=["rp", "origin", "challenge", "replayed-counter"],
)
def test_the_recorded_assertion_is_refused_for_anything_else(overrides: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(InvalidAuthenticationResponse):
        _verify_assertion(**overrides)
```

Crear `backend/tests/test_auth_passkeys.py`:

```python
"""Passkeys as a second factor: `app/core/auth/passkeys.py` (P2 design §2.2).

A software authenticator (`tests/webauthn_authenticator.py`) answers the
options the platform issues, through the same py_webauthn 3.0.1 calls the
routes will make, against the real database (`auth_passkeys`,
`auth_webauthn_challenges`, Task 1). The fixed vectors that need no database
are in `tests/test_auth_passkey_vectors.py`.

Every refusal is asserted by REASON, and each names the line it protects: a
test that only asserted "refused" would pass for the wrong reason.

Falsifier 4 of design §10 ("Una llave de acceso sin verificación del usuario se
rechaza") is `test_a_registration_without_user_verification_is_refused` and
`test_an_assertion_without_user_verification_is_refused`; the browser half is
Task 13's.
"""

from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import func, select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession

from app.core.auth.passkeys import (
    CHALLENGE_BYTES,
    PasskeyRejected,
    authentication_options,
    registration_options,
    user_handle,
    verify_authentication,
    verify_registration,
)
from app.core.client_scope import ClientScope
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.models import Organization, User
from app.models.auth import AuthPasskey, AuthWebauthnChallenge
from tests.webauthn_authenticator import SoftPasskey, b64url, unb64url

RP_ID = "itms.example.com"
ORIGIN = "https://itms.example.com"
RP_NAME = "ITMS"


async def _person(admin_engine: AsyncEngine, org_id: UUID | None = None) -> User:
    """A staff user (and, without `org_id`, a new organisation for them)."""
    async with AsyncSession(admin_engine, expire_on_commit=False) as s:
        if org_id is None:
            slug = f"pk-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"
            org = Organization(name=slug, slug=slug)
            s.add(org)
            await s.flush()
            org_id = org.id
        tag = uuid4().hex[:8]
        user = User(
            org_id=org_id,
            external_subject=f"sub-{tag}",
            email=f"{tag}@example.com",
            display_name=f"Person {tag}",
        )
        s.add(user)
        await s.commit()
        return user


def _session(app_engine: AsyncEngine, org_id: UUID) -> Any:
    """What the sign-in routes run these under: every client, because a staff
    person's rows have no client (module docstring of passkeys.py)."""
    return org_session(org_id, engine=app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all())


async def _registered(
    app_engine: AsyncEngine, user: User, *, backup_eligible: bool = True
) -> tuple[SoftPasskey, AuthPasskey]:
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(
        rp_id=RP_ID,
        user_handle=user_handle(user.id),
        backup_eligible=backup_eligible,
        backed_up=backup_eligible,
    )
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        passkey = await verify_registration(
            s,
            user,
            authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN),
            name="Work laptop",
            expected_origin=ORIGIN,
            rp_id=RP_ID,
        )
    return authenticator, passkey


async def _reason(call: Any) -> str:
    with pytest.raises(PasskeyRejected) as refused:
        await call
    return refused.value.reason


# --- registration ---------------------------------------------------------


async def test_registration_options_require_user_verification_and_no_attestation(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """The options a browser receives, in the W3C JSON shape `startRegistration`
    takes: every key is one `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` defines,
    bytes are unpadded base64url, and the three choices of design §2.2 are
    there -- user verification required, no attestation, EdDSA/ES256/RS256."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)

    w3c_keys = {
        "rp", "user", "challenge", "pubKeyCredParams", "timeout", "excludeCredentials",
        "authenticatorSelection", "hints", "attestation", "attestationFormats", "extensions",
    }
    assert set(options) <= w3c_keys
    assert options["rp"] == {"name": RP_NAME, "id": RP_ID}
    assert options["user"] == {
        "id": b64url(user_handle(user.id)),
        "name": user.email,
        "displayName": user.display_name,
    }
    assert len(unb64url(options["challenge"])) == CHALLENGE_BYTES
    assert "=" not in options["challenge"]
    assert [p["alg"] for p in options["pubKeyCredParams"]] == [-8, -7, -257]
    assert options["authenticatorSelection"]["userVerification"] == "required"
    assert options["authenticatorSelection"]["residentKey"] == "preferred"
    assert options["attestation"] == "none"
    assert options["excludeCredentials"] == []


async def test_a_passkey_registers_with_its_key_flags_and_transports(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, passkey = await _registered(app_engine, user)

    assert passkey.user_id == user.id and passkey.org_id == user.org_id
    assert passkey.credential_id == authenticator.credential_id
    assert passkey.public_key == authenticator.cose_public_key()
    assert passkey.sign_count == 0
    assert passkey.backup_eligible is True and passkey.backup_state is True
    assert passkey.transports == ["hybrid", "internal"]
    assert passkey.name == "Work laptop"


async def test_the_next_options_exclude_the_registered_passkey(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Several passkeys per person, never the same authenticator twice [S14]."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
    assert options["excludeCredentials"] == [
        {
            "id": b64url(authenticator.credential_id),
            "type": "public-key",
            "transports": ["hybrid", "internal"],
        }
    ]


async def test_a_registration_without_user_verification_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """FALSIFIER 4 (design §10). Protects `require_user_verification=True` in
    `verify_registration`: with it removed, py_webauthn's default accepts this
    response (`test_auth_passkey_vectors.py` shows it) and a touch alone would
    be a second factor. Nothing is stored."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN, uv=False),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
        stored = (await s.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(AuthPasskey))).scalar_one()
    assert reason == "verification"
    assert stored == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("origin", "rp_id"),
    [("https://itms.example.org", RP_ID), (ORIGIN, "itms.example.org")],
    ids=["another-origin", "another-rp"],
)
async def test_a_registration_for_another_origin_or_rp_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine, origin: str, rp_id: str
) -> None:
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=rp_id, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=origin),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
    assert reason == "verification"


async def test_a_registration_challenge_is_spent_by_its_first_answer(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects `_spend`'s `used_at IS NULL` and its single UPDATE: the same
    response a second time finds no live challenge -- even though the first
    one failed (no UV), because the challenge is spent before verification."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        unverified = authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN, uv=False)
        first = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s, user, unverified, name="Key", expected_origin=ORIGIN, rp_id=RP_ID
            )
        )
        second = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
    assert (first, second) == ("verification", "challenge")


async def test_an_expired_or_never_issued_challenge_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects `expires_at > now` and the lookup by the response's own
    challenge: an answer to a challenge past its life, or to one the server
    never issued, is refused before any cryptography runs."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
    async with AsyncSession(admin_engine) as admin:
        await admin.execute(
            update(AuthWebauthnChallenge)
            .where(AuthWebauthnChallenge.user_id == user.id)
            .values(expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(seconds=1))
        )
        await admin.commit()
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        expired = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
        forged = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN, challenge=b64url(bytes(32))),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
    assert (expired, forged) == ("challenge", "challenge")


async def test_a_new_options_call_retires_the_previous_challenge(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """One live challenge per person and purpose (`_issue`)."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        first = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(first, origin=ORIGIN),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
        live = (
            await s.execute(
                select(func.count())
                .select_from(AuthWebauthnChallenge)
                .where(AuthWebauthnChallenge.user_id == user.id)
            )
        ).scalar_one()
    assert reason == "challenge"
    assert live == 1


async def test_another_persons_registration_challenge_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects `owner != user.id`: a challenge issued to A does not register
    a passkey on B's account, though B's session sent it."""
    alice = await _person(admin_engine)
    bob = await _person(admin_engine, alice.org_id)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(bob.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, alice.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, alice, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                bob,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                name="Key",
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
    assert reason == "challenge"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["", "   ", "x" * 101])
async def test_a_passkey_needs_a_name_of_at_most_100_characters(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine, name: str
) -> None:
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await registration_options(s, user, rp_id=RP_ID, rp_name=RP_NAME)
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_registration(
                s,
                user,
                authenticator.create(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                name=name,
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
            )
        )
    assert reason == "name"


# --- authentication -------------------------------------------------------


async def test_an_assertion_verifies_and_moves_the_counter(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        assert options["userVerification"] == "required"
        assert options["rpId"] == RP_ID
        assert [c["id"] for c in options["allowCredentials"]] == [
            b64url(authenticator.credential_id)
        ]
        passkey = await verify_authentication(
            s,
            authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
            expected_origin=ORIGIN,
            rp_id=RP_ID,
            purpose="authenticate",
        )
    assert passkey.user_id == user.id
    assert passkey.sign_count == 1
    assert passkey.last_used_at is not None


async def test_an_assertion_without_user_verification_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """FALSIFIER 4 (design §10). Protects `require_user_verification=True` in
    `verify_authentication`; the counter does not move."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN, uv=False),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )
        )
        count = (
            await s.execute(select(AuthPasskey.sign_count).where(AuthPasskey.user_id == user.id))
        ).scalar_one()
    assert reason == "verification"
    assert count == 0


async def test_a_counter_that_did_not_move_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """A cloned authenticator replays a counter it already used."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        first = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        await verify_authentication(
            s,
            authenticator.get(first, origin=ORIGIN),
            expected_origin=ORIGIN,
            rp_id=RP_ID,
            purpose="authenticate",
        )
        second = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                authenticator.get(second, origin=ORIGIN, advance=0),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "verification"


async def test_a_sign_in_challenge_does_not_confirm_a_step_up(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects `purpose == purpose` in `_spend` (design §2.5): an assertion
    made for signing in is not a recent confirmation of anything else."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="step_up",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "challenge"


async def test_another_persons_passkey_does_not_answer_their_challenge(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects `AuthPasskey.user_id == owner`: Bob's genuine passkey signing
    Alice's challenge is not Alice confirming anything."""
    alice = await _person(admin_engine)
    bob = await _person(admin_engine, alice.org_id)
    await _registered(app_engine, alice)
    bobs, _ = await _registered(app_engine, bob)
    async with _session(app_engine, alice.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, alice.id, org_id=alice.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="step_up"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                bobs.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="step_up",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "credential"


async def test_a_user_handle_of_someone_else_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects the `handle != user_handle(passkey.user_id)` comparison."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    authenticator.user_handle = user_handle(uuid4())
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "credential"


async def test_backup_eligibility_cannot_change_after_registration(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Protects the BE comparison: "Backup eligibility is a credential property
    and is permanent" [S14]. A credential registered single-device that now
    claims to be syncable is not the credential that was registered."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user, backup_eligible=False)
    authenticator.backup_eligible = True
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "verification"


async def test_a_discoverable_sign_in_finds_the_person_from_the_passkey(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """No person yet (phase 2's contacts): an empty allow list, an anonymous
    challenge, and the passkey that answers says who it is."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, None, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        assert options["allowCredentials"] == []
        passkey = await verify_authentication(
            s,
            authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
            expected_origin=ORIGIN,
            rp_id=RP_ID,
            purpose="authenticate",
        )
    assert passkey.user_id == user.id


async def test_an_unknown_credential_is_refused(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    await _registered(app_engine, user)
    stranger = SoftPasskey(rp_id=RP_ID, user_handle=user_handle(user.id))
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, None, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                stranger.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "credential"


async def test_another_organisations_passkey_does_not_exist_here(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Invariant 5: the passkey lookup runs under the session's organisation,
    and RLS hides the other one's row -- the same refusal as a stranger's."""
    elsewhere = await _person(admin_engine)
    theirs, _ = await _registered(app_engine, elsewhere)
    here = await _person(admin_engine)
    async with _session(app_engine, here.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, None, org_id=here.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        reason = await _reason(
            verify_authentication(
                s,
                theirs.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
                expected_origin=ORIGIN,
                rp_id=RP_ID,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )
        )
    assert reason == "credential"


async def test_a_malformed_response_is_a_refusal_not_an_error(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine
) -> None:
    """Hostile input is a `PasskeyRejected`, never a 500."""
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        for garbage in ({}, {"response": {"clientDataJSON": "%%%"}}, {"response": "x"}):
            reason = await _reason(
                verify_authentication(
                    s, garbage, expected_origin=ORIGIN, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
                )
            )
            assert reason == "challenge", garbage


async def test_both_verify_calls_ask_the_library_to_require_user_verification(
    admin_engine: AsyncEngine, app_engine: AsyncEngine, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """D22, pinned at the call: py_webauthn's own check runs on both halves.
    `verify_registration` and `verify_authentication` ALSO refuse an
    unverified result themselves, so the two falsifier-4 tests above stay red
    only while at least one of the two checks is there; this one is red the
    moment the keyword argument is dropped from either call."""
    from app.core.auth import passkeys

    seen: list[object] = []

    def spy(original: Any) -> Any:
        def wrapper(**kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            seen.append(kwargs.get("require_user_verification"))
            return original(**kwargs)

        return wrapper

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        passkeys, "verify_registration_response", spy(passkeys.verify_registration_response)
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        passkeys, "verify_authentication_response", spy(passkeys.verify_authentication_response)
    )
    user = await _person(admin_engine)
    authenticator, _ = await _registered(app_engine, user)
    async with _session(app_engine, user.org_id) as s:
        options = await authentication_options(
            s, user.id, org_id=user.org_id, rp_id=RP_ID, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        await verify_authentication(
            s,
            authenticator.get(options, origin=ORIGIN),
            expected_origin=ORIGIN,
            rp_id=RP_ID,
            purpose="authenticate",
        )
    assert seen == [True, True]
```

```python
"""Passkeys (WebAuthn) as the second factor that is offered first (P2 design §2.2).

THE FOUR CEREMONY HALVES, AND NOTHING ELSE. Options out, response in, for
registration and for authentication. Which route calls them, what counts as a
failure, how failures add up (`app/core/auth/failures.py`) and what the person
is told are the callers' (Tasks 7 and 8). A refusal here is a `PasskeyRejected`
with a `reason` for the log and the tests; the caller answers every reason with
the same generic message, because W3C Web Authentication Level 3 asks that a
failed assertion be indistinguishable from "no such credential" [S14].

THE PARAMETERS, EACH WITH ITS SOURCE:

- **User verification is REQUIRED, and checked here, not only asked for.**
  `userVerification: "required"` in the options is a request to the browser; the
  `require_user_verification=True` passed to py_webauthn 3.0.1 on BOTH verify
  calls is the check. The library's default is `False`
  (`webauthn/registration/verify_registration_response.py`,
  `webauthn/authentication/verify_authentication_response.py`, both 3.0.1),
  which accepts a touch alone -- OWASP: "a touch confirming user presence alone
  is not a second factor" [S7]. Coordinator decision D22.
  `tests/test_auth_passkey_vectors.py` shows the default accepting a response
  without UV, which is why the argument is never left out.
- **No attestation** (`attestation: "none"`) and synced passkeys accepted: NIST
  admits syncable authenticators at AAL2 (SP 800-63B-4 App. B) [S1, S10].
- **Several per person** (`excludeCredentials` stops the same authenticator
  registering twice, nothing stops a second one) [S14 §13.4.6].
- **Challenges**: 32 random bytes (at least 16, [S10, S14 §13.4.3]), stored in
  `auth_webauthn_challenges`, live for `CHALLENGE_TTL`, and spent the moment a
  response naming them arrives -- BEFORE the response is verified, so a response
  that fails cannot be retried against the same challenge. One live challenge
  per person and purpose: issuing a new one retires the last.
- **Purposes do not mix.** A challenge issued to sign in (`authenticate`) never
  confirms a step-up (`step_up`, design §2.5), nor the other way round.
- **Backup eligibility is permanent** for a credential [S14: "Backup eligibility
  is a credential property and is permanent for a given public key credential
  source"]: an assertion whose BE flag differs from the one registered is
  refused.
- **The counter**: py_webauthn refuses a counter that did not move past the
  stored one unless both are zero (most synced passkeys always send zero).

THE USER HANDLE (`user.id` in the options) is `user_handle(user_id)`, a SHA-256
of the platform's user id: stable for a person, so an authenticator replaces
rather than duplicates their credential, and free of anything personal -- the
users table's ids are UUIDv7, whose first 48 bits are the account's creation
time.

THE SESSION PASSED IN is the caller's, and it must be able to write a staff
row: `auth_passkeys` and `auth_webauthn_challenges` are O tables keyed to
`users` (Task 1), whose staff rows have no client, so only an every-client
session writes them (migration 0231). The bulk statements below bypass
`app/core/global_rows.py`'s listener; under a narrowed scope RLS would make
them match nothing, which here only ever means "refused".
"""

import hashlib
import json
import secrets
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any, Literal, cast
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import delete, or_, select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from webauthn import (
    generate_authentication_options,
    generate_registration_options,
    options_to_json,
    verify_authentication_response,
    verify_registration_response,
)
from webauthn.helpers import base64url_to_bytes, parse_client_data_json
from webauthn.helpers.exceptions import WebAuthnException
from webauthn.helpers.structs import (
    AttestationConveyancePreference,
    AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria,
    AuthenticatorTransport,
    CredentialDeviceType,
    PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor,
    ResidentKeyRequirement,
    UserVerificationRequirement,
)

from app.models import User
from app.models.auth import AuthPasskey, AuthWebauthnChallenge

#: Bytes of entropy in a challenge ([S10]: "at least 16 bytes").
CHALLENGE_BYTES = 32
#: How long a challenge may be answered.
CHALLENGE_TTL = timedelta(minutes=5)
#: The browser's ceremony timeout, a hint (milliseconds): the challenge's life.
CEREMONY_TIMEOUT_MS = int(CHALLENGE_TTL.total_seconds() * 1000)
#: The longest name a person may give a passkey ("Work laptop").
NAME_MAX = 100
#: Domain separation for `user_handle`: no other hash of a user id collides.
_USER_HANDLE_CONTEXT = b"itms.webauthn.user-handle\x00"
#: The transports W3C defines, as py_webauthn spells them; anything else a
#: browser reports is dropped rather than stored.
_TRANSPORTS = {transport.value: transport for transport in AuthenticatorTransport}

Purpose = Literal["register", "authenticate", "step_up"]
AssertionPurpose = Literal["authenticate", "step_up"]
Reason = Literal["challenge", "credential", "verification", "name"]

#: Every exception a malformed or hostile response can raise on its way
#: through py_webauthn: its own, and the decoding errors of `base64url_to_bytes`
#: (`binascii.Error` is a `ValueError`) and of the JSON walk.
_MALFORMED = (WebAuthnException, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError)


class PasskeyRejected(Exception):
    """A ceremony response the platform does not accept. `reason` is for the
    log and the tests only (module docstring); it is not shown to anyone."""

    def __init__(self, *, reason: Reason) -> None:
        super().__init__(reason)
        self.reason: Reason = reason


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(UTC)


def user_handle(user_id: UUID) -> bytes:
    """The WebAuthn user handle of a person (module docstring): 32 bytes."""
    return hashlib.sha256(_USER_HANDLE_CONTEXT + user_id.bytes).digest()


def _transports(values: object) -> list[str]:
    """The known transports in a browser's list, in its order, without repeats."""
    if not isinstance(values, list):
        return []
    known: list[str] = []
    for value in values:
        if isinstance(value, str) and value in _TRANSPORTS and value not in known:
            known.append(value)
    return known


def _descriptor(
    credential_id: bytes, transports: list[str] | None
) -> PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor:
    return PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor(
        id=credential_id,
        transports=[_TRANSPORTS[t] for t in transports or [] if t in _TRANSPORTS] or None,
    )


async def _issue(
    session: AsyncSession, *, org_id: UUID, user_id: UUID | None, purpose: Purpose
) -> bytes:
    """A fresh challenge for `purpose`, stored. A person's earlier challenge for
    the same purpose is retired, and every spent or expired one of theirs is
    swept; an anonymous request (no person yet) sweeps only spent and expired
    anonymous ones, so two people signing in at once do not retire each other's."""
    now = _now()
    stale = or_(AuthWebauthnChallenge.used_at.is_not(None), AuthWebauthnChallenge.expires_at <= now)
    owner = (
        AuthWebauthnChallenge.user_id.is_(None)
        if user_id is None
        else AuthWebauthnChallenge.user_id == user_id
    )
    retire = stale if user_id is None else or_(stale, AuthWebauthnChallenge.purpose == purpose)
    await session.execute(
        delete(AuthWebauthnChallenge).where(
            AuthWebauthnChallenge.org_id == org_id, owner, retire
        )
    )
    challenge = secrets.token_bytes(CHALLENGE_BYTES)
    session.add(
        AuthWebauthnChallenge(
            org_id=org_id,
            user_id=user_id,
            purpose=purpose,
            challenge=challenge,
            expires_at=now + CHALLENGE_TTL,
        )
    )
    await session.flush()
    return challenge


async def _spend(
    session: AsyncSession, credential: dict[str, Any], *, purpose: Purpose
) -> tuple[bytes, UUID | None]:
    """Spend the challenge `credential` answers: `(challenge, its person)`.

    The challenge is read from the response's own `clientDataJSON` and marked
    used in ONE statement whose WHERE requires it unused and unexpired, so of
    two responses racing for it exactly one gets a row. Spent before the
    response is verified: a response that then fails has used it up."""
    try:
        client_data = parse_client_data_json(
            base64url_to_bytes(credential["response"]["clientDataJSON"])
        )
    except _MALFORMED as exc:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="challenge") from exc
    now = _now()
    row = (
        await session.execute(
            update(AuthWebauthnChallenge)
            .where(
                AuthWebauthnChallenge.challenge == client_data.challenge,
                AuthWebauthnChallenge.purpose == purpose,
                AuthWebauthnChallenge.used_at.is_(None),
                AuthWebauthnChallenge.expires_at > now,
            )
            .values(used_at=now)
            .returning(AuthWebauthnChallenge.challenge, AuthWebauthnChallenge.user_id)
        )
    ).one_or_none()
    if row is None:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="challenge")
    return row.challenge, row.user_id


async def registration_options(
    session: AsyncSession, user: User, *, rp_id: str, rp_name: str
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """`PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON` for `user`, as
    `@simplewebauthn/browser`'s `startRegistration({ optionsJSON })` takes it:
    user verification required, no attestation, a discoverable credential
    preferred, the person's existing passkeys excluded."""
    existing = (
        await session.execute(
            select(AuthPasskey.credential_id, AuthPasskey.transports).where(
                AuthPasskey.user_id == user.id
            )
        )
    ).all()
    challenge = await _issue(session, org_id=user.org_id, user_id=user.id, purpose="register")
    options = generate_registration_options(
        rp_id=rp_id,
        rp_name=rp_name,
        user_name=user.email,
        user_id=user_handle(user.id),
        user_display_name=user.display_name or user.email,
        challenge=challenge,
        timeout=CEREMONY_TIMEOUT_MS,
        attestation=AttestationConveyancePreference.NONE,
        authenticator_selection=AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria(
            resident_key=ResidentKeyRequirement.PREFERRED,
            user_verification=UserVerificationRequirement.REQUIRED,
        ),
        exclude_credentials=[_descriptor(cid, transports) for cid, transports in existing],
    )
    return cast(dict[str, Any], json.loads(options_to_json(options)))


async def verify_registration(
    session: AsyncSession,
    user: User,
    credential: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    name: str,
    expected_origin: str,
    rp_id: str,
) -> AuthPasskey:
    """Verify `navigator.credentials.create()`'s answer and store the passkey.

    Refused (`PasskeyRejected`): a name that is empty or longer than
    `NAME_MAX`; a challenge that is not this person's live registration
    challenge; anything py_webauthn refuses -- another origin or RP ID, no user
    presence, NO USER VERIFICATION; a credential id already registered."""
    label = name.strip()
    if not label or len(label) > NAME_MAX:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="name")
    expected, owner = await _spend(session, credential, purpose="register")
    if owner != user.id:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="challenge")
    try:
        verified = verify_registration_response(
            credential=credential,
            expected_challenge=expected,
            expected_rp_id=rp_id,
            expected_origin=expected_origin,
            require_user_verification=True,
        )
    except _MALFORMED as exc:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="verification") from exc
    # The library refused already; this is the platform's own statement of
    # the rule, so the property does not rest on one keyword argument alone.
    if not verified.user_verified:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="verification")
    taken = (
        await session.execute(
            select(AuthPasskey.id).where(AuthPasskey.credential_id == verified.credential_id)
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if taken is not None:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="credential")
    passkey = AuthPasskey(
        org_id=user.org_id,
        user_id=user.id,
        credential_id=verified.credential_id,
        public_key=verified.credential_public_key,
        sign_count=verified.sign_count,
        transports=_transports(credential.get("response", {}).get("transports")),
        backup_eligible=verified.credential_device_type == CredentialDeviceType.MULTI_DEVICE,
        backup_state=verified.credential_backed_up,
        name=label,
        created_at=_now(),
    )
    session.add(passkey)
    await session.flush()
    return passkey


async def authentication_options(
    session: AsyncSession,
    user_id: UUID | None,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    rp_id: str,
    purpose: AssertionPurpose,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """`PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` for `startAuthentication`.

    With a person: their passkeys in `allowCredentials`. Without one (a
    discoverable credential, phase 2's contacts): an empty list, and the
    challenge belongs to nobody until a passkey answers it. A step-up always
    has a person -- it confirms the one already signed in."""
    if purpose == "step_up" and user_id is None:
        raise ValueError("a step-up confirms a person")  # i18n-exempt: a caller's defect
    allowed: list[PublicKeyCredentialDescriptor] = []
    if user_id is not None:
        rows = (
            await session.execute(
                select(AuthPasskey.credential_id, AuthPasskey.transports).where(
                    AuthPasskey.user_id == user_id
                )
            )
        ).all()
        allowed = [_descriptor(cid, transports) for cid, transports in rows]
    challenge = await _issue(session, org_id=org_id, user_id=user_id, purpose=purpose)
    options = generate_authentication_options(
        rp_id=rp_id,
        challenge=challenge,
        timeout=CEREMONY_TIMEOUT_MS,
        allow_credentials=allowed,
        user_verification=UserVerificationRequirement.REQUIRED,
    )
    return cast(dict[str, Any], json.loads(options_to_json(options)))


async def verify_authentication(
    session: AsyncSession,
    credential: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    expected_origin: str,
    rp_id: str,
    purpose: AssertionPurpose,
) -> AuthPasskey:
    """Verify `navigator.credentials.get()`'s answer; the passkey that signed.

    The challenge says whose ceremony this is; the passkey must be that
    person's, and the response's user handle (when sent) must be theirs too.
    Refused (`PasskeyRejected`): an unknown, spent, expired or other-purpose
    challenge; a passkey that is not that person's; anything py_webauthn
    refuses -- origin, RP ID, signature, presence, NO USER VERIFICATION, a
    counter that did not move; a backup-eligibility flag that changed. On
    success the counter, the backup state and `last_used_at` are updated."""
    expected, owner = await _spend(session, credential, purpose=purpose)
    try:
        raw_id = base64url_to_bytes(credential["rawId"])
        sent_handle = credential["response"].get("userHandle")
        handle = None if sent_handle is None else base64url_to_bytes(sent_handle)
    except _MALFORMED as exc:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="credential") from exc
    query = select(AuthPasskey).where(AuthPasskey.credential_id == raw_id)
    if owner is not None:
        query = query.where(AuthPasskey.user_id == owner)
    passkey = (await session.execute(query)).scalar_one_or_none()
    if passkey is None or (handle is not None and handle != user_handle(passkey.user_id)):
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="credential")
    try:
        verified = verify_authentication_response(
            credential=credential,
            expected_challenge=expected,
            expected_rp_id=rp_id,
            expected_origin=expected_origin,
            credential_public_key=passkey.public_key,
            credential_current_sign_count=passkey.sign_count,
            require_user_verification=True,
        )
    except _MALFORMED as exc:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="verification") from exc
    if not verified.user_verified:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="verification")
    eligible = verified.credential_device_type == CredentialDeviceType.MULTI_DEVICE
    if eligible != passkey.backup_eligible:
        raise PasskeyRejected(reason="verification")
    passkey.sign_count = verified.new_sign_count
    passkey.backup_state = verified.credential_backed_up
    passkey.last_used_at = _now()
    await session.flush()
    return passkey
```

`raise ValueError("a step-up confirms a person")` lleva `# i18n-exempt:` en su línea: es un defecto de quien llama y
no llega a nadie (`tests/test_i18n_catalog.py`, regla `EXEMPT`). `PasskeyRejected` recibe su motivo por palabra clave
(`reason=`), que la regla de mensajes no lee: no es texto para una persona.

**Decisión del plan (1): los consumidores de `ctx.claims` leen `ctx.email`, no `ctx.principal.email`.** D14 pide que
`orgs.py:610,784` y `realm_settings.py:514,564,597` tomen el correo de la sesión. Mientras convivan la cookie y el
Bearer (D21, y MCP hasta la fase 3) una petición tiene `principal` **o** `claims`; `ctx.email` devuelve el del que
haya. `AuthContext.claims` pasa a `TokenClaims | None`, y `mcp/server.py` estrecha el tipo donde lo lee (el canal MCP
nunca lee la cookie, así que ahí nunca es `None`; las dos guardas solo dan tipo).

**Decisión del plan (2): las primitivas no auditan ni mandan correo.** `start_session`, `mark_factor`, `end*`,
`remember`, `revoke*` las llaman actos de las Tasks 7 y 8, que auditan una vez (`auth.signed_in`,
`auth.device_remembered`, `auth.device_revoked`, `auth.sessions_ended`, de la lista de la Task 8) y avisan por correo.
Esta tarea solo audita su propia ruta: `auth.session_settings_updated`.

**Decisión del plan (3): la regla CSRF también cubre `/api/v1/auth/` sin cookie, y no cubre un Bearer sin cookie.**
Global Constraints dice «con sesión por cookie»; las rutas de inicio de sesión de la Task 7 no traen cookie todavía, y
un formulario de otro sitio que inicie la sesión del atacante en el navegador de la víctima es *login CSRF*: se
exige la cabecera y el `Origin` en todo `/api/v1/auth/`. Un Bearer sin cookie no es autoridad ambiente (el navegador
no lo pone solo): las llamadas internas de MCP, el bucle del asistente y las pruebas hasta la Task 13 no cambian.
`Sec-Fetch-Site`, si viene, tiene que ser `same-origin`. Sin `ITS_PUBLIC_CONSOLE_URL` no hay origen con que comparar:
se rechaza (y la Task 5 tampoco tendría RP ID). **Las pruebas de la Task 7 que llamen a `/api/v1/auth/*` mandan
`console_headers()` y fijan `use_console`.**

**Decisión del plan (4): el identificador cambia al iniciar sesión y al confirmar el factor, no en la confirmación
reciente.** Es lo que dice §2.4. Rotar en cada confirmación reciente dejaría con 401 a las peticiones de la consola que
ya volaban con la cookie anterior. `start_session` además **termina** la sesión que todavía nombra la cookie del
navegador (`replaced`): una sesión plantada no sobrevive a un inicio de sesión [S6].

**Decisión del plan (5): `step_up_at` es «la última vez que se verificó de verdad un segundo factor en esta sesión».**
El factor al iniciar sesión cuenta (10 min); un equipo recordado no verificó nada y empieza sin él, así que la bóveda
sigue pidiéndolo (§2.6, falsificador 5). Un inicio reanudado con la contraseña tampoco cuenta.

**Decisión del plan (6): una sesión inactiva no se termina; `resumable` + `start_session(resume=…)` implementan «tras
la inactividad se pide solo la contraseña dentro de la duración máxima» (§2.4).** NIST 800-63B-4 §2.2.3 lo permite en
AAL2 («reauthenticate using only a successful password … in conjunction with the session secret» [S1]). La sesión
nueva hereda el máximo y el factor de la vieja. **La Task 7 lo conecta en `POST /auth/login`:** si `resumable(...)`
devuelve una, responde `{"state": "signed_in"}` sin pedir factor (hoy su interfaz solo lo dice del equipo recordado).

**Decisión del plan (7): `remembered_max_hours` es la duración máxima de una sesión iniciada en un equipo recordado**
(«duración máxima en un equipo recordado», §2.4); la de un contacto es siempre `contact_max_days`.

**Decisión del plan (8): la regla del dominio de la consola se aplica al técnico, no al contacto.** Es la lista de
quién puede usar la *consola*; un contacto (fase 2) entra solo al portal y su dominio es el de su cliente.

**Decisión del plan (9): `resolve` descarta la sesión de una persona que no está `active`,** aunque nadie la haya
terminado: desactivar a alguien la corta en la siguiente petición (§2.4). `last_seen_at` se escribe como mucho una vez
por minuto; los sockets resuelven con `touch=False` (una pestaña abierta no es actividad).

**Decisión del plan (10): la confirmación reciente se conecta ya a sacar una credencial de la bóveda**
(`POST /credentials/{id}/checkout`), la acción de §2.5 que no es de la Task 7 ni de la 8. Un Bearer no tiene sesión que
confirmar y pasa, como antes, hasta la Task 13; el canal MCP nunca llega (`MCP_FORBIDDEN_CODES`, `NEVER_EXPOSED`).
**La Task 13 tiene que hacer estricta `require_step_up` cuando la consola deje el Bearer.**

**Decisión del plan (11): en los sockets, la cookie solo cuando no se ofrece subprotocolo y hay cookie.** Sin token y
sin cookie, el camino Bearer con `""` cierra 4401, como hoy. Con cookie: `Origin` primero (otro origen, 4403: un
WebSocket no pasa por CORS y la cookie viaja en cualquier apretón de manos), luego la sesión (4401), luego la misma
puerta. Se acepta sin subprotocolo: el navegador no ofreció ninguno.

**Decisión del plan (12): el rechazo CSRF no se registra en el log.** El recuento de llamadas de log
(`tests/test_logging_discipline.py::test_the_sweep_actually_finds_log_calls`, 107) y su espejo en
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-logging-kernel-design.md` §2.2 no se mueven por un 403 que la consola ya muestra.

**Decisión del plan (13): `recognised` rechaza un equipo recordado antes del último cambio de contraseña**
(`auth_passwords.changed_at`), aunque quien cambió la contraseña olvide `revoke_all_for_user`: el falsificador 5 no
depende de que nadie se acuerde.

**Decisión del plan (14): `GET` y `PUT /api/v1/settings/sessions` son herramientas MCP, como `/settings/email`**, con su
descripción en `part_d.py`; el GET pasa las seis propiedades y espera en `PENDING_TOOL_REVIEW`, como `/settings/email`.

**Decisión del plan (15): `end`, `mark_factor` y `mark_step_up` reciben la sesión de base de datos** (la interfaz las
listaba sin ella): sin organización no se puede abrir una.

Crear `backend/tests/session_support.py`:

```python
"""Console sessions for API tests (P2 phase 1, Task 6).

`sign_in` starts a REAL session through `app.core.auth.sessions.start_session`
-- the same row, hash and lifetimes a sign-in makes -- and returns the headers a
browser on the console would send with it: the cookie, `X-ITMS-Request` and
the console's `Origin` (`app/core/auth/csrf.py`).

THE COOKIE IS A HEADER HERE, ON PURPOSE (coordinator decision D12). httpx keeps
a cookie jar, and it will not send a `Secure` cookie -- every `__Host-` one is
-- to `http://api.test`. The tests therefore pass `Cookie:` explicitly, which
is exactly what the browser puts on the wire.

`use_console` sets `ITS_PUBLIC_CONSOLE_URL` for the test: without it there is
no console origin, and every write on a session is refused.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from starlette.requests import Request

from app.core.auth.csrf import CSRF_HEADER
from app.core.auth.sessions import DEVICE_COOKIE, SESSION_COOKIE, start_session
from app.core.client_scope import ClientScope
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.models import User

CONSOLE = "https://itms.test"


def use_console(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, env: Any) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(env.app.state.settings, "public_console_url", CONSOLE)


def console_headers() -> dict[str, str]:
    """What the console's `ApiClient` adds to every request (Task 10)."""
    return {CSRF_HEADER: "1", "Origin": CONSOLE}


def cookie_header(session_token: str | None = None, device_token: str | None = None) -> str:
    parts = []
    if session_token is not None:
        parts.append(f"{SESSION_COOKIE}={session_token}")
    if device_token is not None:
        parts.append(f"{DEVICE_COOKIE}={device_token}")
    return "; ".join(parts)


def http_request(env: Any, *, cookie: str = "", user_agent: str = "pytest") -> Request:
    """A request as a sign-in route receives it: what `start_session` reads."""
    headers = [(b"user-agent", user_agent.encode())]
    if cookie:
        headers.append((b"cookie", cookie.encode()))
    return Request(
        {
            "type": "http",
            "method": "POST",
            "path": "/api/v1/auth/login",
            "headers": headers,
            "query_string": b"",
            "client": ("203.0.113.9", 50000),
            "app": env.app,
        }
    )


async def user_id_of(env: Any, sub: str) -> UUID:
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine) as s:
        user_id: UUID = (
            await s.execute(select(User.id).where(User.external_subject == sub))
        ).scalar_one()
        return user_id


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SignedIn:
    session_id: UUID
    user_id: UUID
    token: str
    headers: dict[str, str]


async def sign_in(
    env: Any,
    org_id: UUID,
    sub: str,
    *,
    factor_done: bool = True,
    trusted_device_id: UUID | None = None,
) -> SignedIn:
    """A session for the user `ApiEnv.create_user` returned `sub` for."""
    user_id = await user_id_of(env, sub)
    async with org_session(org_id, engine=env.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as s:
        user = (await s.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))).scalar_one()
        row, token = await start_session(
            s,
            user,
            kind=user.kind,
            request=http_request(env),
            factor_done=factor_done,
            trusted_device_id=trusted_device_id,
        )
        session_id = row.id
    headers = {"Cookie": cookie_header(token), **console_headers()}
    return SignedIn(session_id=session_id, user_id=user_id, token=token, headers=headers)
```

```python
"""Sessions, their policy and remembered devices (P2 design §2.4-§2.6, §6.4).

`app/core/auth/sessions.py`, `session_policy.py` and `devices.py` against the
real database (`auth_sessions`, `auth_trusted_devices`, `auth_org_settings`,

Each refusal names the line it protects.
"""

import hashlib
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from starlette.requests import Request

from app.core.auth.devices import (
```
