**Decisión del plan (1): `kc_client.py` no se toca.** Se queda sin llamador en el ciclo de vida, pero
`mcp/api.py:90` sigue usando `KeycloakAdminConfig` y `revoke_consent` (MCP en Keycloak hasta la fase 3), y
`tests/test_user_admin_client.py` prueba el resto. `ENROLMENT_ACTIONS` y `PASSWORD_RESET_ACTIONS` se quedan, así
que `_actions_the_backend_mails` (`tests/test_console_auth_realm.py`) no se re-apunta. La fase 4 borra el módulo con
Keycloak (diseño §8.4).

**Decisión del plan (2): no hay «restablecer contraseña» de un administrador.** El diseño §7 da al administrador
invitar, reenviar, cancelar y restablecer **factores**; la contraseña la restablece la persona por su enlace (§2.8,
Task 7). `POST /users/{id}/reset-password` (un correo de Keycloak) desaparece y su prueba se re-apunta a «esta ruta
ya no existe». `resend-enrolment` pasa a `invite/resend`.

**Decisión del plan (3): cancelar una invitación marca la cuenta como eliminada.** Una cuenta invitada que no
eligió contraseña no puede entrar; cancelarla deja el enlace muerto, quita sus permisos y la marca `deleted`
(la fila se conserva, regla 2), con los raíles de eliminar (último `org-admin`, `super-admin`). Una vez aceptada,
cancelar es 409: para eso están desactivar y eliminar.

**Decisión del plan (4): el enlace de invitación se muestra si el correo no salió, por la razón que sea.** El diseño
lo dice para «sin correo configurado»; un servidor SMTP caído deja al administrador en la misma situación. El
enlace solo lo ve quien tiene `users.manage` en todos los clientes, que ya podría concederse cualquier cosa: no es
una escalada. `user.invited` / `user.invite_resent` guardan `link_shown`, nunca el enlace.

**Decisión del plan (5): restablecer los factores de otro usa la puerta de todos los clientes y la confirmación
reciente de la Task 6.** `_MANAGE` (`users.manage` sobre todos los clientes, `api.py:65`) y, en el manejador,
`require_step_up(ctx)` (Task 6): con la cookie, 403 `{"code": "step_up_required"}` si el segundo factor del
administrador no se confirmó en los últimos 10 minutos. El Bearer de la consola (D21) pasa, como pasa hoy en el
checkout de la bóveda: la Task 13 hace estricta `require_step_up` cuando retira el Bearer, y entonces esta ruta lo
rechaza sin tocarla. No hay raíl de `super-admin` (restablecer quita factores; no da acceso sin la contraseña), pero
sí `_refuse_self`: los factores propios se cambian en Mi seguridad.

**Decisión del plan (6): el raíl del último `org-admin` sigue contando las cuentas activas, con o sin contraseña.**
Hasta la Task 13 las pruebas crean administradores sin contraseña (`tests/conftest.py:268-287`); contar solo los que
ya eligieron contraseña rompería esos raíles. Consecuencia conocida: un `org-admin` invitado y aún no aceptado cuenta
para el raíl. Se anota para la Task 13 / revisión.

**Decisión del plan (7): eliminar y cancelar terminan las sesiones con el motivo `"disabled"`.** El `EndReason` de
la Task 6 no tiene `"deleted"`; las dos dejan la cuenta sin poder entrar, como desactivarla, y `auth.sessions_ended`
no se escribe por ellas (lo dice `user.deleted` / `user.invite_cancelled`). Terminar las sesiones de otro, sin más,
es `"ended_by_admin"`.

**Decisión del plan (8): «invitación pendiente» es un token de invitación sin usar de alguien sin contraseña.** Se
lee de `auth_action_tokens` (propósito `invite`, `used_at` nulo) y de la ausencia de `auth_passwords`, sin columna
nueva. Una invitación caducada sigue pendiente (se puede reenviar o cancelar); una persona creada antes de esta
fase, sin contraseña y sin invitación, no aparece como pendiente.

**Decisión del plan (9): el recuento de llamadas de log se da como «menos 5», no como un número.** Las Tasks 3, 4 y
9 añaden un `logger.warning` cada una (`rate_limit.py`, `totp.py`, el token `loopback`) y la 9 va en paralelo con
esta: el número absoluto depende del orden en que se fusionen. Lo que esta tarea cambia es fijo: quita cinco.

**Decisión del plan (10): el enlace de recuperación no cambia la contraseña; abre una sesión sin factor.** Decisión
del coordinador: quien recupera perdió los segundos factores, no la contraseña. `POST /auth/recover/accept` consume el
enlace, borra los factores (`factors.clear_second_factors`), revoca los equipos, termina todas las sesiones
(`"factors_reset"`) y abre una sesión pendiente, como la de una invitación aceptada: la consola lleva al alta del
primer factor y `enroll/finish` (Task 7) la completa. El enlace solo lo emite el comando del servidor (falsificador
9), así que esa sesión sin contraseña la abre quien ya tiene el servidor.

- [ ] **Step 1: Las pruebas nuevas del ciclo de vida, que fallan**

Crear `backend/tests/test_user_lifecycle.py`:

```python
"""The platform's own technician lifecycle (P2 phase 1 Task 8, design §2.4, §7).

- An invitation is a 72-hour, single-use link; the invitee chooses a password
  and goes straight to enrolling the first factor. The link is shown to the
  administrator once, and only when no mail carried it.
- Resend replaces the link; cancel kills it and the account.
- Resetting another person's factors needs the administrator's OWN second
  factor confirmed in the last ten minutes (design §2.5), wipes the factors,
  ends the person's sessions, forgets their devices and tells them.
- Disabling a person ends their sessions and forgets their devices at once
  (design §2.4); ending their sessions is an act of its own.
"""

from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any
from uuid import UUID

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core.auth.sessions import DEVICE_COOKIE, SESSION_COOKIE
from app.models import AuditEvent, Role, User, UserRole
from app.models.auth import AuthPassword, AuthSession, AuthTotp
from tests.auth_support import (
    CONSOLE,
    Staff,
    browser,
    capture_mail,
    console_ready,
    cookie,
    enrol_totp,
    fresh_code,
    link_token,
    login,
    signed_in,
)


@pytest.fixture()
def lifecycle_env(api_env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Any:
    console_ready(api_env, monkeypatch)
    api_env.mail = capture_mail(monkeypatch)
    return api_env


async def _role(env: Any, name: str) -> UUID:
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine) as session:
        return (
            await session.execute(select(Role.id).where(Role.name == name, Role.org_id.is_(None)))
        ).scalar_one()


async def _audit(env: Any, org_id: UUID, action: str) -> list[AuditEvent]:
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine) as session:
        return list(
            (
                await session.execute(
                    select(AuditEvent)
                    .where(AuditEvent.org_id == org_id, AuditEvent.action == action)
                    .order_by(AuditEvent.id)
                )
            ).scalars()
        )


async def _invite(env: Any, headers: dict[str, str], email: str = "ana@toeshee.test") -> Any:
    tech = await _role(env, "technician")
    return await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/users/invite",
        headers=headers,
        json={"email": email, "display_name": "Ana", "grants": [{"role_id": str(tech)}]},
    )


async def _age_step_up(env: Any, user_id: UUID) -> None:
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine) as session:
        await session.execute(
            update(AuthSession)
            .where(AuthSession.user_id == user_id)
            .values(step_up_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(minutes=11))
        )
        await session.commit()


async def test_an_invitee_chooses_a_password_and_goes_on_to_the_first_factor(
    lifecycle_env: Any,
) -> None:
    env = lifecycle_env
    org = await env.create_org("invite")
    admin = await signed_in(env, org, "org-admin")
    invited = await _invite(env, admin.headers())
    assert invited.status_code == 201, invited.text
    assert invited.json()["invite_link"] is None
    mail = env.mail.sent[-1]
    assert mail.to == "ana@toeshee.test"
    token = link_token(mail.text)

    details = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/invite/details", headers=browser(), json={"token": token}
    )
    weak = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/invite/accept", headers=browser(), json={"token": token, "password": "short"}
    )
    network = browser()
    accepted = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/invite/accept",
        headers=network,
        json={"token": token, "password": "Pelican-Orbit-Lantern-58"},
    )
    again = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/invite/accept",
        headers=browser(),
        json={"token": token, "password": "Pelican-Orbit-Lantern-59"},
    )

    assert details.json() == {"email": "ana@toeshee.test", "display_name": "Ana"}
    assert weak.status_code == 422
    assert weak.json() == {"code": "password_rejected", "detail": "Use at least 12 characters."}
    assert accepted.status_code == 200, accepted.text
    assert accepted.json() == {"state": "enroll_required"}
    assert again.status_code == 410 and again.json()["code"] == "invalid_link"
    pending = cookie(accepted, SESSION_COOKIE)
    assert pending
    ana = Staff(
        org,
        UUID(invited.json()["user_id"]),
        "",
        "ana@toeshee.test",
        "Pelican-Orbit-Lantern-58",
        network,
        session=pending,
    )
    await enrol_totp(env, ana)
    assert (await env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=ana.headers())).status_code == 200
    changed = await _audit(env, org, "auth.password_changed")
    assert [e.meta for e in changed][-1] == {"via": "invite"}
    listed = (await env.client.get("/api/v1/users", headers=admin.headers())).json()["users"]
    row = next(u for u in listed if u["id"] == invited.json()["user_id"])
    assert (row["invite_pending"], row["invite_expires_at"]) == (False, None)


async def test_the_link_is_shown_once_when_no_mail_could_carry_it(lifecycle_env: Any) -> None:
    env = lifecycle_env
    org = await env.create_org("invite-nomail")

async def test_resend_replaces_the_link_and_cancel_kills_it_with_the_account(
    lifecycle_env: Any,
) -> None:
    env = lifecycle_env
    org = await env.create_org("invite-resend")
    admin = await signed_in(env, org, "org-admin")
    env.mail.configured = False
    invited = (await _invite(env, admin.headers())).json()
    first = invited["invite_link"].split("#", 1)[1]

    resent = await env.client.post(
        f"/api/v1/users/{invited['user_id']}/invite/resend", headers=admin.headers()
    )
    assert set(resent.json()) == {"invite_link"}
    second = resent.json()["invite_link"].split("#", 1)[1]
    old = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/invite/details", headers=browser(), json={"token": first}
    )
    cancelled = await env.client.delete(
        f"/api/v1/users/{invited['user_id']}/invite", headers=admin.headers()
    )
    new = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/invite/details", headers=browser(), json={"token": second}
    )

    assert resent.status_code == 200 and second != first
    assert old.status_code == 410
    assert cancelled.status_code == 204
    assert new.status_code == 410
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine) as session:
        user = await session.get(User, UUID(invited["user_id"]))
        grants = (
            await session.execute(
                select(UserRole.id).where(UserRole.user_id == UUID(invited["user_id"]))
            )
        ).scalars().all()
    assert user is not None and user.status == "deleted" and grants == []
    resent_events = await _audit(env, org, "user.invite_resent")
    assert [e.action for e in resent_events] == ["user.invite_resent"]
    assert len(await _audit(env, org, "user.invite_cancelled")) == 1

async def test_a_factor_reset_needs_the_administrators_own_recent_confirmation(
    lifecycle_env: Any,
) -> None:
    """Design §2.5 and plan decision 5: eleven minutes after the
    administrator's own factor, the reset is a 403 and nothing is wiped.
    Delete the `require_step_up(ctx)` line in `api.py::reset_factors` and the
    member's TOTP is gone."""

async def test_a_factor_reset_wipes_the_factors_ends_the_sessions_and_tells_the_person(
    lifecycle_env: Any,
) -> None:
    env = lifecycle_env
    org = await env.create_org("reset")
    admin = await signed_in(env, org, "org-admin")
    member = await signed_in(env, org, "technician")
    member.session = None
    await login(env, member)
    done = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/factor/totp",
        headers=member.headers(),
        json={"code": await fresh_code(env, member), "remember_device": True},
    )
    member.session, member.device = cookie(done, SESSION_COOKIE), cookie(done, DEVICE_COOKIE)

    reset = await env.client.post(
        f"/api/v1/users/{member.user_id}/factors/reset", headers=admin.headers()
    )

    assert reset.status_code == 204, reset.text
    assert (await env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=member.headers())).status_code == 401
    member.session = None
    assert (await login(env, member)).json() == {"state": "enroll_required"}
    assert any(m.to == member.email and "reset" in m.subject.lower() for m in env.mail.sent)
    events = await _audit(env, org, "user.factors_reset")
    assert [(e.actor_id, e.meta["via"]) for e in events] == [(admin.user_id, "administrator")]

async def test_disable_signs_the_person_out_and_forgets_their_devices(lifecycle_env: Any) -> None:
    """Design §2.4: "Desactivar a una persona corta sus sesiones ... y sus equipos
    recordados al instante". Delete the two calls in `service.set_enabled` and the
    re-enabled person signs straight back in through the remembered device."""
    env = lifecycle_env
    org = await env.create_org("disable")
    admin = await signed_in(env, org, "org-admin")
    member = await signed_in(env, org, "technician")
    member.session = None
    await login(env, member)
    done = await env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/factor/totp",
        headers=member.headers(),
        json={"code": await fresh_code(env, member), "remember_device": True},
    )
    member.session, member.device = cookie(done, SESSION_COOKIE), cookie(done, DEVICE_COOKIE)

    disabled = await env.client.post(
        f"/api/v1/users/{member.user_id}/disable", headers=admin.headers()
    )
    cut = await env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=member.headers())
    await env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{member.user_id}/enable", headers=admin.headers())
    member.session = None
    after = await login(env, member)

    assert disabled.status_code == 200 and cut.status_code == 401
    assert after.json()["state"] == "factor_required"
```

```python
"""`python -m app.core.auth.recover --email <address>` (design §7, Q5; falsifier 9).

async def test_the_link_removes_the_factors_once_and_leads_to_a_new_one(auth_env: Any) -> None:
    org = await auth_env.create_org("recover")
    who = await signed_in(auth_env, org, "org-admin")
    old_session = who.session

    link = await recover.issue_recovery_link(settings=auth_env.settings, email=who.email)
    token = link.split("#", 1)[1]
    details = await auth_env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/recover/details", headers=browser(), json={"token": token}
    )
    network = browser()
    accepted = await auth_env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/recover/accept", headers=network, json={"token": token}
    )
    again = await auth_env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/recover/accept", headers=browser(), json={"token": token}
    )
    as_reset = await auth_env.client.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/password/reset",
        headers=browser(),
        json={"token": token, "password": "Pelican-Orbit-Lantern-58"},
    )

    assert link.startswith(f"{CONSOLE}/recover#")
    assert details.json() == {"email": who.email}
    assert accepted.status_code == 200, accepted.text
    assert accepted.json() == {"state": "enroll_required"}
    assert again.status_code == 410 and again.json()["code"] == "invalid_link"
    assert as_reset.status_code == 410
    # Every earlier session ended; the new one is pending and enrols a factor.
    who.session = old_session
    assert (await auth_env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=who.headers())).status_code == 401
    who.session, who.network = cookie(accepted, SESSION_COOKIE), network
    await enrol_totp(auth_env, who)
    assert (await auth_env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=who.headers())).status_code == 200
    # The password did not change.
    who.session = None
    assert (await login(auth_env, who)).json()["state"] == "factor_required"
    async with AsyncSession(auth_env.admin_engine) as session:
        events = {
            e.action: e
            for e in (
                await session.execute(select(AuditEvent).where(AuditEvent.org_id == org))
            ).scalars()
        }
    issued = events["user.recovery_link_issued"]
    assert (issued.actor_type, issued.actor_id) == ("system", None)
    assert token not in str(issued.meta)
    used = events["user.recovery_link_used"]
    assert (used.actor_type, used.actor_id) == ("user", who.user_id)
    assert token not in str(used.meta)
    subjects = [m.subject.lower() for m in auth_env.mail.sent if m.to == who.email]
    assert any("recovery link" in s for s in subjects)
    assert any("sign-in methods were reset" in s for s in subjects)

def test_the_command_prints_the_link_or_says_why_not(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    async def gives(*, settings: Any, email: str) -> str:

    monkeypatch.setattr(recover, "get_settings", lambda: None)

def test_the_recovery_command_does_not_exist_over_http() -> None:
    """FALSIFIER 9. Each assertion fails if somebody wires the command to a route."""
    for path, route in flatten(build_router_only_app().router):
        module = getattr(getattr(route, "endpoint", None), "__module__", "")
        assert module != "app.core.auth.recover", path

    for py in APP.rglob("*.py"):
        if py == RECOVER_PY:
            continue
        for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(py.read_text())):
            if isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                assert node.module != "app.core.auth.recover", py
                assert not (
                    node.module == "app.core.auth" and any(a.name == "recover" for a in node.names)
                ), py
            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                assert all(a.name != "app.core.auth.recover" for a in node.names), py

    source = RECOVER_PY.read_text()
    assert "APIRouter" not in source and "fastapi" not in source
    issuers = sorted(
        str(py.relative_to(APP))
        for py in APP.rglob("*.py")
        if "purpose=action_tokens.RECOVER" in py.read_text()
    )
    assert issuers == ["core/auth/recover.py"]
```

```python
async def test_a_made_up_link_is_the_same_410_on_every_link_page(lifecycle_env: Any) -> None:
    env = lifecycle_env
```

En `backend/app/modules/user_admin/words.py`, sustituir el archivo entero por:

```python
"""The words the user-administration refusals say about what was being done.

`say(table, value)` (app/core/wire_words.py) returns the English phrase itself
in English, so every English message is what it always was. In Spanish the
phrase is an infinitive that fits the sentence it is printed in; the console's
own words are "Deshabilitar", "Eliminar" and "Quitar"
(`settings.users` in `frontend/src/i18n/es/settings.ts`).

Two tables, because the two sentences need two grammars:

- `ACTION_WORDS`: after "you cannot ... your own account".
- `OUTCOME_WORDS`: after "cannot be ..." (the English participle; the Spanish
  infinitive of "no se puede ...").

(A third, for "the identity provider ... to ...", went with the identity
provider's calls in P2 phase 1 Task 8.)
"""

from app.core.i18n import N_

# The wire words the refusal helpers are called with. Constants, so a call such as
# `_refuse_self(actor, user, DISABLE)` reads as what it is: a word the tables below
# say, not a sentence handed to a raiser.
DISABLE = "disable"
DELETE = "delete"
RESET_FACTORS = "reset the sign-in methods of"
CANNOT_BE_DISABLED = "disabled"
CANNOT_BE_DELETED = "deleted"
CANNOT_BE_STRIPPED = "stripped of the role"

ACTION_WORDS = {
    DISABLE: N_("user admin, you cannot ... your own account: disable"),
    DELETE: N_("user admin, you cannot ... your own account: delete"),
    RESET_FACTORS: N_("user admin, you cannot ... your own account: reset the sign-in methods of"),
}

OUTCOME_WORDS = {
    CANNOT_BE_DISABLED: N_("user admin, cannot be ...: disabled"),
    CANNOT_BE_DELETED: N_("user admin, cannot be ...: deleted"),
    CANNOT_BE_STRIPPED: N_("user admin, cannot be ...: stripped of the role"),
}
```

En `backend/app/modules/user_admin/service.py`:

1. `:1-36` (docstring) pasa a:

```python
"""User lifecycle: the decisions, separately from the HTTP.

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-rbac-and-user-lifecycle-design.md` §2, and
the platform's own accounts since P2 phase 1
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-autenticacion-propia-design.md` §7):
invite, resend, cancel, reset the factors, disable, delete.

Everything worth arguing about lives here rather than in `api.py`: the rails
that stop an administrator locking the organization out of itself, the tenant
predicates, and the audit records. The route handlers open a tenant session,
call one function, and translate `UserAdminError` into the status this module
chose.

THE THREE THINGS THIS MODULE REFUSES TO DO, each stated where it is enforced
below but collected here because they are the reason the module exists:

1. **It never sees a password.** A technician chooses their own on the page a
   one-time link opens (`app.core.auth.flows.accept_invite`,
   `flows.reset_password`). Nothing here generates, stores, displays or
   returns one, and `tests/test_user_admin_api.py` scans every response body
   on the surface to keep it that way. The one secret that leaves is an
   invitation link -- once, to the administrator who asked for it, and only
   when no mail carried it (design §7).
2. **It never hard-deletes a user.** 89 foreign-key columns across 21 tables
   reference `users.id` -- audit `actor_id` among them -- so deleting the row
   would either fail on the constraints or turn the audit log from evidence into
   a list of anonymous events. The row is marked `status='deleted'` and kept.
3. **It never calls an identity provider.** Since P2 phase 1 the platform is
   its own. A technician invited here has no Keycloak identity --
   `external_subject` is a placeholder no provider issued
   (`LOCAL_SUBJECT_PREFIX`) -- so until phase 3 moves the MCP server onto the
   platform's own sign-in they cannot connect an AI app over MCP (plan
   decision D5, accepted: nothing is deployed before the four projects end).

DISABLE, DELETE AND A FACTOR RESET END THE PERSON'S SESSIONS AND FORGET THEIR
REMEMBERED DEVICES in the same transaction as the change (design §2.4):
`users.status` refuses the next admission at every door, and ending the
sessions stops the cookie already in a browser -- at once, not at its expiry.
"""
```

```python
async def _open_invites(
    session: AsyncSession, org_id: UUID, user_ids: Sequence[UUID]
) -> dict[UUID, datetime]:
    """The expiry of each person's unused invitation, for people who have not
    chosen a password yet. Read under the request's scope: these are global
    rows (a technician's), which a pinned scope may read."""
    if not user_ids:
        return {}
    rows = await session.execute(
        select(AuthActionToken.user_id, func.max(AuthActionToken.expires_at))
        .where(
            AuthActionToken.org_id == org_id,
            AuthActionToken.user_id.in_(list(user_ids)),
            AuthActionToken.purpose == action_tokens.INVITE,
            AuthActionToken.used_at.is_(None),
            ~exists().where(AuthPassword.user_id == AuthActionToken.user_id),
        )
        .group_by(AuthActionToken.user_id)
    )
    return {user_id: expires for user_id, expires in rows.tuples()}


async def _accepted(session: AsyncSession, user_id: UUID) -> bool:
    """Has this person chosen a password -- accepted their invitation?"""
    return await session.get(AuthPassword, user_id) is not None
```

9. La sección de creación (`:559-714`, de `# create -- rule 3 (ordering) and rule 5 (SMTP)` hasta el

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# create and invite -- rules 1 and 3
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def _normalise_email(email: str) -> str:
    """One `@`, lowercased, or a 422.

    Refusing rather than parsing anything with other than exactly one `@` is the
    same call `is_allowed_domain` makes and for the same reason: quoted local
    parts are legal RFC and carrying a second parser for them buys nothing.
    """
    cleaned = email.strip().lower()
    local, _, domain = cleaned.partition("@")
    if cleaned.count("@") != 1 or not local or not domain:
        raise UserAdminError(422, tr("that is not an email address this console can use"))
    return cleaned


async def create_user(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    actor_id: UUID,
    email: str,
    display_name: str,
    grants: Sequence[Grant],
    email_domain: str | None,
) -> UserView:
    """The local row and its grants -- and nothing else (rules 1 and 3).

    Shared by the invitation and the first boot (`app/api/v1/setup.py`), so
    the domain rule, the role rails, the address check and the `user.created`
    record are one implementation. The person gets no credential here: the
    invitation's link (`invite_user`) or the setup form's password
    (`staff_password.store`) gives them one.

    Everything that can be refused is refused before the first write.
    """
    address = _normalise_email(email)

    # THE DOMAIN RULE, ENFORCED HERE TOO (spec §3, rule 4), and through
    # `domain_refusal` -- the helper every door calls -- so an EMPTY or
    # whitespace-only setting means no restriction here exactly as there.
    refusal = domain_refusal(address, email_domain)
    if refusal is not None:
        raise UserAdminError(422, refusal)

    if len({(g.role_id, g.client_id) for g in grants}) != len(grants):
        raise UserAdminError(422, tr("the same role is listed twice for the same client"))
    roles = [await _visible_role(session, org_id, g.role_id) for g in grants]
    for grant in grants:
        if grant.client_id is not None:
            await _grantable_client(session, org_id, grant.client_id)

    # ANY user, contacts included: one address is one person (MSP clients
    # Task 9 review 1, I1). LIMIT 1: rows from before D2's unique index may
    # share an address, and that is a 409 here, not a MultipleResultsFound.
    existing = (
        await session.execute(
            select(User.id).where(User.org_id == org_id, User.email == address).limit(1)
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if existing is not None:
        raise UserAdminError(409, tr("a user with that email address already exists here"))

    user = User(
        org_id=org_id,
        external_subject=f"{LOCAL_SUBJECT_PREFIX}{uuid4()}",
        email=address,
        display_name=display_name,
        status=ACTIVE,
    )
    session.add(user)
    try:
        await session.flush()
        for grant, role in zip(grants, roles, strict=True):
            session.add(
                UserRole(org_id=org_id, user_id=user.id, role_id=role.id, client_id=grant.client_id)
            )
        await session.flush()
    except IntegrityError as exc:
        # The address in another case (`ux_users_org_lower_email_staff`, D2)
        # or a concurrent create: raising rolls the whole transaction back.
        raise UserAdminError(409, tr("a user with that email address already exists here")) from exc

    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="user.created",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={
            "email": address,
            "display_name": display_name,
            "roles": sorted(r.name for r in roles),
            "grants": [
                {"role": role.name, "client_id": str(g.client_id) if g.client_id else None}
                for g, role in zip(grants, roles, strict=True)
            ],
        },
    )
    return await _view(session, org_id, user)


async def _issue_invitation(
    session: AsyncSession,
    org_id: UUID,
    actor_id: UUID,
    user: User,
    console_url: str,
    deliver: Deliver,
) -> InvitedUser:
    """A new 72-hour link (replacing any earlier one), handed to `deliver`."""
    token = await action_tokens.issue(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        user_id=user.id,
        purpose=action_tokens.INVITE,
        ttl=action_tokens.INVITE_TTL,
        created_by=actor_id,
    )
    link = action_tokens.link(console_url, "invite", token)
    view = await _view(session, org_id, user)
    return InvitedUser(user=view, link=link, delivered=await deliver(view, link))


async def invite_user(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    actor_id: UUID,
    email: str,
    display_name: str,
    grants: Sequence[Grant],
    email_domain: str | None,
    console_url: str,
    deliver: Deliver,
) -> InvitedUser:
    """Design §7: the technician, their grants, and a one-time link to choose a
    password and set up the second factor."""
    created = await create_user(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_id=actor_id,
        email=email,
        display_name=display_name,
        grants=grants,
        email_domain=email_domain,
    )
    user = await _target(session, org_id, created.id)
    invited = await _issue_invitation(session, org_id, actor_id, user, console_url, deliver)
    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="user.invited",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={"email": user.email, "link_shown": not invited.delivered},
    )
    return invited


async def resend_invite(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    actor_id: UUID,
    user_id: UUID,
    console_url: str,
    deliver: Deliver,
) -> InvitedUser:
    """A new link for an invitation not accepted yet; the old one stops working."""
    user = await _target(session, org_id, user_id)
    _require_live(user)
    if await _accepted(session, user.id):
        raise UserAdminError(409, tr("this person has already accepted their invitation"))
    invited = await _issue_invitation(session, org_id, actor_id, user, console_url, deliver)
    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="user.invite_resent",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={"email": user.email, "link_shown": not invited.delivered},
    )
    return invited


async def cancel_invite(
    session: AsyncSession, *, org_id: UUID, actor_id: UUID, user_id: UUID
) -> None:
    """Plan decision 3: the link dies, the grants go, the account is marked
    deleted -- with delete's rails. An accepted invitation is a 409."""
    user = await _target(session, org_id, user_id)
    _require_live(user)
    if await _accepted(session, user.id):
        raise UserAdminError(409, tr("this person has already accepted their invitation"))
    await _refuse_touching_a_super_admin(session, org_id, user.id, CANNOT_BE_DELETED)
    await _refuse_stranding_the_org(session, org_id, user.id, CANNOT_BE_DELETED)
    await action_tokens.revoke_open(session, user_id=user.id, purpose=action_tokens.INVITE)
    # Counted before the delete, as `delete_user` does: `Result.rowcount` is
    # not on the type `session.execute` returns.
    grants = list(
        (
            await session.execute(
                select(UserRole.id).where(UserRole.user_id == user.id, UserRole.org_id == org_id)
            )
        ).scalars()
    )
    await session.execute(
        delete(UserRole).where(UserRole.user_id == user.id, UserRole.org_id == org_id)
    )
    await end_all_for_user(session, user.id, "disabled")
    user.status = DELETED
    session.add(user)
    await session.flush()
    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="user.invite_cancelled",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={"email": user.email, "roles_removed": len(grants)},
    )
```

10. `set_enabled` (`:855-904`, desde el encabezado `# disable / enable`) pasa a:

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# disable / enable
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def set_enabled(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    actor_id: UUID,
    user_id: UUID,
    enabled: bool,
) -> UserView:
    """Turn an account off, or back on.

    OFF MEANS NOW (design §2.4). `users.status` refuses the next admission at
    every door -- an AI app over MCP included -- and the person's sessions and
    remembered devices end in this same transaction, so the cookie already in
    a browser stops working too. ON restores the status only: the person signs
    in again, with their second factor.
    """
    user = await _target(session, org_id, user_id)
    _require_live(user)
    if not enabled:
        _refuse_self(actor_id, user.id, DISABLE)
        await _refuse_touching_a_super_admin(session, org_id, user.id, CANNOT_BE_DISABLED)
        await _refuse_stranding_the_org(session, org_id, user.id, CANNOT_BE_DISABLED)

    user.status = ACTIVE if enabled else DISABLED
    session.add(user)
    await session.flush()
    if not enabled:
        await end_all_for_user(session, user.id, "disabled")
        await revoke_all_for_user(session, user.id)
    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="user.enabled" if enabled else "user.disabled",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={"email": user.email, "status": user.status},
    )
    return await _view(session, org_id, user)
```

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the factors and the sessions of somebody else (design §2.5, §7)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def reset_factors(
    session: AsyncSession,
    *,
    org_id: UUID,
    actor_id: UUID,
    user_id: UUID,
    vault: VaultService,
) -> None:
    """Every passkey, the TOTP, the recovery codes and the failure counters
    go; the sessions end and the remembered devices are forgotten; the person
    is told. Their next sign-in enrols a new factor (design §7). The route
    has already checked the administrator's own recent confirmation."""
    user = await _target(session, org_id, user_id)
    _require_live(user)
    _refuse_self(actor_id, user.id, RESET_FACTORS)
    await clear_second_factors(session, user.id)
    await end_all_for_user(session, user.id, "factors_reset")
    await revoke_all_for_user(session, user.id)
    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="user.factors_reset",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={"email": user.email, "via": "administrator"},
    )
    await notices.tell(session, user, "factors_reset", vault=vault, actor_id=actor_id)


async def end_sessions(
    session: AsyncSession, *, org_id: UUID, actor_id: UUID, user_id: UUID
) -> None:
    """Every console session of the person ends; their remembered devices stay
    (a reset or a disable forgets those)."""
    user = await _target(session, org_id, user_id)
    await end_all_for_user(session, user.id, "ended_by_admin")
    await audit_service.record(
        session,
        org_id=org_id,
        actor_type="user",
        actor_id=actor_id,
        action="auth.sessions_ended",
        target_type="user",
        target_id=str(user.id),
        metadata={"by": "administrator", "scope": "everywhere"},
    )
```

2. `:29-43` (WHY THESE HANDLERS ARE THIN … NO RESPONSE …) pasa a:

```python
WHY THESE HANDLERS ARE THIN. The rails, the tenant predicates and the audit
records are all in `service.py`, because none of them is an HTTP concern and
all of them are worth testing without a client. A handler opens the tenant
session, calls one function, and translates `UserAdminError` into the status
the service chose.

AUDIT (invariant #4). Every write records an event through `audit_service` in
the SAME transaction as the change, so the record and the change commit or
roll back together. A refused write raises out of `org_session`'s
transaction, which rolls the audit row back too -- a log saying a change
happened when it did not is worse than no log.

NO RESPONSE ON THIS SURFACE CARRIES A CREDENTIAL (invariant #3, rule 1) but
one: an invitation link, in the answer to the invite or the resend, when no
mail carried it (design §7). `tests/test_user_admin_api.py` drives every route
here -- with the mail working -- and scans the bodies.
"""
```

4. `:77-122` (`keycloak_config`, `_NOT_CONFIGURED`, `_provisioning`) se sustituyen por:

```python
def _console_url(request: Request) -> str:
    """Where an invitation link points: `ITS_PUBLIC_CONSOLE_URL`, never the
    request's Host header (host-header injection). Checked before anything is
    written, so a deployment without it creates nobody it cannot invite."""
    url = request.app.state.settings.public_console_url
    if not url:
        raise HTTPException(
            status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
            tr(
                "this installation's console address is not configured, so an invitation link "
                "cannot be made. That is a server setting, not something this screen can fix."
            ),
        )
    return str(url)


async def _mailer(session: AsyncSession, request: Request, ctx: AuthContext) -> service.Deliver:
    """The invitation mail, from the administrator who asked for it, sent in
    the request's session (Task 3: the relay credential's checkout is audited
    there, and a failed send is caught inside it, `notices.deliver`)."""
    inviter = (
        await session.execute(
            select(User.display_name, User.email).where(
                User.id == ctx.user_id, User.org_id == ctx.org_id
            )
        )
    ).one()
    name = inviter.display_name or inviter.email

    async def deliver(user: service.UserView, link: str) -> bool:
        subject, text = notices.invitation_mail(link, inviter=name)
        return await notices.deliver(
            session,
            org_id=ctx.org_id,
            to=user.email,
            subject=subject,
            text=text,
            vault=request.app.state.vault,
            actor_id=ctx.user_id,
        )

    return deliver
```

```python
) -> InvitedOut:

    valid 72 hours, to choose a password and set up their second factor.

                display_name=body.display_name,

@router.delete("/users/{user_id}/invite", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
async def cancel_invite(
    user_id: UUID,
    request: Request,
    ctx: AuthContext = Depends(_MANAGE),
) -> Response:
```

```python
async def reset_factors(

    ctx: AuthContext = Depends(_MANAGE),
) -> Response:
    """Remove this person's passkeys, authenticator app and recovery codes,
    end their sessions and forget their devices; they set up a new second
    factor at their next sign-in, and are told by mail. Needs your own second
    factor confirmed in the last ten minutes. Not for your own account."""
```

6. `claim_platform` (`:328-447`) pasa a (los comentarios de bloqueo, baseline y `setup.claimed` se conservan):

```python
@router.post("/setup/claim", response_model=ClaimedOut, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
async def claim_platform(body: SetupClaim, request: Request) -> ClaimedOut:
    """Create this installation's organization and its first administrator.

    THE ORDER OF THE REFUSALS IS PART OF THE DESIGN:

      1. the install code, before anything else -- a caller without it never
         reaches the database and never learns even the password rule;
      2. the password rule (design §2.1), before the first write;
      3. zero users, so a leaked code cannot re-claim a running platform.

    Then one transaction: the organization, the administrator (through the same
    service an invitation uses), their password, and the audit records.
    """
    settings: Settings = request.app.state.settings
    engine: AsyncEngine = request.app.state.admin_engine

    _refuse_without_the_code(body.code)
    await staff_password.require_acceptable(
        body.password, email=body.email.strip().lower(), display_name=body.display_name
    )

    async with admin_session(engine=engine) as session:
        # SERIALIZE CLAIMS. Two requests arriving together would both read zero
        # users and both create an organization; a double-clicked button is
        # exactly that. The lock is held to the end of this transaction, so the
        # second claim reads the first one's committed user and is refused.
        await session.execute(text("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('setup:claim'))"))

        if not await _no_users_yet(session):
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
                tr(
                    "this installation has already been set up. Sign in, or ask one of its "
                    "administrators to add you.",
                ),
            )

        role_id = (
            await session.execute(
                select(Role.id).where(Role.name == ORG_ADMIN, Role.org_id.is_(None))
            )
        ).scalar_one_or_none()
        if role_id is None:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE,
                tr("this installation is missing its built-in roles and cannot be set up."),
            )

        slug = _org_slug(settings, body.organization_name)
        taken = (
            await session.execute(select(Organization.id).where(Organization.slug == slug))
        ).scalar_one_or_none()
        if taken is not None:
            raise HTTPException(
                status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT,
                tr(
                    "an organization with the identifier {slug} already exists on this "
                    "installation.",
                    slug=repr(slug),
                ),
            )

        org = Organization(name=body.organization_name.strip(), slug=slug)
        session.add(org)
        await session.flush()

        # Monitoring from day one. In a SAVEPOINT: a seed that fails must not
        # fail the claim, and the worker's hourly reconcile retries it.
        await ensure_baseline_contained(session, org.id)

        try:
            # THE SAME FUNCTION AN INVITATION CALLS. Everything that makes
            # creating an account safe lives in it, and none of it is repeated
            # here: the email-domain rule, the role rails, the `user.created`
            # audit entry.
            created = await user_admin.create_user(
                session,
                org_id=org.id,
                actor_id=NO_ACTOR_YET,
                email=body.email,
                display_name=body.display_name,
                grants=[user_admin.Grant(role_id=role_id)],
                email_domain=settings.console_email_domain,
            )
        except UserAdminError as exc:
            # Raising here rolls the organization row back with it: the whole
            # point of doing both in one transaction. Every refusal left is
            # about the request (an address, a role), so it is said as it is.
            raise HTTPException(exc.status_code, exc.detail) from exc

        await staff_password.store(
            session, org_id=org.id, user_id=created.id, plain=body.password
        )
        await audit_service.record(
            session,
            org_id=org.id,
            actor_type="user",
            actor_id=created.id,
            action="auth.password_changed",
            target_type="user",
            target_id=str(created.id),
            metadata={"via": "setup"},
        )
        await audit_service.record(
            session,
            org_id=org.id,
            actor_type="system",
            actor_id=None,
            action="setup.claimed",
            target_type="organization",
            target_id=str(org.id),
            metadata={
                # NEVER THE INSTALL CODE. It is still valid for as long as this
                # transaction might roll back, and the audit log is readable by
                # every auditor in the organization afterwards.
                "organization_name": org.name,
                "organization_slug": org.slug,
                "administrator_id": str(created.id),
                "email": created.email,
            },
        )

        return ClaimedOut(
            organization_id=org.id,
            organization_slug=org.slug,
            user_id=created.id,
            email=created.email,
        )
```

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the invitation (Task 8, design §7)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def _invited(session: AsyncSession, token: str, *, consume: bool) -> User:
    """The invitee of a live, unaccepted invitation, or `invalid_link`."""
    if consume:
        row = await action_tokens.consume(session, token=token, purposes=(action_tokens.INVITE,))
    else:
        row = await action_tokens.peek(session, token=token, purposes=(action_tokens.INVITE,))
    user = await session.get(User, row.user_id) if row is not None else None
    if (
        row is None
        or user is None
        or user.kind != STAFF_KIND
        or user.status != ACTIVE_STATUS
        or await session.get(AuthPassword, user.id) is not None
    ):
        raise _invalid_link()
    return user


async def invite_details(request: Request, *, token: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The address and the name an invitation is for. Leaves the link unused."""
    org_id = action_tokens.org_of(token)
    if org_id is None:
        raise _invalid_link()
    async with _identity_session(org_id, _engine(request)) as session:
        user = await _invited(session, token, consume=False)
        return user.email, user.display_name


async def accept_invite(request: Request, *, token: str, password: str) -> SignIn:
    """The invitee's own password, and a session waiting for its first factor
    (design §2.2: the person reaches the console only after registering one).
    A refused password rolls the `consume` back: the link stays usable."""
    org_id = action_tokens.org_of(token)
    if org_id is None:
        raise _invalid_link()
    async with _identity_session(org_id, _engine(request)) as session:
        user = await _invited(session, token, consume=True)
        await staff_password.require_acceptable(
            password, email=user.email, display_name=user.display_name
        )
        await staff_password.store(session, org_id=org_id, user_id=user.id, plain=password)
        await _audit(session, user, "auth.password_changed", {"via": "invite"})
        return await _started(session, request, user, state="enroll_required")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the server's recovery link (Task 8, design §7; plan decision 10)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def _recovering(session: AsyncSession, token: str, *, consume: bool) -> User:
    """The holder of a live recovery link, still an active technician, or
    `invalid_link`."""
    purposes = (action_tokens.RECOVER,)
    if consume:
        row = await action_tokens.consume(session, token=token, purposes=purposes)
    else:
        row = await action_tokens.peek(session, token=token, purposes=purposes)
    user = await session.get(User, row.user_id) if row is not None else None
    if row is None or user is None or user.kind != STAFF_KIND or user.status != ACTIVE_STATUS:
        raise _invalid_link()
    return user


async def recovery_details(request: Request, *, token: str) -> str:
    """The address a recovery link is for. Leaves the link unused."""
    org_id = action_tokens.org_of(token)
    if org_id is None:
        raise _invalid_link()
    async with _identity_session(org_id, _engine(request)) as session:
        return (await _recovering(session, token, consume=False)).email


async def accept_recovery(request: Request, *, token: str) -> SignIn:
    """Every second factor, every remembered device and every session go; a
    session waiting for a new first factor is opened. The password stays."""
    org_id = action_tokens.org_of(token)
    if org_id is None:
        raise _invalid_link()
    async with _identity_session(org_id, _engine(request)) as session:
        user = await _recovering(session, token, consume=True)
        await clear_second_factors(session, user.id)
        await revoke_all_for_user(session, user.id)
        await end_all_for_user(session, user.id, "factors_reset")
        await _audit(session, user, "user.recovery_link_used", {"email": user.email})
        await notices.tell(session, user, "factors_reset", vault=_vault(request), actor_id=None)
        return await _started(session, request, user, state="enroll_required")
```

```python
    email, name = await flows.invite_details(request, token=body.token)
    return InviteOut(email=email, display_name=name)


@router.post(
    "/invite/accept",
    response_model=SignInOut,
    response_model_exclude_unset=True,
    dependencies=[Depends(_LINK)],
)
async def accept_invite(body: InviteAcceptIn, request: Request, response: Response) -> SignInOut:
    """Choose a password through an invitation; the first factor comes next."""
    step = await flows.accept_invite(request, token=body.token, password=body.password)
    return _answer(response, step)


@router.post("/recover/details", response_model=RecoveryOut, dependencies=[Depends(_LINK)])
async def recovery_details(body: LinkTokenIn, request: Request) -> RecoveryOut:
    """The address a recovery link is for. Leaves the link unused."""
    return RecoveryOut(email=await flows.recovery_details(request, token=body.token))


@router.post(
    "/recover/accept",
    response_model=SignInOut,
    response_model_exclude_unset=True,
    dependencies=[Depends(_LINK)],
)
async def accept_recovery(body: LinkTokenIn, request: Request, response: Response) -> SignInOut:
    """Use the server's recovery link: the second factors, remembered browsers
    and sessions go, and a new first factor is set up next."""
    step = await flows.accept_recovery(request, token=body.token)
    return _answer(response, step)
```

4. Crear `backend/app/core/auth/recover.py`:

```python
"""`python -m app.core.auth.recover --email <address>` (design §7, Q5).

For the one administrator who lost every second factor and has nobody to
reset them: it prints a one-time recovery link, valid 15 minutes, to the
console's `/recover` page. Following it removes the person's factors and
opens a session that enrols a new one (`flows.accept_recovery`); the
password does not change.

    docker compose exec api python -m app.core.auth.recover --email <address>

NOT OVER HTTP, BY CONSTRUCTION (falsifier 9): no router, no FastAPI import,
and nothing in `app/` imports this module -- whoever runs it already holds the
server (`tests/test_auth_recover_command.py`). Audited as
`user.recovery_link_issued`, actor `system`, and the holder is told by mail
(design §2.7: "toda recuperación avisa al titular").

The link on stdout and nothing else; a refusal on stderr and exit status 1.
In English: it is the server operator's terminal, like the server's own log.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import sys

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine

from app.core.audit import audit_service, load_audit_hmac_key
from app.core.auth import action_tokens, notices
from app.core.auth.lookup import find_staff
from app.core.client_scope import ClientScope
from app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
from app.core.identity import ACTIVE_STATUS
from app.core.tenancy import org_session
from app.core.vault import get_vault
from app.models import User


class RecoveryRefused(Exception):
    """Why no link was printed."""


async def issue_recovery_link(*, settings: Settings, email: str) -> str:
    if not settings.default_org_slug:
        raise RecoveryRefused(  # i18n-exempt: printed to the server operator's terminal
            "ITS_DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG is not set, so there is no organization to look in"
        )
    if not settings.public_console_url:
        raise RecoveryRefused(  # i18n-exempt: printed to the server operator's terminal
            "ITS_PUBLIC_CONSOLE_URL is not set, so no link can be made"
        )
    # The same key the API chains with, or this process's record would not verify.
    audit_service.set_hmac_key(load_audit_hmac_key(settings))
    engine = create_async_engine(settings.database_url)
    try:
        found = await find_staff(engine, org_slug=settings.default_org_slug, email=email)
        if found is None or found.status != ACTIVE_STATUS:
            raise RecoveryRefused(  # i18n-exempt: printed to the server operator's terminal
                "no active technician has that address"
            )
        async with org_session(found.org_id, engine=engine, clients=ClientScope.all()) as session:
            user = await session.get(User, found.user_id)
            if user is None:
                raise RecoveryRefused(  # i18n-exempt: printed to the server operator's terminal
                    "no active technician has that address"
                )
            token = await action_tokens.issue(
                session,
                org_id=found.org_id,
                user_id=user.id,
                purpose=action_tokens.RECOVER,
                ttl=action_tokens.RECOVER_TTL,
                created_by=None,
            )
            await audit_service.record(
                session,
                org_id=found.org_id,
                actor_type="system",
                actor_id=None,
                action="user.recovery_link_issued",
                target_type="user",
                target_id=str(user.id),
                metadata={"email": user.email, "valid_minutes": 15},
            )
            # The holder is told (design §2.7), through the same account mail
            # as the API, with this process's own vault client.
            await notices.tell(
                session, user, "recovery_link_issued", vault=get_vault(settings), actor_id=None
            )
        return action_tokens.link(settings.public_console_url, "recover", token)
    finally:
        await engine.dispose()


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python -m app.core.auth.recover",
        description="Print a one-time, 15-minute recovery link for a technician.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--email", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        link = asyncio.run(issue_recovery_link(settings=get_settings(), email=args.email))
    except RecoveryRefused as exc:
        print(f"refused: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(link)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

```python
async def test_no_lifecycle_route_reaches_another_orgs_user(users_env: Any) -> None:
    """THE CROSS-TENANT PATH, every write that addresses a user by id: the
    target is read off the TENANT-SCOPED row and nowhere else, so another
    org's id is a clean 404 and its row is untouched. Driven on the BYPASSRLS
    ADMIN ENGINE, so RLS is not what produces the refusal. `factors/reset`
    is here too: a token has no session to confirm and passes the step-up
    until Task 13, so it reaches the target read like the rest."""
    mine = await users_env.create_org("x-mine")
    theirs = await users_env.create_org("x-theirs")
    _sub, headers, _id = await _admin(users_env, mine)
    stranger = await users_env.create_user(theirs, "technician")
    stranger_id = await _user_id(users_env.admin_engine, stranger)

    users_env.app.state.app_engine = users_env.admin_engine
    try:
        attempts = {
            "disable": await users_env.client.post(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}/disable", headers=headers
            ),
            "enable": await users_env.client.post(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}/enable", headers=headers
            ),
            "invite/resend": await users_env.client.post(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}/invite/resend", headers=headers
            ),
            "invite cancel": await users_env.client.delete(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}/invite", headers=headers
            ),
            "factors/reset": await users_env.client.post(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}/factors/reset", headers=headers
            ),
            "sessions": await users_env.client.delete(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}/sessions", headers=headers
            ),
            "delete": await users_env.client.delete(
                f"/api/v1/users/{stranger_id}", headers=headers
            ),
        }
    finally:
        users_env.app.state.app_engine = users_env.app_engine

    assert {name: r.status_code for name, r in attempts.items()} == {
        name: 404 for name in attempts
    }, {name: r.text for name, r in attempts.items()}
    assert users_env.kc.seen == []
    row = await _user_row(users_env.admin_engine, stranger_id)
    assert row is not None and row.status == "active"
```

```python
async def test_the_lifecycle_needs_no_identity_provider_configuration(users_env: Any) -> None:
    """Rule 3, from the deployment's side: with no `ITS_KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_*` at all

    assert users_env.settings.keycloak_admin_url is None

        await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{victim_id}/disable", headers=headers),
        await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{victim_id}/enable", headers=headers),
        await users_env.client.delete(f"/api/v1/users/{victim_id}/sessions", headers=headers),
        await users_env.client.delete(f"/api/v1/users/{victim_id}", headers=headers),
    ]

    assert [r.status_code for r in responses] == [201, 200, 200, 204, 204]
    assert users_env.kc.seen == []


async def test_authorization_runs_before_anything_else(users_env: Any) -> None:
    """No credential, then the wrong one: 401 and 403 on every write that
    takes a user id, before the handler reads anything. Non-vacuity: an
    authorized caller DOES reach the handler, which answers 404 for an id
    that is nobody."""
    org = await users_env.create_org("dep-order")
    nobody = await users_env.create_user(org)
    unprivileged = await users_env.headers(org, nobody)
    victim = uuid4()

    async def drive(headers: dict[str, str]) -> list[int]:
        return [
            (await _invite(users_env, headers, email="a@toeshee.com")).status_code,
            (
                await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/disable", headers=headers)
            ).status_code,
            (
                await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/enable", headers=headers)
            ).status_code,
            (
                await users_env.client.post(
                    f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/invite/resend", headers=headers
                )
            ).status_code,
            (
                await users_env.client.delete(f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/invite", headers=headers)
            ).status_code,
            (
                await users_env.client.post(
                    f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/factors/reset", headers=headers
                )
            ).status_code,
            (
                await users_env.client.delete(f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/sessions", headers=headers)
            ).status_code,
            (await users_env.client.delete(f"/api/v1/users/{victim}", headers=headers)).status_code,
        ]

    assert await drive({}) == [401] * 8
    assert await drive(unprivileged) == [403] * 8
    _sub, headers, _id = await _admin(users_env, org)
    reached = await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{victim}/disable", headers=headers)
    assert reached.status_code == 404
```

```python
async def test_disable_writes_the_status_and_ends_the_persons_sessions(
    users_env: Any,
) -> None:
    """`users.status` stops the next admission; the sessions end now (design
    §2.4) -- the cookie already in the person's browser stops working."""
    org = await users_env.create_org("disable")
    _sub, headers, actor_id = await _admin(users_env, org)
    member = await signed_in(users_env, org, "technician")

    response = await users_env.client.post(
        f"/api/v1/users/{member.user_id}/disable", headers=headers
    )

    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    row = await _user_row(users_env.admin_engine, member.user_id)
    assert row is not None and row.status == "disabled"
    assert (await users_env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=member.headers())).status_code == 401
    events = [e for e in await _audit(users_env.admin_engine, org) if e.action == "user.disabled"]
    assert len(events) == 1 and events[0].actor_id == actor_id
    assert users_env.kc.seen == []


async def test_enable_restores_the_status(users_env: Any) -> None:
    org = await users_env.create_org("enable")
    _sub, headers, _id = await _admin(users_env, org)
    tech = await users_env.create_user(org, "technician")
    tech_id = await _user_id(users_env.admin_engine, tech)
    await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{tech_id}/disable", headers=headers)

    response = await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{tech_id}/enable", headers=headers)

    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
    row = await _user_row(users_env.admin_engine, tech_id)
    assert row is not None and row.status == "active"
    assert users_env.kc.seen == []


async def test_a_failure_inside_disable_rolls_the_status_back(
    users_env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """A half-applied disable -- "disabled" with live sessions, or the reverse
    -- is the worst outcome: the sessions end inside the same transaction as
    the status, so a failure there takes both down."""
    org = await users_env.create_org("disable-fail")
    _sub, headers, _id = await _admin(users_env, org)
    tech = await users_env.create_user(org, "technician")
    tech_id = await _user_id(users_env.admin_engine, tech)

    async def broken(*_args: Any, **_kwargs: Any) -> None:
        raise RuntimeError("the session store did not answer")

    monkeypatch.setattr(user_admin_service, "end_all_for_user", broken)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        await users_env.client.post(f"/api/v1/users/{tech_id}/disable", headers=headers)

    row = await _user_row(users_env.admin_engine, tech_id)
    assert row is not None and row.status == "active"
    events = await _audit(users_env.admin_engine, org)
    assert [e for e in events if e.action == "user.disabled"] == []
```

- [ ] **Step 11: `test_me_locale.py` re-apuntado**

Sustituir el archivo entero por (los tests de `set_locale_attribute` conservan sus aserciones; las del espejo pasan
a afirmar que no hay espejo):

```python
"""`PATCH /me` locale (spec 2026-10-09 §3.5, §4), and the identity-provider
write it no longer makes (P2 phase 1 Task 8; design §1.3 retires "el espejo del
idioma en Keycloak (`me.py`)").

TWO HALVES.

1. The route: the format check (unchanged), and the language staying in the
   platform. `PATCH /me` calls no identity provider whatever is configured,
   and its answer carries no `identity_locale_synced`. The sign-in pages and
   the account mails are the platform's own now and read `users.locale`.
2. `kc_client.set_locale_attribute`, which keeps no caller until phase 4
   retires `kc_client.py` with Keycloak: its read-modify-write is still held
   here, driven directly, so the function cannot rot while it exists.

WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW: `httpx.MockTransport` proves the requests the function
sends, not what a real Keycloak does with them.
"""

import copy
import json
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import httpx
import pytest
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession

from app.models import User
from app.modules.user_admin.kc_client import (
    KeycloakAdminConfig,
    KeycloakAdminError,
    set_locale_attribute,
)

_REAL_CLIENT = httpx.AsyncClient

CONFIG = KeycloakAdminConfig(
```

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# the route

async def test_es_is_stored_and_no_identity_provider_is_told(env: Any) -> None:
    response = await _patch(env, {"locale": "es"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body["locale"] == "es"
    assert "identity_locale_synced" not in body
    assert (await _row(env.api.admin_engine, env.sub)).locale == "es"
    assert env.kc.seen == []


async def test_a_regional_value_stored_earlier_stays_valid(env: Any) -> None:
    response = await _patch(env, {"locale": "en-GB"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json()["locale"] == "en-GB"
    assert env.kc.seen == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad", ["<script>", "e", "en_GB", "english-", "es es", "1234"])
async def test_a_malformed_tag_is_refused_and_writes_nothing(env: Any, bad: str) -> None:
    response = await _patch(env, {"locale": bad})
    assert response.status_code == 422
    assert (await _row(env.api.admin_engine, env.sub)).locale is None
    assert env.kc.seen == []


async def test_no_identity_shaped_field_reaches_anything(env: Any) -> None:
    other = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-00000000dead"
    for field in ("user_id", "external_subject", "sub", "keycloak_id"):
        response = await _patch(env, {"locale": "es", field: other})
        assert response.status_code == 422
    assert env.kc.seen == []


async def test_a_changed_or_cleared_language_is_kept_here_only(env: Any) -> None:
    """The cases the mirror used to treat differently -- a change, a clear,
    null over null, the same value again -- all just save."""
    await _store(env, "es")
    assert (await _patch(env, {"locale": "en"})).status_code == 200
    assert (await _patch(env, {"locale": None})).status_code == 200
    assert (await _patch(env, {"locale": None, "phone": "0101"})).status_code == 200
    assert (await _patch(env, {"locale": "es"})).status_code == 200
    assert (await _patch(env, {"locale": "es"})).status_code == 200
    assert (await _row(env.api.admin_engine, env.sub)).locale == "es"
    assert env.kc.seen == []


async def test_a_broken_provisioning_setting_cannot_touch_the_save(
    env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Was: a misconfigured secret file or an unconfigured Keycloak is skipped.
    Now nothing reads the setting at all on this route."""

    def broken(cls: Any, settings: Any) -> Any:
        raise FileNotFoundError("secret path missing")

    monkeypatch.setattr(KeycloakAdminConfig, "from_settings", classmethod(broken))
    response = await _patch(env, {"locale": "es"})
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert (await _row(env.api.admin_engine, env.sub)).locale == "es"


async def test_get_me_does_not_claim_a_sync_state(env: Any) -> None:
    response = await env.api.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=env.headers)
    assert "identity_locale_synced" not in response.json()


async def test_a_failed_client_map_read_saves_nothing_and_the_retry_saves(
    env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """`PATCH /me` answers with the client map (phase 3 design §1.3), read
    before the commit: a failed read saves nothing, so a retry is a first try.
    FALSIFIER: `update_own_profile` reading the map after its `org_session`."""
    from app.core.identity import own_profile

    real = own_profile._own_clients
    calls: list[int] = []

    async def unreachable_once(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        calls.append(1)
        if len(calls) == 1:
            raise ConnectionError("the client map could not be read")
        return await real(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(own_profile, "_own_clients", unreachable_once)

    try:
        failed = await _patch(env, {"locale": "es"})
    except ConnectionError:
        pass  # the test transport re-raises what the 500 was made of
    else:
        assert failed.status_code == 500, failed.text
    assert (await _row(env.api.admin_engine, env.sub)).locale is None

    retried = await _patch(env, {"locale": "es"})
    assert retried.status_code == 200, retried.text
    assert retried.json()["locale"] == "es"
    assert env.kc.seen == []

# kc_client.set_locale_attribute on its own (no caller until phase 4)

async def test_the_attribute_update_is_a_get_put_get_with_only_the_profile_fields(
    env: Any,
) -> None:
    before = copy.deepcopy(env.kc.user)
    await _write(env, "es")

    assert env.kc.methods == ["GET", "PUT", "GET"]
    sent = env.kc.bodies[0]
    assert set(sent) == PUT_KEYS
    for kept in ("email", "firstName", "lastName", "username"):
        assert sent[kept] == before[kept]
    assert sent["attributes"] == {"org": ["acme"], "locale": ["es"]}
    assert env.kc.user["enabled"] is True
    assert env.kc.user["requiredActions"] == []


async def test_a_concurrent_disable_is_not_undone(env: Any) -> None:
    original = env.kc.handler

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        response = original(request)
        if request.method == "GET" and len(env.kc.seen) == 1:
            env.kc.user["enabled"] = False  # the admin acts after our read
        return response

    env.kc.handler = handler  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    await _write(env, "es")
    assert env.kc.user["enabled"] is False


async def test_a_null_locale_removes_the_attribute_and_keeps_the_rest(env: Any) -> None:
    env.kc.user["attributes"]["locale"] = ["es"]
    await _write(env, None)
    sent = env.kc.bodies[0]
    assert set(sent) == PUT_KEYS
    assert sent["attributes"] == {"org": ["acme"]}


async def test_the_target_is_the_subject_given(env: Any) -> None:
    await _write(env, "es")
    assert {r.url.path.rpartition("/")[2] for r in env.kc.seen} == {env.sub}


async def test_a_write_keycloak_accepted_but_did_not_keep_raises(env: Any) -> None:
    env.kc.drop_locale = True
    with pytest.raises(KeycloakAdminError):
        await _write(env, "es")
    assert env.kc.methods == ["GET", "PUT", "GET"]


async def test_clearing_is_verified_too(env: Any) -> None:
    env.kc.user["attributes"]["locale"] = ["es"]
    original = env.kc.handler

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        response = original(request)
        if request.method == "PUT" and response.status_code < 300:
            env.kc.user["attributes"]["locale"] = ["es"]
        return response

    env.kc.handler = handler  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    with pytest.raises(KeycloakAdminError):
        await _write(env, None)


async def test_a_user_with_no_attributes_map_gets_one(env: Any) -> None:
    del env.kc.user["attributes"]
    await _write(env, "es")
    assert env.kc.bodies[0]["attributes"] == {"locale": ["es"]}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "knob",
    [
        ("put_status", 500),
        ("put_status", 403),
        ("get_status", 404),
        ("token_status", 401),
        ("raise_connect", True),
    ],
)
async def test_a_keycloak_failure_raises_and_carries_no_secret(
    env: Any, knob: tuple[str, Any]
) -> None:
    setattr(env.kc, knob[0], knob[1])
    with pytest.raises((httpx.HTTPError, KeycloakAdminError)) as caught:
        await _write(env, "es")
    for forbidden in (TOKEN, "not-a-real-secret"):
        assert forbidden not in str(caught.value)


async def test_set_locale_attribute_raises_on_a_non_object_user(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    kc = FakeKeycloak("abc")
    kc.user = ["not", "an", "object"]  # type: ignore[assignment]
    _install(monkeypatch, kc)
    with pytest.raises(KeycloakAdminError):
        await set_locale_attribute(CONFIG, user_id="abc", locale="es")
    assert kc.bodies == []
```

**Decisión del plan (1): «solo en las llamadas internas» se prueba con una extensión del scope ASGI, y
`X-ITMS-Loopback: 1` se exige además.** El diseño dice «la puerta lo admite solo en las llamadas internas» y la
interfaz nombra la cabecera. Una cabecera la puede poner cualquier cliente de red; una clave de
`scope["extensions"]` no, porque una petición de red llega por uvicorn y uvicorn no la pone. Es el mecanismo que
ya protege el canal MCP (`backend/app/core/mcp_channel.py:1-8`, `EXTENSION_KEY = "itms.mcp"`). Los ejecutores
envuelven la app en `LoopbackMarked` (añade `itms.loopback`) y envían la cabecera solo cuando el valor de
`Authorization` es un token interno. La puerta toma la rama interna si ve la cabecera; dentro de ella exige la
extensión, y cualquier fallo es 401: una petición que dice ser el asistente nunca cae al camino de la cookie o del
Bearer.

**Decisión del plan (2): el token interno solo sirve para GET y HEAD.** Todo lo que el asistente lee por la vuelta
es GET: los registros de herramientas solo admiten `ReadTool` GET (`tests/test_ai_boundaries.py:322`), la sonda de
equipo es GET (`act.py:184-191`) y los actos no llaman a ninguna ruta (`orchestrator.py:635-640`). Admitirlo en
una escritura no daría nada al asistente y sí a quien lo robara.

**Decisión del plan (3): el token interno nunca cuenta como confirmación reciente.** `verify_loopback` devuelve el
principal con `step_up_at=None` aunque la sesión tenga una confirmación de hace un minuto: las acciones de §2.5
(cambiar factores, restablecer los de otro, sacar una credencial) son de la persona, nunca del asistente. Y una
petición admitida por el token interno no acuña otro (`loopback_authorization` lo rechaza): no hay cadenas.

**Decisión del plan (4): el `kid` va en la cabecera antes de firmar.** `sign_es256` devuelve el `kid` después de
firmar, pero la cabecera firmada tiene que llevarlo. `mint_loopback` toma como primera apuesta el `kid` de la
primera clave de `keys.jwks()`, firma, y si `sign_es256` dice que firmó otra clave (una rotación entre las dos
llamadas, o un JWKS que no pone la actual primero) vuelve a firmar una vez con ese `kid`. Dos discrepancias
seguidas son un error. Así la tarea no depende del orden del JWKS. Emisor fijo `urn:itms:loopback` y
`typ: "loopback+jwt"` (RFC 8725 §3.11, *explicit typing*): el token no puede confundirse con el de MCP de la
fase 3, que firmará la misma clave con otra audiencia y otro emisor.

**Decisión del plan (5): transición (D21).** Hasta la Task 13 la puerta sigue admitiendo el Bearer de la consola, y
las pruebas existentes entran así. Una petición admitida por ese Bearer no tiene sesión; para ella
`loopback_authorization` reenvía la cabecera recibida, exactamente como hoy, y los ejecutores no la marcan. La Task
13 quita esa rama.

**Decisión del plan (6): el asistente sigue sin «token de servicio».** `executor_portal.py:36-45` prohíbe acuñar un
token de servicio para la capa de IA. El token interno no lo es: nombra a la persona y a su sesión, no lleva
permisos propios, y la ruta interna vuelve a pasar por `admit()`, `require_permission` / `require_portal_permission`
y RLS con las filas de esa persona. Los docstrings lo dicen con esas palabras.

**Decisión del plan (7): la confirmación reciente de las pruebas es un argumento de `sign_in`,
`step_up: bool = False`.** Una llamada en vez de dos en cada sitio que la necesita (la Task 13 la pide en
`ApiEnv.headers`, porque la bóveda exige la confirmación desde la Task 6), y las llamadas de las Tasks 7 y 8 no
cambian: el valor por defecto es el de hoy. `sign_in` llama a `mark_step_up` de la Task 6 en la misma transacción
que crea la sesión. `step_up=True` sin `factor_done` es un error de la prueba.

**Decisión del plan (8): un solo registro nuevo, y con `extra`.** `verify_loopback` escribe un WARNING por cada
negativa, `logger.warning("loopback token refused", extra={"reason": ...})`, con la razón fija y nunca el token:
la plantilla es constante y el valor va en `extra`, como pide `tests/test_logging_discipline.py:188-193`. Es una
llamada más en el recuento del barrido (`:524`) y en el espejo de §2.2 del diseño del kernel de logs: **+1** sobre
la base que vea esta tarea (107 en la rama hoy; el coordinador suma los deltas de cada tarea al fusionar).

**Pruebas existentes que cambian a propósito.** `tests/test_ai_act_api.py:598-620`
(`test_the_turn_context_built_for_a_confirm_redacts_its_bearer`): `_turn_context` pasa a ser `async`, porque acuñar
espera a OpenBao. La prueba pasa a `async`, su `_Request` gana `state` y sigue afirmando lo mismo (el token no
aparece en el `repr`, el plazo, el `X-Client-Id`). Ninguna otra prueba cambia en esta tarea: las que pasan
`bearer=headers["Authorization"]` siguen recibiendo un Bearer de Keycloak hasta la Task 13.

y se añaden `import httpx` (junto a `import pytest`) y `from app.models.auth import AuthSession` (después de
