```ts
// Live status: WebSocket to /api/v1/ws, events published by gateway/API.
//
// THE SESSION COOKIE IS THE CREDENTIAL (own-auth design §6.5, plan decision
// D15). The browser sends `__Host-itms_session` with this same-origin
// handshake as it does with every request; the server checks it and the
// handshake's `Origin`, and re-checks the open socket every 60 s. NO TOKEN
// TRAVELS: not in the URL, which an access log records verbatim, and no
// longer in the subprotocol list, which carried Keycloak's five-minute access
// token and made the console swap to a new socket on every renewal.
//
// 1. AFTER ANY UNPLANNED CLOSE the next open delivers `{kind: "resync"}`
//    (`RESYNC_KIND`): events may have been missed, and the page re-reads
//    what it keeps fresh from them.
// 2. A 4401 SAYS THE SESSION THE SOCKET WAS CHECKED AGAINST IS NOT THE ONE IN
//    THE COOKIE ANY MORE. Either it ended -- inactivity, the maximum, a
//    sign-out elsewhere, an administrator -- or its identifier rotated when
//    the person confirmed their second factor (design §2.4). So the console
//    asks `/me` again: a 401 there ends the session in this tab
//    (`./sessionEnd`) and no socket opens again; an answer means the cookie
//    holds a live session, and the socket reopens at once on it.
// 3. Any other unplanned close keeps the doubling backoff (2 s, 4 s ... 30 s).
// 4. THE CHOSEN CLIENT (phase 3 design §1.5) travels as `?client=<id>` -- a
//    UUID, not a credential, so the query string is the right place for it --
//    and the socket opens again when the choice changes. A 4403 on an OPEN
//    socket says the scope is no longer the one subscribed: access to that
//    client went, or a grant changed (`backend/app/api/v1/ws.py` re-checks
//    every `RECHECK_INTERVAL_S`). The console asks `/me` again, which moves
//    the top bar back to every client when the client is gone
//    (`lib/clientScope.tsx`), and reconnects at once.
//    ONE IMMEDIATE RECONNECT PER QUIET SPELL, for 4401 and 4403 alike: when
//    the socket reopened that way closes 4401 or 4403 again before it has
//    delivered anything, the next attempt backs off. A server that accepts
//    every handshake and then refuses it (an `Origin` it does not expect,
//    say) cannot make this spin; an event delivered ends the spell.
// 5. A HANDSHAKE THE SERVER REFUSES NEVER ARRIVES AS A CLOSE CODE OF ITS OWN.
//    It refuses before `accept()` -- no session, a foreign `Origin`, an
//    identity not admitted, an empty scope -- so uvicorn answers the upgrade
//    with HTTP 403, and all a browser reports is a close before open, 1006:
//    the same as a server that is down. So a socket that closes without ever
//    opening asks `/me` again ONCE, until a socket next opens -- a session or
//    a client that went while the socket was down is noticed, and an outage
//    does not become a `/me` per retry -- and backs off like any other close:
//    reconnecting at once to a handshake the server has just refused would
//    loop.
// 6. NO SOCKET WHILE THE SESSION HAS ENDED (`./sessionEnd`), and none in
//    fixture mode, which has no server to stream from.

import { useQueryClient } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useEffect, useRef, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
import { FIXTURE_MODE } from "../fixtures/mode";
import { selectedClient, subscribeClient } from "./clientChoice";
import { RESYNC_KIND } from "./resync";
import { isSessionEnded, subscribeSessionEnd } from "./sessionEnd";

export interface UiEvent {
  kind: string;
  job_id?: string;
  state?: string;
  [key: string]: unknown;
}

/** The server's close code for a session that is not (or no longer) the one the socket was checked against. */
export const CLOSE_SESSION_ENDED = 4401;
/** The server's close code for a scope that is empty, or no longer the one subscribed. */
export const CLOSE_SCOPE_REFUSED = 4403;
const INITIAL_RETRY_MS = 1000;
const MAX_RETRY_MS = 30_000;

/** The socket's address: `?client=` names the chosen client, and is absent for every client. */
export function liveUrl(client: string | null): string {
  const scheme = window.location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss" : "ws";
  const query = client === null ? "" : `?client=${encodeURIComponent(client)}`;
  return `${scheme}://${window.location.host}/api/v1/ws${query}`;
}

export function useLiveEvents(onEvent: (event: UiEvent) => void): void {
  const handler = useRef(onEvent);
  handler.current = onEvent;
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const client = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeClient, selectedClient, selectedClient);
  const ended = useSyncExternalStore(subscribeSessionEnd, isSessionEnded, isSessionEnded);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (FIXTURE_MODE || ended) return undefined;
    let disposed = false;
    // The socket whose loss is a gap.
    let current: WebSocket | null = null;
    // Sockets the server accepted. A close on one that never got here is a
    // refused (or failed) handshake, whatever the server meant (point 5).
    const accepted = new WeakSet<WebSocket>();
    // `/me` asked again for this run of closes-before-open (point 5).
    let askedMe = false;
    // Reconnected at once after a 4401 or a 4403, and nothing delivered
    // since (point 4): the next such close backs off.
    let rechecked = false;
    let retryTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
    let retryMs = INITIAL_RETRY_MS;
    // Events may have been missed: the next open says so.
    let gap = false;

    const deliver = (event: UiEvent) => handler.current(event);

    const opened = () => {
      retryMs = INITIAL_RETRY_MS;
      askedMe = false;
      if (gap) {
        gap = false;
        deliver({ kind: RESYNC_KIND });
      }
    };

    const backoff = () => {
      retryMs = Math.min(retryMs * 2, MAX_RETRY_MS);
      retryTimer = setTimeout(() => connect(), retryMs);
    };

    // A 4401 (point 2) or a 4403 (point 4) on an open socket: `/me` first,
    // then at once -- unless `/me` said the session ended.
    //
    // `disposed` IS NOT A PROMISE THAT THE FALLBACK HAS LANDED. The await
    // ends when the refetch has answered, but TanStack hands the answer to
    // its observers through `setTimeout(0)` (its `notifyManager`), so the
    // provider may not have re-rendered: `disposed` can still be false and
    // the choice still the refused client. Where the choice has already
    // moved, `connect()` sees it and opens nothing. Where it has not, the
    // socket opened here is refused or closed by this effect's cleanup once
    // the fallback lands -- a planned close, no gap and no reconnect.
    const recheck = async () => {
      await queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["me"] });
      if (disposed) return;
      if (rechecked) {
        backoff();
        return;
      }
      rechecked = true;
      connect();
    };

    const lost = (socket: WebSocket, code: number) => {
      if (disposed || socket !== current) return;
      current = null;
      gap = true;
      if (!accepted.has(socket)) {
        // Never opened (point 5): `/me` once, then the backoff.
        if (!askedMe) {
          askedMe = true;
          void queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["me"] });
        }
        backoff();
      } else if (code === CLOSE_SESSION_ENDED || code === CLOSE_SCOPE_REFUSED) void recheck();
      else backoff();
    };

    const connect = () => {
      retryTimer = null;
      // Not for a session that has ended, nor for a client the choice has
      // already left: this effect is about to stop, or to start over with
      // the new client (see `recheck`).
      if (disposed || isSessionEnded() || selectedClient() !== client) return;
      const socket = new WebSocket(liveUrl(client));
      current = socket;
      socket.onmessage = (message) => {
        if (socket !== current) return;
        rechecked = false;
        try {
          deliver(JSON.parse(message.data as string) as UiEvent);
        } catch {
          // ignore malformed frames
        }
      };
      socket.onopen = () => {
        accepted.add(socket);
        opened();
      };
      socket.onclose = (event) => lost(socket, event.code);
    };

    connect();
    return () => {
      disposed = true;
      if (retryTimer) clearTimeout(retryTimer);
      current?.close();
    };
    // A new choice is a new socket, and an ended session is none: the old
    // one is closed by this cleanup, with `disposed` set, so its close
    // schedules nothing.
  }, [client, ended, queryClient]);
}
```

2. `frontend/src/modules/remote/tunnel.ts`, entero:

```ts
/**
 * Where a screen session's live stream is. Same origin as the console.
 *
 * The URL carries NO credential: access logs record URLs verbatim, so a token
 * there would be replayable by anyone who reads a proxy log. Nor does the
 * handshake carry one any more: the session cookie is the credential, and the
 * browser sends it with this same-origin upgrade itself (own-auth design
 * §6.5; the server also checks the handshake's `Origin`). The subprotocol
 * list that carried Keycloak's access token is gone with it.
 */
export function screenUrl(sessionId: string, location: { protocol: string; host: string }): string {
  const scheme = location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss" : "ws";
  const id = encodeURIComponent(sessionId);
  return `${scheme}://${location.host}/api/v1/remote/sessions/${id}/screen`;
}
```

### Task 11: Consola — las pantallas públicas: iniciar sesión, segundo factor, primer factor, códigos, olvidé y restablecer la contraseña, aceptar la invitación

Diseño §2.1–§2.3, §2.6, §2.8, §7. Oleada 3, en paralelo con las Tasks 7 y 9. Depende de la Task 10 (su
`ApiClient`, `request()` con `anonymous`, `lib/session.ts` y `errorBody`/`apiErrorCode`) y de los contratos de las
Tasks 5, 7 y 8 (las rutas `/api/v1/auth/*`, sus cuerpos y sus negativas). Ninguna prueba habla con el backend.

Siete páginas fuera de `RequireAuth`, en `frontend/src/modules/auth/`, con su catálogo `auth` en inglés y español,
sus fixtures (harmony las recorre) y los 15 métodos nuevos de `ApiClient` (`logout` lo añadió la Task 10). Las
claves de acceso pasan por `@simplewebauthn/browser` 14.0.0, cuya API se leyó del paquete publicado:
`https://registry.npmjs.org/@simplewebauthn/browser/-/browser-14.0.0.tgz` (integridad
`sha512-1odWVqeEBTl7lJ9zMKLEsmTlnyrDO5iRcTvfMKKk1WThUnp/i8JJdffdj2icP+tty159s4PgwE3BiMoEW9NFow==`, MIT, sin

**Decisiones del plan (Task 11):**
- *Decisión del plan: el alta de la app TOTP muestra la clave de configuración y el enlace `otpauth://`, sin código QR.* La consola no trae un codificador QR y añadir una dependencia a una plataforma que es un objetivo de primer orden es una decisión de cadena de suministro que esta tarea no toma; la clave en grupos de cuatro se teclea en cualquier app, el enlace abre la app en un teléfono, y la clave de acceso se ofrece primero (§2.2). Si el coordinador quiere QR: que la Task 7 devuelva además un SVG hecho en el servidor, o una dependencia revisada.
- *Decisión del plan: «No volver a preguntar en este equipo» solo aparece si `POST /auth/login` dice cuántos días* (`remember_device_days`, entero o `null`). El Apéndice A no lo traía (ya enmendado); sin él la consola no sabe si la organización lo tiene encendido (§2.4) ni cuántos días, y sin el dato no se dibuja la casilla. **Se pide a la Task 7** añadir `remember_device_days` a la respuesta `factor_required` (de `auth_org_settings.remember_device_days`, o `null` si `remember_device_enabled` es falso). La casilla nace desmarcada siempre.
- *Decisión del plan: los métodos del segundo factor llegan en el estado del router;* abierta directamente (recarga, marcador, harmony) la página ofrece los tres. El servidor rechaza uno que la cuenta no tiene con 409 `method_unavailable` (Task 7, `_unavailable`), y la página lo dice con su frase; la contraseña ya estaba comprobada, así que no revela nada a quien no la sabe.
- *Decisión del plan: los diez códigos de recuperación pasan de una página a otra en memoria (`flow.ts`), nunca en la URL ni en el estado del router* (que es `history.state`, que el navegador guarda con el historial y puede escribir a disco). Una recarga los pierde, que es lo cierto: el servidor solo guarda su hash. La consola solo abre tras marcar «He guardado estos códigos».
- *Decisión del coordinador (sustituye a `/reset-password/:token` e `/invite/:token` del contrato inicial): el token de los enlaces va en el **fragmento*** (`/invite#<token>`, `/reset-password#<token>`; también `#token=<token>`). El navegador nunca manda el fragmento: no llega al registro de acceso de `nginx` ni al `Referer`. La página lo lee una vez, lo quita de la dirección (`useLinkToken`, con `replace`, para que tampoco quede en el historial de la pestaña) y lo manda en el cuerpo. Una recarga ya no tiene token y el servidor la trata como un enlace desconocido (410); el correo lo sigue teniendo. Sin fragmento la página pregunta igual, con un token vacío: el 410 del servidor decide, y el modo fixtures (harmony no puede añadir un fragmento: `withFixtures` pone `?__fixtures` detrás) dibuja el formulario. **No** se usa `<meta name="referrer" content="no-referrer">`: con esa política el navegador manda `Origin: null` en un POST del mismo origen y la puerta de CSRF de la Task 6 lo rechaza.
- *Decisión del plan: cada refusal dice una frase.* Un 401 o un 400 de un paso es «no se aceptó» (§2.3: la página no puede ser más precisa que el servidor); solo se distinguen `auth_required` (la sesión previa al factor se fue: empezar de nuevo) y 429 (esperar, con los segundos si llegan). Una contraseña rechazada dice su motivo (NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.1.2, «SHALL provide the reason for rejection», [S1]): la frase de `password_rejected` (`detail`, ya traducida por `tr()`), tal cual; la longitud se comprueba antes en la consola contando puntos de código (`Array.from`), como el servidor. Un 503 `sign_in_unavailable` cae en `describeSubmitError` («el servicio no está disponible»).
- *Decisión del plan: las páginas públicas no comprueban si ya hay sesión* (D19, y el modo fixtures de harmony): abrir `/sign-in` con sesión inicia sesión otra vez. Rebotar a la consola exigiría un `/me` aquí, y el modo fixtures, que siempre tiene sesión, no dejaría ver nunca la página.
- *La `SetupPage` (contraseña del dueño) y la página `/recover` son del addendum del coordinador, al final de esta tarea.*
- *Decisión del plan: `enrollTotpConfirm(code)` y `enrollPasskey(credential, name)` llevan argumentos sueltos, no un objeto*: es la firma que la Task 12 (Mi seguridad) consume.

- [ ] **Step 4: Los tipos y los métodos**

1. Crear `frontend/src/modules/auth/types.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The wire shapes of `/api/v1/auth/*` (own-auth plan, Tasks 7 and 8), as the
 * console's sign-in pages read them. The WebAuthn options and responses are
 * the W3C `*JSON` dictionaries, typed by `@simplewebauthn/browser` itself so
 * what the server sends is exactly what `startRegistration` /
 * `startAuthentication` take.
 */
import type {
  AuthenticationResponseJSON,
  PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON,
  PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON,
  RegistrationResponseJSON,
} from "@simplewebauthn/browser";

export type {
  AuthenticationResponseJSON,
  PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON,
  PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON,
  RegistrationResponseJSON,
};

/** A second factor the account can finish signing in with. The server lists them passkey first. */
export type FactorMethod = "passkey" | "totp" | "recovery";

/**
 * `POST /auth/login`. `factor_required` and `enroll_required` set a session
 * cookie that has no factor yet; `signed_in` comes only from a remembered
 * computer (design §2.6).
 *
 * `remember_device_days` is the organisation's "Remember this computer"
 * length, or `null` when it is switched off (Settings → Sessions). Absent, the
 * console offers no "remember" box -- the safe reading of a server that did
 * not say.
 */
export type LoginResult =
  | { state: "factor_required"; methods: FactorMethod[]; remember_device_days?: number | null }
  | { state: "enroll_required" }
  | { state: "signed_in" };

/** A second factor accepted: the session is complete and its identifier rotated. */
export interface SignedIn {
  state: "signed_in";
}

/** `POST /auth/enroll/totp/start`: the new secret, ONCE, as an `otpauth://` URI. */
export interface TotpEnrollment {
  otpauth_uri: string;
}

/** `POST /auth/enroll/finish` and the regeneration in Sign-in and security: ten codes, shown once. */
export interface RecoveryCodes {
  recovery_codes: string[];
}

/** `POST /auth/invite/details {token}`: who the invitation is for. */
export interface InviteDetails {
  email: string;
  display_name: string;
}
```

```diff
+
+  /** `POST /auth/factor/passkey/options`: the challenge for `startAuthentication`, untouched. */
+  factorPasskeyOptions(): Promise<PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON> {
+    return this.request<PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON>(
+      "/auth/factor/passkey/options",
+      { method: "POST" },
+      { anonymous: true },
+    );
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/factor/passkey`: the browser's answer, untouched. */
+  factorPasskey(body: { credential: AuthenticationResponseJSON; remember_device: boolean }): Promise<SignedIn> {
+    return this.request<SignedIn>("/auth/factor/passkey", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/factor/recovery`: one of the ten codes. */
+  factorRecovery(body: { code: string; remember_device: boolean }): Promise<SignedIn> {
+    return this.request<SignedIn>("/auth/factor/recovery", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/enroll/totp/start`: a new secret, once, as an `otpauth://` URI. */
+  enrollTotpStart(): Promise<TotpEnrollment> {
+    return this.request<TotpEnrollment>("/auth/enroll/totp/start", { method: "POST" }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/enroll/totp/confirm`: the first code, which proves the app holds the secret. */
+  enrollTotpConfirm(code: string): Promise<void> {
+    return this.request<void>(
+      "/auth/enroll/totp/confirm",
+      { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ code }) },
+      { anonymous: true },
+    );
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/enroll/passkey/options`: the options for `startRegistration`, untouched. */
+  enrollPasskeyOptions(): Promise<PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON> {
+    return this.request<PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON>(
+      "/auth/enroll/passkey/options",
+      { method: "POST" },
+      { anonymous: true },
+    );
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/enroll/passkey`: the new credential, and the name the person gave it. */
+  enrollPasskey(credential: RegistrationResponseJSON, name: string): Promise<void> {
+    return this.request<void>(
+      "/auth/enroll/passkey",
+      { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ credential, name }) },
+      { anonymous: true },
+    );
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/enroll/finish`: the ten recovery codes, the only time they exist in the clear. */
+  enrollFinish(): Promise<RecoveryCodes> {
+    return this.request<RecoveryCodes>("/auth/enroll/finish", { method: "POST" }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/password/forgot`: always 202, whether or not the address has an account. */
+  forgotPassword(body: { email: string }): Promise<void> {
+    return this.request<void>("/auth/password/forgot", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/password/reset`: the emailed token, in the body. */
+  resetPassword(body: { token: string; password: string }): Promise<void> {
+    return this.request<void>("/auth/password/reset", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/invite/details`: who an invitation is for. The token travels in the body. */
+  getInvite(token: string): Promise<InviteDetails> {
+    return this.request<InviteDetails>(
+      "/auth/invite/details",
+      { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ token }) },
+      { anonymous: true },
+    );
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/invite/accept`: the password; answers `{"state": "enroll_required"}` and a session that still needs a factor. */
+  acceptInvite(body: { token: string; password: string }): Promise<void> {
+    return this.request<void>("/auth/invite/accept", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
+
+  /** `POST /auth/logout-everywhere`: end every session of this person, this one included. */
+  logoutEverywhere(): Promise<void> {
+    return this.request<void>("/auth/logout-everywhere", { method: "POST" }, { anonymous: true });
+  }
```

```tsx
/**
 * The sign-in pages under a router, over a fake `ApiClient` whose every
 * method is a `vi.fn` (`calls`). Each test file mocks `lib/ApiContext` to hand
 * out `authApi()` -- `vi.mock` is hoisted per file, so it cannot live here --
 * and spies on `navigation` for the whole-document loads (`enterConsole`).
 */
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { render, type RenderResult } from "@testing-library/react";
import { MemoryRouter, Route, Routes, useLocation, type Location } from "react-router-dom";
import { vi } from "vitest";

import type { ApiClient } from "../../../lib/api";
import { EnrollPage } from "../EnrollPage";
import { FactorPage } from "../FactorPage";
import { ForgotPasswordPage } from "../ForgotPasswordPage";
import { InvitePage } from "../InvitePage";
import { RecoveryCodesPage } from "../RecoveryCodesPage";
import { ResetPasswordPage } from "../ResetPasswordPage";
import { SignInPage } from "../SignInPage";

export const calls = {
  login: vi.fn(),
  factorTotp: vi.fn(),
  factorPasskeyOptions: vi.fn(),
  factorPasskey: vi.fn(),
  factorRecovery: vi.fn(),
  enrollTotpStart: vi.fn(),
  enrollTotpConfirm: vi.fn(),
  enrollPasskeyOptions: vi.fn(),
  enrollPasskey: vi.fn(),
  enrollFinish: vi.fn(),
  forgotPassword: vi.fn(),
  resetPassword: vi.fn(),
  getInvite: vi.fn(),
  acceptInvite: vi.fn(),
};

export const TEN_CODES = [
  "7K3QD-9XM2P", "H4WTR-2N8VB", "Q6ZJC-5PF1K", "M9XED-3GH7A", "T2BVN-8KR4W",
  "C5YQP-1DJ6M", "R8HFW-4TZ2E", "N3KGA-7VX9Q", "W1PDM-6CB5T", "F7JRE-2QY8H",
];

export const OTPAUTH =
  "otpauth://totp/ITMS:dana%40example.test?secret=JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXPJBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP&issuer=ITMS";

/** Every method back to a successful answer, as the server gives it. */
export function installDefaults(): void {
  for (const fn of Object.values(calls)) fn.mockReset();
  calls.login.mockResolvedValue({ state: "factor_required", methods: ["passkey", "totp", "recovery"], remember_device_days: 15 });
  calls.factorTotp.mockResolvedValue({ state: "signed_in" });
  calls.factorPasskeyOptions.mockResolvedValue({ challenge: "c2lnbi1pbg", userVerification: "required" });
  calls.factorPasskey.mockResolvedValue({ state: "signed_in" });
  calls.factorRecovery.mockResolvedValue({ state: "signed_in" });
  calls.enrollTotpStart.mockResolvedValue({ otpauth_uri: OTPAUTH });
  calls.enrollTotpConfirm.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  calls.enrollPasskeyOptions.mockResolvedValue({ challenge: "cmVnaXN0ZXI", rp: { name: "ITMS" } });
  calls.enrollPasskey.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  calls.enrollFinish.mockResolvedValue({ recovery_codes: TEN_CODES });
  calls.forgotPassword.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  calls.resetPassword.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  calls.getInvite.mockResolvedValue({ email: "dana@example.test", display_name: "Dana Okafor" });
  calls.acceptInvite.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
}

export function authApi(): ApiClient {
  return calls as unknown as ApiClient;
}

/** Where the router is now. Set by `LocationProbe`, which renders nothing. */
export const where: { location: Location | null } = { location: null };

function LocationProbe() {
  where.location = useLocation();
  return null;
}

/** The seven pages, at `path` (fragment included), with router `state` when a step hands one over. */
export function renderAuth(path: string, state?: unknown): RenderResult {
  const url = new URL(path, "https://itms.example");
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } } });
  return render(
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[{ pathname: url.pathname, search: url.search, hash: url.hash, state }]}>
        <Routes>
          <Route path="/sign-in" element={<SignInPage />} />
          <Route path="/sign-in/factor" element={<FactorPage />} />
          <Route path="/sign-in/enroll" element={<EnrollPage />} />
          <Route path="/sign-in/recovery-codes" element={<RecoveryCodesPage />} />
          <Route path="/forgot-password" element={<ForgotPasswordPage />} />
          <Route path="/reset-password" element={<ResetPasswordPage />} />
          <Route path="/invite" element={<InvitePage />} />
          <Route path="*" element={<p data-testid="elsewhere" />} />
        </Routes>
        <LocationProbe />
      </MemoryRouter>
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in` and `/forgot-password` (own-auth design §2.1, §2.3, §2.8).
 *
 * What these hold the pages to:
 *   - the server's answer alone decides the next step, and `next` rides along;
 *   - a refusal is ONE sentence whatever the server's reason (§2.3: the page
 *     must not be more precise than the server), and the password is cleared;
 *   - a wait is said with its length, because a person can act on it;
 *   - "forgot" says the same thing whether or not the address has an account;
 *   - no request leaves twice for one double-click.
 */
import { screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ApiError } from "../../../lib/api";
import { navigation } from "../../../lib/session";
import { authApi, calls, installDefaults, renderAuth, where } from "./harness";

vi.mock("../../../lib/ApiContext", () => ({ useApi: () => authApi() }));

let replace: ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn>;

beforeEach(() => {
  installDefaults();
  replace = vi.spyOn(navigation, "replace").mockImplementation(() => {});
});

// A spy on a property that is already one is the same spy, calls and all:
// restore it, or one test's navigation answers the next test's assertion.
afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

async function signIn(email = "dana@example.test", password = "correct horse battery") {
  const user = userEvent.setup();
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Email address"), email);
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Password"), password);
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue" }));
  return user;
}

describe("signing in", () => {
  it("sends the address and password, and goes to the second factor with what the server said", async () => {
    renderAuth("/sign-in?next=%2Fdevices");
    await signIn("  dana@example.test ");

    expect(calls.login).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ email: "dana@example.test", password: "correct horse battery" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/factor"));
    expect(where.location?.search).toBe("?next=%2Fdevices");
    expect(where.location?.state).toEqual({ methods: ["passkey", "totp", "recovery"], rememberDays: 15 });
  });

  it("goes to add a first factor when the account has none", async () => {
    calls.login.mockResolvedValue({ state: "enroll_required" });
    renderAuth("/sign-in");
    await signIn();
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/enroll"));
    expect(where.location?.search).toBe("");
  });

  it("enters the console at the page asked for on a remembered computer", async () => {
    calls.login.mockResolvedValue({ state: "signed_in" });
    renderAuth("/sign-in?next=%2Fsettings%3Ftab%3Dusers");
    await signIn();
    await waitFor(() => expect(replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/settings?tab=users"));
  });

  it("never sends the person off-site, whatever next says", async () => {
    calls.login.mockResolvedValue({ state: "signed_in" });
    renderAuth("/sign-in?next=%2F%2Fevil.example");
    await signIn();
    await waitFor(() => expect(replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/"));
  });

  it("says one sentence for any refusal, and clears the password", async () => {
    calls.login.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(401, '{"code":"invalid_credentials"}'));
    renderAuth("/sign-in");
    await signIn();

    const alert = await screen.findByRole("alert");
    expect(alert).toHaveTextContent("That email address and password do not match an account here.");
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Password")).toHaveValue("");
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Email address")).toHaveValue("dana@example.test");
    expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in");
  });

  it("says how long to wait when the server asks for one", async () => {
    calls.login.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(429, '{"code":"factor_wait","wait_s":7.2}'));
    renderAuth("/sign-in");
    await signIn();
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("Too many attempts. Wait 8 seconds and try again.");
  });

  it("asks once for a double-click", async () => {
    let answer: (value: unknown) => void = () => {};
    calls.login.mockReturnValue(new Promise((resolve) => (answer = resolve)));
    renderAuth("/sign-in");
    const user = await signIn();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Working…" }));
    answer({ state: "enroll_required" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/enroll"));
    expect(calls.login).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  it("offers the password link, carrying next", async () => {
    renderAuth("/sign-in?next=%2Fdevices");
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Forgot your password?" })).toHaveAttribute(
      "href",
      "/forgot-password?next=%2Fdevices",
    );
  });

  it("asks for nothing when the page opens: no /me, no session check", () => {
    renderAuth("/sign-in");
    for (const fn of Object.values(calls)) expect(fn).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});

describe("forgetting the password", () => {
  it("says the same thing whether or not the address has an account", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/forgot-password");
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Email address"), "nobody@example.test");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send the link" }));

    expect(calls.forgotPassword).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ email: "nobody@example.test" });
    expect(await screen.findByRole("status")).toHaveTextContent(
      /If that address belongs to an account here, a link is on its way\. It works once, for 30 minutes\./,
    );
    expect(screen.getByRole("status")).toHaveTextContent(/second factor is still asked for/);
  });

  it("says a wait when the server asks for one", async () => {
    calls.forgotPassword.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(429, ""));
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/forgot-password");
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Email address"), "dana@example.test");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Send the link" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.");
  });
});
```

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in/factor` (own-auth design §2.2, §2.3, §2.6).
 *
 * The passkey goes through `@simplewebauthn/browser`, mocked at its own
 * boundary so `../passkey.ts` runs for real: the options the server sent
 * reach `startAuthentication` untouched, and its answer reaches the server
 * untouched -- the console adds nothing to a ceremony the server verifies.
 */
import { screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ApiError } from "../../../lib/api";
import { navigation } from "../../../lib/session";

vi.mock("../../../lib/ApiContext", () => ({ useApi: () => authApi() }));

const webauthn = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  supported: true,
  startAuthentication: vi.fn(),
  startRegistration: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock("@simplewebauthn/browser", async (importOriginal) => ({
  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import("@simplewebauthn/browser")>()),
  browserSupportsWebAuthn: () => webauthn.supported,
  startAuthentication: (options: unknown) => webauthn.startAuthentication(options),
  startRegistration: (options: unknown) => webauthn.startRegistration(options),
}));

const { WebAuthnError } = await import("@simplewebauthn/browser");

const ASSERTION = { id: "Y3JlZA", rawId: "Y3JlZA", type: "public-key", response: {}, clientExtensionResults: {} };
const EVERY = { methods: ["passkey", "totp", "recovery"], rememberDays: 15 };

let replace: ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn>;

beforeEach(() => {

  webauthn.supported = true;
  webauthn.startAuthentication.mockReset().mockResolvedValue(ASSERTION);

});

// A spy on a property that is already one is the same spy, calls and all:
// restore it, or one test's navigation answers the next test's assertion.
afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

describe("the second factor", () => {
  it("offers the passkey first, then the app, with the recovery code folded away", () => {
    renderAuth("/sign-in/factor", EVERY);
    const headings = screen.getAllByRole("heading", { level: 2 }).map((h) => h.textContent);
    expect(headings).toEqual(["Passkey", "Authenticator app"]);

    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("Recovery code")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("passes the server's options to the browser untouched, and the browser's answer back", async () => {
```

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in/enroll` and `/sign-in/recovery-codes` (own-auth design §2.2).
 *
 * THE RECOVERY CODES NEVER TOUCH THE URL OR THE ROUTER'S STATE. Router state
 * is `history.state`, which a browser keeps with the tab's history and may
 * write to disk; the codes are handed over in memory (`../flow.ts`). The test
 * that asserts it reads the location the codes page was reached with.
 */

vi.mock("../../../lib/ApiContext", () => ({ useApi: () => authApi() }));

const webauthn = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  supported: true,
  startAuthentication: vi.fn(),
  startRegistration: vi.fn(),
}));

vi.mock("@simplewebauthn/browser", async (importOriginal) => ({
  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import("@simplewebauthn/browser")>()),
  browserSupportsWebAuthn: () => webauthn.supported,
  startAuthentication: (options: unknown) => webauthn.startAuthentication(options),
  startRegistration: (options: unknown) => webauthn.startRegistration(options),
}));

const { WebAuthnError } = await import("@simplewebauthn/browser");

const ATTESTATION = { id: "bmV3", rawId: "bmV3", type: "public-key", response: {}, clientExtensionResults: {} };

let replace: ReturnType<typeof vi.spyOn>;

beforeEach(() => {
  installDefaults();
  forgetCodes();
  webauthn.supported = true;
  webauthn.startRegistration.mockReset().mockResolvedValue(ATTESTATION);
  replace = vi.spyOn(navigation, "replace").mockImplementation(() => {});
});

// A spy on a property that is already one is the same spy, calls and all:
// restore it, or one test's navigation answers the next test's assertion.
afterEach(() => {
  vi.restoreAllMocks();
});

describe("adding the first second factor", () => {
  it("makes a passkey from the server's options, names it, and shows the recovery codes", async () => {
    const options = { challenge: "cmVnaXN0ZXI", rp: { name: "ITMS" }, excludeCredentials: [] };
    calls.enrollPasskeyOptions.mockResolvedValue(options);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/sign-in/enroll?next=%2Fdevices");

    const name = screen.getByLabelText("Name for this passkey");
    expect(name).toHaveValue("My passkey");
    await user.clear(name);
    await user.type(name, "Work laptop");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Create a passkey" }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/recovery-codes"));
    expect(webauthn.startRegistration).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ optionsJSON: options });
    expect(calls.enrollPasskey).toHaveBeenCalledWith(ATTESTATION, "Work laptop");
    expect(calls.enrollFinish).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(where.location?.search).toBe("?next=%2Fdevices");
    // NOT in the URL, NOT in history.state.
    expect(where.location?.state ?? null).toBeNull();
    expect(JSON.stringify(where.location)).not.toContain(TEN_CODES[0]);
    for (const code of TEN_CODES) expect(screen.getByText(code)).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("sets up an authenticator app from its setup key, and confirms it with a code", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/sign-in/enroll");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Set up an authenticator app" }));

    expect(await screen.findByText("JBSW Y3DP EHPK 3PXP JBSW Y3DP EHPK 3PXP")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Open in an authenticator app" })).toHaveAttribute("href", OTPAUTH);
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("Six-digit code the app now shows"), "654 321");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Confirm code" }));

    await waitFor(() => expect(calls.enrollTotpConfirm).toHaveBeenCalledWith("654321"));
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/recovery-codes"));
  });

  it("says a refused code in one sentence, clears it, and keeps the key on screen", async () => {
    calls.enrollTotpConfirm.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(400, '{"code":"factor_failed"}'));
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/sign-in/enroll");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Set up an authenticator app" }));
    await user.type(await screen.findByLabelText("Six-digit code the app now shows"), "111111");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Confirm code" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/That code was not accepted/);
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Six-digit code the app now shows")).toHaveValue("");
    expect(calls.enrollFinish).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("says when this device already holds a passkey for the account", async () => {
    webauthn.startRegistration.mockRejectedValue(
      new WebAuthnError({
        message: "The authenticator was previously registered",
        code: "ERROR_AUTHENTICATOR_PREVIOUSLY_REGISTERED",
        cause: Object.assign(new Error("invalid state"), { name: "InvalidStateError" }),
      }),
    );
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/sign-in/enroll");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Create a passkey" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("This device already holds a passkey for your account.");
    expect(calls.enrollPasskey).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("offers the app alone, and says why, where the browser cannot make a passkey", () => {
    webauthn.supported = false;
    renderAuth("/sign-in/enroll");
    expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: "Create a passkey" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText(/This browser cannot use passkeys/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Set up an authenticator app" })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

describe("the recovery codes", () => {
  it("open the console only once the person says they saved them", async () => {
    handOverCodes(TEN_CODES);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/sign-in/recovery-codes?next=%2Fdevices");
    const list = screen.getByRole("list", { name: "Your recovery codes" });
    expect(within(list).getAllByRole("listitem")).toHaveLength(10);

    const go = screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Continue to the console" });
    expect(go).toBeDisabled();
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "I have saved these codes somewhere safe" }));
    await user.click(go);
    expect(replace).toHaveBeenCalledWith("/devices");
  });

  it("copies them, and says so; and says so when the browser refuses", async () => {
    handOverCodes(TEN_CODES);
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const writeText = vi.spyOn(navigator.clipboard, "writeText").mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    renderAuth("/sign-in/recovery-codes");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Copy the codes" }));
    expect(writeText).toHaveBeenCalledWith(TEN_CODES.join("\n"));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("status")).toHaveTextContent("The codes are on the clipboard.");

    writeText.mockRejectedValue(new Error("denied"));
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Copy the codes" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/would not copy them/);
  });

  it("are not there to show again on a page opened directly", () => {
    renderAuth("/sign-in/recovery-codes");
    expect(screen.getByText(/There are no codes to show/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.queryByRole("list")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("are dropped from memory once their page is gone", () => {
    handOverCodes(TEN_CODES);
    const { unmount } = renderAuth("/sign-in/recovery-codes");
    unmount();
    renderAuth("/sign-in/recovery-codes");
    expect(screen.getByText(/There are no codes to show/)).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

5. `frontend/src/modules/auth/__tests__/links.test.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * The two emailed links: `/reset-password#<token>` (own-auth design §2.8) and
 * `/invite#<token>` (§7).
 *
 * THE TOKEN IS IN THE FRAGMENT, which a browser never sends: it reaches no
 * access log and no `Referer`. The page reads it, takes it off the address,
 * and sends it in a request body -- never in a URL of its own.
 *
 * A REJECTED PASSWORD STATES ITS REASON (NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.1.2: the
 * verifier "SHALL provide the reason for rejection", [S1]): the server's
 * `password_rejected` carries the sentence in `detail`, shown as sent.
 */
import { screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ApiError } from "../../../lib/api";
import { authApi, calls, installDefaults, renderAuth, where } from "./harness";

vi.mock("../../../lib/ApiContext", () => ({ useApi: () => authApi() }));

const GOOD = "a long phrase I can remember";

beforeEach(() => {
  installDefaults();
});

async function choose(password: string, again = password) {
  const user = userEvent.setup();
  await user.type(await screen.findByLabelText("New password"), password);
  await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("The same password again"), again);
  return user;
}

describe("resetting the password from the emailed link", () => {
  it("sends the token from the fragment with the new password, and says the second factor still follows", async () => {
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok-reset-1");
    const user = await choose(GOOD);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));

    expect(calls.resetPassword).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ token: "tok-reset-1", password: GOOD });
    expect(await screen.findByRole("status")).toHaveTextContent(/your second factor is still asked for/);
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Sign in" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "/sign-in");
  });

  it.each([
    ["short", "eleven char", "Use at least 12 characters."],
    ["long", "x".repeat(129), "Use at most 128 characters."],
  ])("refuses a %s password before asking, counting characters as a person does", async (_, password, sentence) => {
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok");
    const user = await choose(password);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(sentence);
    expect(calls.resetPassword).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("counts each character once, emoji included: eleven are too few, twelve are enough", async () => {
    // A key emoji is two UTF-16 units: `.length` would call eleven of them 22.
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok");
    const eleven = "🔑".repeat(11);
    const user = await choose(eleven);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("Use at least 12 characters.");
    expect(calls.resetPassword).not.toHaveBeenCalled();

    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("New password"), "🔑");
    await user.type(screen.getByLabelText("The same password again"), "🔑");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    const twelve = "🔑".repeat(12);
    await waitFor(() => expect(calls.resetPassword).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ token: "tok", password: twelve }));
  });

  it("refuses two passwords that differ", async () => {
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok");
    const user = await choose(GOOD, `${GOOD}!`);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("The two passwords are not the same.");
    expect(calls.resetPassword).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it.each([400, 422])("shows the server's sentence for a refused password (%i password_rejected)", async (status) => {
    const sentence = "That password is on the list of passwords already exposed in breaches.";
    calls.resetPassword.mockRejectedValue(
      new ApiError(status, JSON.stringify({ code: "password_rejected", detail: sentence })),
    );
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok");
    const user = await choose(GOOD);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(sentence);
    // A refused password is not a dead link: the form stays.
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("New password")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("takes the token off the address once it has read it", async () => {
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok-reset-1");
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.hash).toBe(""));
    expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/reset-password");
    const user = await choose(GOOD);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    expect(calls.resetPassword).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ token: "tok-reset-1", password: GOOD });
  });

  it("says a link the server no longer honours is dead, and offers a new one", async () => {
    calls.resetPassword.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(410, '{"code":"invalid_link"}'));
    renderAuth("/reset-password#tok");
    const user = await choose(GOOD);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("This link has expired or was already used.");
    expect(screen.getByRole("link", { name: "Ask for a new link" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "/forgot-password");
  });
});

describe("accepting an invitation", () => {
  it("names who it is for, and goes on to the first factor once a password is chosen", async () => {
    renderAuth("/invite#tok-invite-1");
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { name: "Welcome, Dana Okafor" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(calls.getInvite).toHaveBeenCalledWith("tok-invite-1");
    expect(screen.getByText("dana@example.test", { selector: "b" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByLabelText("Email address")).toHaveValue("dana@example.test");

    const user = await choose(GOOD);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Set password and continue" }));

    expect(calls.acceptInvite).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ token: "tok-invite-1", password: GOOD });
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/enroll"));
  });

  it("says an expired, used or cancelled invitation for what it is", async () => {
    calls.getInvite.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(410, '{"code":"invalid_link"}'));
    renderAuth("/invite#tok-gone");
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/This invitation has expired, was already used, or was cancelled/);
    expect(screen.queryByLabelText("New password")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("says the server's reason when the password is refused, and stays", async () => {
    const sentence = "That password contains your email address.";
    calls.acceptInvite.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(400, JSON.stringify({ code: "password_rejected", detail: sentence })));
    renderAuth("/invite#tok");
    const user = await choose(GOOD);
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Set password and continue" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(sentence);
    expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/invite");
  });

  it("asks with an empty token when the link lost its fragment, and the server's 410 decides", async () => {
    calls.getInvite.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(410, '{"code":"invalid_link"}'));
    renderAuth("/invite");
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/This invitation has expired/);
    expect(calls.getInvite).toHaveBeenCalledWith("");
  });
});
```

6. `frontend/src/modules/auth/__tests__/routes.test.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The pages reached without a session, as `App.tsx` mounts them (own-auth
 * Task 11).
 *
 * THREE LISTS MUST AGREE, AND NONE CAN SEE THE OTHERS:
 *   - `App.tsx`'s routes for these pages, which must sit OUTSIDE
 *     `RequireAuth` -- inside it, a person with no session would be sent to
 *     sign in from the page where they sign in;
 *   - `lib/session.ts::PUBLIC_PATHS`, which keeps `goToSignIn` from starting
 *     a navigation from one of them (plan decision D20) and refuses them as a
 *     `?next=`;
 *   - `scripts/routes.mjs`, which the harmony gate walks.
 * And each must start with a prefix the edge sends to the console, not to the
 * api (plan decision D19).
 */
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { resolve } from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

import { ROUTES, fillPath } from "../../../../scripts/routes.mjs";
import { PUBLIC_PATHS, isPublicPath } from "../../../lib/session";

const APP = readFileSync(resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../../../App.tsx"), "utf8");

/** Every `path="..."` App.tsx mounts (the pattern `routes-covered.test.ts` reads). */
function allPaths(): string[] {
  return [...APP.matchAll(/<Route\b[^>]*?\bpath="([^"]+)"/gs)].map((match) => match[1] as string);
}

/** `path -> element source` for every `<Route>` App.tsx declares on one line. */
function oneLineRoutes(): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    [...APP.matchAll(/<Route\s+path="([^"]+)"\s+element=\{(.*?)\}\s*\/>/g)].map(
      (match) => [match[1] as string, match[2] as string] as const,
    ),
  );
}

const PAGES = [
  "/sign-in",
  "/sign-in/factor",
  "/sign-in/enroll",
  "/sign-in/recovery-codes",
  "/forgot-password",
  "/reset-password",
  "/invite",
];

describe("the pages reached without a session", () => {
  it("are mounted, each outside RequireAuth", () => {
    const mounted = oneLineRoutes();
    for (const page of PAGES) {
      expect(mounted.has(page), `${page} is not a one-line <Route> in App.tsx`).toBe(true);
      expect(mounted.get(page)).not.toContain("RequireAuth");
    }
  });

  it("are exactly the public paths, and every other route is not one", () => {
    for (const page of PAGES) expect(isPublicPath(page), page).toBe(true);
    const paths = allPaths();
    expect(paths.length).toBeGreaterThan(50);
    for (const path of paths) {
      if (!PAGES.includes(path) && path !== "*") expect(isPublicPath(path), path).toBe(false);
    }
    expect(new Set(PAGES.map((page) => `/${page.split("/")[1]}`))).toEqual(new Set(PUBLIC_PATHS));
  });

  it("are walked by the harmony gate", () => {
    for (const page of PAGES) expect(ROUTES).toContain(fillPath(page));
  });

  it("start with no prefix the edge sends to the api", () => {
    for (const page of PAGES) {
      expect(page).not.toMatch(/^\/(api|enroll|i|mcp|\.well-known|realms|resources|js)(\/|$)/);
    }
  });
});
```

4. `frontend/src/modules/auth/errors.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * What a refused sign-in step says (own-auth design §2.1, §2.3), from the
 * refusals of own-auth Tasks 6–8:
 *
 *   401 `invalid_credentials`   the first step: wrong address or password
 *   401 `factor_failed`         a second factor at sign-in not accepted
 *   400 `factor_failed`         a first factor (enrolment) not accepted
 *   401 `auth_required`         the pre-factor session is gone (the door)
 *   429 `factor_wait`           wait; `wait_s` in the body (and `Retry-After`)
 *   410 `invalid_link`          an emailed or server-made link used, expired or unknown
 *   `password_rejected`         a new password refused; `detail` says why
 *   503 `sign_in_unavailable`   the server cannot sign anyone in right now
 *
 * GENERIC ON PURPOSE. The server answers a wrong password the same whether or
 * not the account exists, and a wrong code the same whatever was wrong with
 * it; the page must not be more precise than the server is. So a 401 or a 400
 * from a step is the step's one "not accepted" sentence, and only two things
 * are told apart: a pre-factor session that is gone, which can only be started
 * again, and a wait, which a person can do something about.
 *
 * A REJECTED PASSWORD STATES ITS REASON. NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.1.2: the
 * verifier "SHALL provide the reason for rejection" ([S1]). The server words
 * it (`detail`, translated by `tr()`); this page shows it as sent. The length
 * is also checked here first, in code points as the server counts it, so the
 * commonest refusal costs no round trip.
 *
 * Bodies are read from `ApiError.message`, which `ApiClient` fills with the
 * server's text on these routes (`request()`'s `anonymous`), through
 * `lib/api.ts::errorBody`.
 */
import { describeSubmitError } from "../../components/form";
import { translate, type MessageKey } from "../../i18n/core";
import { ApiError, apiErrorCode, errorBody } from "../../lib/api";

/** How long the server asked to wait, in whole seconds, when it said. */
export function waitSeconds(error: unknown): number | null {
  const wait = errorBody(error).wait_s;
  return typeof wait === "number" && Number.isFinite(wait) && wait > 0 ? Math.ceil(wait) : null;
}

/** The server's sentence for a refused new password (`password_rejected`), when it sent one. */
export function passwordRefusal(error: unknown): string | null {
  if (apiErrorCode(error) !== "password_rejected") return null;
  const detail = errorBody(error).detail;
  return typeof detail === "string" && detail.trim() !== "" ? detail : null;
}

/**
 * The sentence for a refused step. `rejected` is the step's own "not
 * accepted", for a 401 or a 400; without one those fall to the server's own
 * words. `canTimeOut` is false where there is no pre-factor session to lose
 * (the first step, the emailed links).
 */
export function describeAuthError(
  error: unknown,
  { rejected, canTimeOut = true }: { rejected?: MessageKey; canTimeOut?: boolean } = {},
): string {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) {
    if (error.status === 429) {
      const seconds = waitSeconds(error);
      return seconds === null ? translate("auth.common.tooMany") : translate("auth.common.wait", { count: seconds });
    }
    const refusal = passwordRefusal(error);
    if (refusal) return refusal;
    if (error.status === 401 && canTimeOut && apiErrorCode(error) === "auth_required") {
      return translate("auth.common.timedOut");
    }
    if (rejected && (error.status === 401 || error.status === 400)) return translate(rejected);
  }
  return describeSubmitError(error);
}

/** A link the server no longer honours: used, expired or unknown (410 `invalid_link`). */
export function isDeadLink(error: unknown): boolean {
  return error instanceof ApiError && (error.status === 410 || apiErrorCode(error) === "invalid_link");
}

/** The new-password checks the console can make before asking (length in code points, design §2.1). */
export function checkNewPassword(password: string, again: string): string | null {
  const length = Array.from(password).length;
  if (length < 12) return translate("auth.password.too_short");
  if (length > 128) return translate("auth.password.too_long");
  if (password !== again) return translate("auth.password.mismatch");
  return null;
}
```

5. `frontend/src/modules/auth/flow.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * What the sign-in steps hand each other (own-auth Task 11).
 *
 * `?next=` travels from step to step in the URL -- it is a page, not a
 * secret -- and is filtered by `lib/session.ts::safeNext` wherever it is used.
 *
 * THE TOKEN OF AN EMAILED OR SERVER-MADE LINK TRAVELS IN THE FRAGMENT
 * (`/invite#<token>`, `/reset-password#<token>`, `/recover#<token>`), which a
 * browser never sends: it reaches no access log and no `Referer`. The page
 * reads it once, takes it off the address (`useLinkToken`) so it does not sit
 * in the tab's history either, and sends it in a request body.
 *
 * THE RECOVERY CODES DO NOT TRAVEL IN THE URL OR IN THE ROUTER'S STATE. Router
 * state is `history.state`, which a browser keeps with the session's history
 * and may write to disk to restore tabs; ten single-use codes that each sign
 * the person in do not belong there, any more than a token in
 * `sessionStorage` did (design §1.2, [S6]). They are handed from the step
 * that made them to the page that shows them in this module's memory, which a
 * reload or a sign-in empties.
 */
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { useLocation, useNavigate, useSearchParams } from "react-router-dom";

import { DEFAULT_AFTER_SIGN_IN, safeNext } from "../../lib/session";

/** The raw `?next=` of the current step, filtered where it is used. */
export function useNext(): string | null {
  const [params] = useSearchParams();
  return params.get("next");
}

/** `path`, carrying `next` on to the following step when there is somewhere to go back to. */
export function carryNext(path: string, next: string | null): string {
  const back = safeNext(next);
  return back === DEFAULT_AFTER_SIGN_IN ? path : `${path}?next=${encodeURIComponent(back)}`;
}

/** The token in a link's fragment: `#<token>`, or `#token=<token>`. Empty when there is none. */
export function tokenFromHash(hash: string): string {
  const raw = hash.startsWith("#") ? hash.slice(1) : hash;
  if (raw.includes("=")) return new URLSearchParams(raw).get("token") ?? "";
  try {
    return decodeURIComponent(raw);
  } catch {
    return raw;
  }
}

/**
 * The link's token, read once from the fragment, which then leaves the
 * address (`replace`, so Back does not bring it back). A reload therefore
 * finds no token, and the server answers that link as it would any unknown
 * one; the email still holds it.
 */
export function useLinkToken(): string {
  const location = useLocation();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const [token] = useState(() => tokenFromHash(location.hash));
  useEffect(() => {
    if (location.hash) navigate({ pathname: location.pathname, search: location.search }, { replace: true });
  }, [location.hash, location.pathname, location.search, navigate]);
  return token;
}

/** A six-digit code as typed: spaces and dashes a phone app shows between the halves dropped. */
export function digitsOf(code: string): string {
  return code.replace(/[\s-]/g, "");
}

/**
 * A recovery code as typed, in the form it was shown (`XXXXX-XXXXX`, own-auth
 * Task 4): upper case, with the dash where it belongs whether or not the
 * person typed it. Anything that is not ten characters is sent as typed and
 * the server refuses it like any other wrong code.
 */
export function recoveryCodeOf(code: string): string {
  const compact = code.toUpperCase().replace(/[\s-]/g, "");
  return compact.length === 10 ? `${compact.slice(0, 5)}-${compact.slice(5)}` : code.trim();
}

/** The setup key inside an `otpauth://` URI, in groups of four for typing, or `null`. */
export function setupKeyOf(otpauthUri: string): string | null {
  try {
    const secret = new URL(otpauthUri).searchParams.get("secret");
    return secret ? secret.replace(/(.{4})(?=.)/g, "$1 ") : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

let handed: readonly string[] = [];

/** From the step that made the recovery codes to the page that shows them. */
export function handOverCodes(codes: readonly string[]): void {
  handed = [...codes];
}

/** The codes handed over, if any. Reading does not clear them: React may render twice. */
export function heldCodes(): readonly string[] {
  return handed;
}

/** Drop the codes, once the page that showed them is gone. */
export function forgetCodes(): void {
  handed = [];
}
```

6. `frontend/src/modules/auth/passkey.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The browser half of a passkey (own-auth design §2.2), through
 * `@simplewebauthn/browser` 14.0.0.
 *
 * THE LIBRARY'S CONTRACT, READ FROM ITS PUBLISHED PACKAGE
 * (https://registry.npmjs.org/@simplewebauthn/browser/-/browser-14.0.0.tgz,
 * `esm/methods/startRegistration.d.ts`, `startAuthentication.d.ts`):
 *
 *   startRegistration({ optionsJSON: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON })
 *     -> Promise<RegistrationResponseJSON>
 *   startAuthentication({ optionsJSON: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON })
 *     -> Promise<AuthenticationResponseJSON>
 *
 * Both are the W3C `*JSON` dictionaries, base64url for every byte string,
 * which is what py_webauthn's `options_to_json` sends and
 * `verify_registration_response` / `verify_authentication_response` accept
 * (own-auth Task 5). The options come from the server whole -- the challenge,
 * `userVerification: "required"`, the credentials to exclude -- and this file
 * adds nothing to them: what the authenticator is asked for is the server's
 * decision, and the server checks the answer (design §2.2; the console
 * protects nothing, invariant 6).
 *
 * A refusal arrives as the library's `WebAuthnError`, whose `name` is the
 * browser's (`NotAllowedError` when the person closed the prompt or it timed
 * out) and whose `code` names the case (`webAuthnError.d.ts`).
 */
import {
  WebAuthnError,
  browserSupportsWebAuthn,
  startAuthentication,
  startRegistration,
} from "@simplewebauthn/browser";

import { translate } from "../../i18n/core";
import type {
  AuthenticationResponseJSON,
  PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON,
  PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON,
  RegistrationResponseJSON,
} from "./types";

/** Whether this browser can make or use a passkey at all; the passkey option is not offered when not. */
export function canUsePasskeys(): boolean {
  return browserSupportsWebAuthn();
}

/** Make a passkey from the server's registration options. */
export function createPasskey(optionsJSON: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON): Promise<RegistrationResponseJSON> {
  return startRegistration({ optionsJSON });
}

/** Sign the server's challenge with a passkey. */
export function signWithPasskey(optionsJSON: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON): Promise<AuthenticationResponseJSON> {
  return startAuthentication({ optionsJSON });
}

/** The sentence for a passkey the browser refused, or `null` when the refusal was not the browser's. */
export function describePasskeyError(error: unknown): string | null {
  if (error instanceof WebAuthnError) {
    if (error.code === "ERROR_AUTHENTICATOR_PREVIOUSLY_REGISTERED") return translate("auth.passkey.alreadyRegistered");
    if (error.name === "NotAllowedError" || error.code === "ERROR_CEREMONY_ABORTED") {
      return translate("auth.passkey.cancelled");
    }
  }
  if (error instanceof Error && error.name === "NotAllowedError") return translate("auth.passkey.cancelled");
  if (error instanceof Error && /not supported in this browser/i.test(error.message)) {
    return translate("auth.passkey.unsupported");
  }
  return null;
}
```

7. `frontend/src/modules/auth/AuthCard.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * The ground every page reached without a session stands on (own-auth Task
 * 11): one card on the page ground, the page-title rung for its headline,
 * and a language switch -- the same composition as the first-boot screen
 * (`modules/setup/SetupPage.tsx`), because v3 draws no sign-in screen and
 * these, like that one, are built from the kit alone.
 *
 * OUTSIDE THE SHELL, AND IT MUST BE: the shell asks `/me` for a session these
 * pages exist to create. So the card is the page's `<main>` landmark, with
 * its one `<h1>`, and every colour and size is a token (the harmony gate
 * walks these routes).
 *
 * THE LANGUAGE SWITCH IS HERE because nothing else on these pages can change
 * it, and a person who chose Spanish on another computer has no saved
 * language this browser knows of yet. The choice is kept in this browser
 * (`itms.lang`); it is not saved to an account, because there is no session
 * to save it with (`App.tsx`'s `LanguageBridge`, plan decision D20).
 */
import { useId, type CSSProperties, type ReactNode } from "react";

import { useLanguage, useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { LANGUAGES } from "../../i18n/types";
import { Btn, KIND_ICON } from "../../shell/components";
import { Icon } from "../../shell/icons";

const GROUND: CSSProperties = {
  minHeight: "100vh",
  display: "flex",
  alignItems: "center",
  justifyContent: "center",
  background: "var(--bg)",
  padding: 16,
};
const CARD: CSSProperties = { width: "100%", maxWidth: 480, padding: 32, margin: 0 };
/** The page-title rung (`.ph h1`), on a screen that has no `.ph`. */
const HEADLINE: CSSProperties = { fontSize: "var(--t-h1)", fontWeight: 600, letterSpacing: "-.015em", margin: 0 };
/** The panel-title rung (`.panel-h h2`), for one choice inside the card. */
const SECTION_HEADING: CSSProperties = { fontSize: "var(--t-h2)", fontWeight: 600, margin: 0 };

export function AuthCard({ title, intro, children }: { title: string; intro?: ReactNode; children: ReactNode }) {
  const t = useT();
  const { language, setLanguage } = useLanguage();
  return (
    <main style={GROUND}>
      <div className="panel" style={CARD}>
        <h1 style={HEADLINE}>{title}</h1>
        {intro ? (
          <p className="note" style={{ marginTop: 6 }}>
            {intro}
          </p>
        ) : null}
        <div style={{ marginTop: 20, display: "grid", gap: 16 }}>{children}</div>
        <div role="group" aria-label={t("common.language.label")} style={{ marginTop: 24, display: "flex", gap: 8 }}>
          {LANGUAGES.map((option) => (
            <Btn
              key={option}
              small
              variant="ghost"
              label={option === "es" ? t("common.language.spanish") : t("common.language.english")}
              pressed={language === option}
              onClick={() => setLanguage(option)}
            />
          ))}
        </div>
      </div>
    </main>
  );
}

/** A refusal or a failure, announced: these pages change under a person who just pressed a button. */
export function AuthAlert({ text }: { text: string | null }) {
  if (!text) return null;
  return (
    <p role="alert" className="notice red">
      <Icon name={KIND_ICON.crit} size={16} />
      <span>{text}</span>
    </p>
  );
}

/** Something that happened as asked, said once, politely. */
export function AuthDone({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <p role="status" className="notice">
      <Icon name={KIND_ICON.ok} size={16} />
      <span>{children}</span>
    </p>
  );
}

/** One way through a step (a passkey, an app, a recovery code), named by its own heading. */
export function AuthSection({ title, hint, children }: { title: string; hint?: string; children: ReactNode }) {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <section aria-labelledby={id} style={{ display: "grid", gap: 10 }}>
      <h2 id={id} style={SECTION_HEADING}>
        {title}
      </h2>
      {hint ? (
        <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          {hint}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {children}
    </section>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * A new password, twice (own-auth design §2.1): at least 12 characters,
 * at most 128, each code point counting as one; any characters, spaces
 * included; no composition rules, and pasting from a password manager is
 * welcome (NIST SP 800-63B-4 §3.1.1.2, [S1]). The list of common and leaked
 * passwords, and the words of the context, are the server's to check: its
 * `password_rejected` says which rule refused a password, and this console
 * shows that sentence (`./errors.ts::passwordRefusal`).
 */
import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";

export function NewPasswordFields({
  password,
  again,
  onPassword,
  onAgain,
}: {
  password: string;
  again: string;
  onPassword: (value: string) => void;
  onAgain: (value: string) => void;
}) {
  const t = useT();
  return (
    <>
      <Field label={t("auth.password.new")} help={t("auth.password.rules")}>
        <input
          className={inputClass}
          type="password"
          autoComplete="new-password"
          value={password}
          onChange={(event) => onPassword(event.target.value)}
        />
      </Field>
      <Field label={t("auth.password.confirm")}>
        <input
          className={inputClass}
          type="password"
          autoComplete="new-password"
          value={again}
          onChange={(event) => onAgain(event.target.value)}
        />
      </Field>
    </>
  );
}
```
