9. `frontend/src/modules/auth/SignInPage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in` — the first step: email address and password (own-auth design
 * §2.1, §2.3).
 *
 * WHAT THE SERVER ANSWERS DECIDES THE NEXT PAGE, AND NOTHING ELSE DOES:
 * `factor_required` -> `/sign-in/factor` (with the methods and the
 * remember-this-computer length, which are not secrets, in the router's
 * state); `enroll_required` -> `/sign-in/enroll`; `signed_in` -> the console,
 * which happens only on a computer the person chose to remember (§2.6). A
 * wrong password, an unknown address and a locked account read the same here,
 * as they do on the server (§2.3).
 *
 * A PAGE FOR PEOPLE WITHOUT A SESSION, AND IT DOES NOT CHECK FOR ONE: a person
 * who is signed in and opens this page signs in again, and the session they
 * had is replaced. Bouncing them to the console would need a `/me` here, and
 * the harmony gate, whose fixture session is always signed in, could then
 * never see this page.
 */
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Link, useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";

import { Form } from "../../components/form";
import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { enterConsole } from "../../lib/session";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard } from "./AuthCard";
import { describeAuthError } from "./errors";
import { carryNext, useNext } from "./flow";

export function SignInPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const next = useNext();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  // A ref, not the state above: two submits in one frame both read `busy` as
  // false (the same guard as the first-boot screen's).
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function submit() {
    if (inFlight.current || !email.trim() || !password) return;
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const result = await api.login({ email: email.trim(), password });
      if (result.state === "signed_in") {
        enterConsole(next);
        return;
      }
      if (result.state === "enroll_required") {
        navigate(carryNext("/sign-in/enroll", next));
        return;
      }
      navigate(carryNext("/sign-in/factor", next), {
        state: { methods: result.methods, rememberDays: result.remember_device_days ?? null },
      });
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      setPassword("");
      setError(describeAuthError(cause, { rejected: "auth.signIn.rejected", canTimeOut: false }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <AuthCard title={t("auth.signIn.title")} intro={t("auth.signIn.intro")}>
      <Form onSubmit={() => void submit()}>
        <Field label={t("auth.common.email")}>
          <input
            className={inputClass}
            type="email"
            autoComplete="username"
            spellCheck={false}
            value={email}
            onChange={(event) => setEmail(event.target.value)}
          />
        </Field>
        <Field label={t("auth.common.password")}>
          <input
            className={inputClass}
            type="password"
            autoComplete="current-password"
            value={password}
            onChange={(event) => setPassword(event.target.value)}
          />
        </Field>
        <AuthAlert text={error} />
        <div className="form-actions">
          <Btn
            type="submit"
            variant="primary"
            icon="lock"
            label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.signIn.submit")}
            disabled={busy || !email.trim() || !password}
          />
        </div>
      </Form>
      <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Link to={carryNext("/forgot-password", next)}>{t("auth.signIn.forgot")}</Link>
      </p>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

10. `frontend/src/modules/auth/FactorPage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in/factor` — the second factor, after the password (own-auth design
 * §2.2, §2.3, §2.6).
 *
 * THE PASSKEY IS OFFERED FIRST (§2.2): it is the factor a phishing page cannot
 * collect, because the browser binds it to this origin. Then the
 * authenticator app; then, folded away, a recovery code.
 *
 * THE METHODS COME FROM THE SIGN-IN STEP, in the router's state. On a page
 * opened directly -- a reload, a bookmark, the harmony gate -- there are
 * none, and all three are offered: the server refuses one the account does
 * not have exactly as it refuses a wrong code, so offering it reveals nothing
 * the password step had not already established.
 *
 * "DO NOT ASK AGAIN ON THIS COMPUTER" (§2.6) is offered only when the
 * sign-in step said how long the organisation allows (`rememberDays`); absent
 * or `null`, the organisation switched it off or the page cannot know, and no
 * box is drawn. It is unticked every time: a shared computer is the case it
 * must not be ticked on, and the hint says so. The server decides what a
 * remembered computer may skip; the box only asks.
 *
 * EVERY REFUSAL READS THE SAME: "not accepted", whatever the reason (§2.3).
 * Only a pre-factor session that has gone (`auth_required`) and a wait (429)
 * are told apart, because a person can act on those.
 */
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Link, useLocation } from "react-router-dom";

import { Form } from "../../components/form";
import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { enterConsole } from "../../lib/session";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard, AuthSection } from "./AuthCard";
import { describeAuthError } from "./errors";
import { carryNext, digitsOf, recoveryCodeOf, useNext } from "./flow";
import { canUsePasskeys, describePasskeyError, signWithPasskey } from "./passkey";
import type { FactorMethod, SignedIn } from "./types";

const EVERY_METHOD: readonly FactorMethod[] = ["passkey", "totp", "recovery"];

/** What the sign-in step hands this page, read defensively: router state is whatever the history holds. */
function handedOver(state: unknown): { methods: readonly FactorMethod[]; rememberDays: number | null } {
  const given = (state ?? {}) as { methods?: unknown; rememberDays?: unknown };
  const methods = Array.isArray(given.methods)
    ? EVERY_METHOD.filter((method) => (given.methods as unknown[]).includes(method))
    : [];
  const days = given.rememberDays;
  return {
    methods: methods.length > 0 ? methods : EVERY_METHOD,
    rememberDays: typeof days === "number" && Number.isInteger(days) && days > 0 ? days : null,
  };
}

export function FactorPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const location = useLocation();
  const next = useNext();
  const { methods, rememberDays } = handedOver(location.state);
  const passkey = methods.includes("passkey") && canUsePasskeys();
  const totp = methods.includes("totp");
  const recovery = methods.includes("recovery");
  const [showRecovery, setShowRecovery] = useState(!passkey && !totp);
  const [remember, setRemember] = useState(false);
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const [recoveryCode, setRecoveryCode] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function finish(step: () => Promise<SignedIn>) {
    if (inFlight.current) return;
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await step();
      enterConsole(next);
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      setCode("");
      setRecoveryCode("");
      setError(describePasskeyError(cause) ?? describeAuthError(cause, { rejected: "auth.factor.rejected" }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <AuthCard title={t("auth.factor.title")} intro={t("auth.factor.intro")}>
      {rememberDays !== null ? (
        <div>
          <label className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <input type="checkbox" checked={remember} onChange={(event) => setRemember(event.target.checked)} />
            {t("auth.factor.remember", { count: rememberDays })}
          </label>
          <p className="note" style={{ margin: "4px 0 0" }}>
            {t("auth.factor.rememberHint")}
          </p>
        </div>
      ) : null}

      {passkey ? (
        <AuthSection title={t("auth.factor.passkeyTitle")} hint={t("auth.factor.passkeyHint")}>
          <div>
            <Btn
              variant="primary"
              icon="key"
              label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.factor.usePasskey")}
              disabled={busy}
              onClick={() =>
                void finish(async () => {
                  const options = await api.factorPasskeyOptions();
                  const credential = await signWithPasskey(options);
                  return api.factorPasskey({ credential, remember_device: remember });
                })
              }
            />
          </div>
        </AuthSection>
      ) : null}

      {totp ? (
        <AuthSection title={t("auth.factor.totpTitle")}>
          <Form
            onSubmit={() => {
              if (digitsOf(code)) void finish(() => api.factorTotp({ code: digitsOf(code), remember_device: remember }));
            }}
          >
            <Field label={t("auth.factor.totpLabel")}>
              <input
                className={inputClass}
                inputMode="numeric"
                autoComplete="one-time-code"
                spellCheck={false}
                value={code}
                onChange={(event) => setCode(event.target.value)}
              />
            </Field>
            <div className="form-actions">
              <Btn
                type="submit"
                variant={passkey ? "secondary" : "primary"}
                label={t("auth.factor.totpSubmit")}
                disabled={busy || !digitsOf(code)}
              />
            </div>
          </Form>
        </AuthSection>
      ) : null}

      {recovery && !showRecovery ? (
        <div>
          <Btn variant="ghost" small label={t("auth.factor.showRecovery")} onClick={() => setShowRecovery(true)} />
        </div>
      ) : null}
      {recovery && showRecovery ? (
        <AuthSection title={t("auth.factor.recoveryTitle")} hint={t("auth.factor.recoveryHint")}>
          <Form
            onSubmit={() => {
              if (recoveryCode.trim()) {
                void finish(() =>
                  api.factorRecovery({ code: recoveryCodeOf(recoveryCode), remember_device: remember }),
                );
              }
            }}
          >
            <Field label={t("auth.factor.recoveryLabel")}>
              <input
                className={inputClass}
                autoComplete="off"
                autoCapitalize="characters"
                spellCheck={false}
                value={recoveryCode}
                onChange={(event) => setRecoveryCode(event.target.value)}
              />
            </Field>
            <div className="form-actions">
              <Btn
                type="submit"
                label={t("auth.factor.recoverySubmit")}
                disabled={busy || !recoveryCode.trim()}
              />
            </div>
          </Form>
        </AuthSection>
      ) : null}

      <AuthAlert text={error} />
      <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Link to={carryNext("/sign-in", next)}>{t("auth.common.startOver")}</Link>
      </p>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

11. `frontend/src/modules/auth/EnrollPage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in/enroll` — the first second factor (own-auth design §2.2): the
 * person does not reach the console until they have one.
 *
 * Reached from the sign-in step (`enroll_required`) and from an accepted
 * invitation, both of which leave a session that has a password and no
 * factor; every request here rides on it, and a 401 `auth_required` means it
 * has gone and only starting again helps.
 *
 * THE PASSKEY FIRST (§2.2). The options come from the server whole --
 * `userVerification: "required"`, no attestation, the person's existing
 * credentials excluded -- and the server verifies what comes back with user
 * verification required (own-auth Task 5, plan decision D22). This page adds
 * nothing to either: it only carries them.
 *
 * THE AUTHENTICATOR APP SHOWS ITS SETUP KEY, NOT A QR CODE. The secret arrives
 * once, as an `otpauth://` URI (own-auth Task 7); the page shows the key in
 * groups of four to type into the app, and the URI as a link, which a phone
 * opens straight in its authenticator. Drawing a QR code needs a QR encoder,
 * which this console does not carry (plan decision recorded in the plan).
 *
 * EITHER WAY, `enroll/finish` MAKES THE TEN RECOVERY CODES and the next page
 * shows them, handed over in memory (`./flow`), never in the URL or the
 * router's state.
 */
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Link, useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";

import { Form } from "../../components/form";
import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { translate, type MessageKey } from "../../i18n/core";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard, AuthSection } from "./AuthCard";
import { describeAuthError } from "./errors";
import { carryNext, digitsOf, handOverCodes, setupKeyOf, useNext } from "./flow";
import { canUsePasskeys, createPasskey, describePasskeyError } from "./passkey";

export function EnrollPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const next = useNext();
  const passkeys = canUsePasskeys();
  const [name, setName] = useState(() => translate("auth.enroll.passkeyDefaultName"));
  const [otpauthUri, setOtpauthUri] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function run(step: () => Promise<void>, rejected: MessageKey) {
    if (inFlight.current) return;
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await step();
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      setCode("");
      setError(describePasskeyError(cause) ?? describeAuthError(cause, { rejected }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  /** The factor is in: make the recovery codes and show them, once. */
  async function finished() {
    const { recovery_codes } = await api.enrollFinish();
    handOverCodes(recovery_codes);
    navigate(carryNext("/sign-in/recovery-codes", next), { replace: true });
  }

  const setupKey = otpauthUri ? setupKeyOf(otpauthUri) : null;

  return (
    <AuthCard title={t("auth.enroll.title")} intro={t("auth.enroll.intro")}>
      {passkeys ? (
        <AuthSection title={t("auth.enroll.passkeyTitle")} hint={t("auth.enroll.passkeyHint")}>
          <Form
            onSubmit={() =>
              void run(async () => {
                const options = await api.enrollPasskeyOptions();
                const credential = await createPasskey(options);
                await api.enrollPasskey(credential, name.trim());
                await finished();
              }, "auth.enroll.rejected")
            }
          >
            <Field label={t("auth.enroll.passkeyName")}>
              <input className={inputClass} value={name} maxLength={64} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)} />
            </Field>
            <div className="form-actions">
              <Btn
                type="submit"
                variant="primary"
                icon="key"
                label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.enroll.createPasskey")}
                disabled={busy || !name.trim()}
              />
            </div>
          </Form>
        </AuthSection>
      ) : (
        <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          {t("auth.passkey.unsupported")}
        </p>
      )}

      <AuthSection title={t("auth.enroll.totpTitle")} hint={t("auth.enroll.totpHint")}>
        {otpauthUri === null ? (
          <div>
            <Btn
              icon="device-mobile"
              label={t("auth.enroll.startTotp")}
              disabled={busy}
              onClick={() =>
                void run(async () => {
                  const { otpauth_uri } = await api.enrollTotpStart();
                  setOtpauthUri(otpauth_uri);
                }, "auth.enroll.rejected")
              }
            />
          </div>
        ) : (
          <Form
            onSubmit={() => {
              if (digitsOf(code)) {
                void run(async () => {
                  await api.enrollTotpConfirm(digitsOf(code));
                  await finished();
                }, "auth.enroll.rejected");
              }
            }}
          >
            <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
              {t("auth.enroll.setupKey")}
            </p>
            {setupKey ? <code className="code">{setupKey}</code> : null}
            <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
              <a href={otpauthUri}>{t("auth.enroll.openInApp")}</a>
            </p>
            <Field label={t("auth.enroll.totpLabel")}>
              <input
                className={inputClass}
                inputMode="numeric"
                autoComplete="one-time-code"
                spellCheck={false}
                value={code}
                onChange={(event) => setCode(event.target.value)}
              />
            </Field>
            <div className="form-actions">
              <Btn
                type="submit"
                variant="primary"
                label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.enroll.confirmTotp")}
                disabled={busy || !digitsOf(code)}
              />
            </div>
          </Form>
        )}
      </AuthSection>

      <AuthAlert text={error} />
      <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Link to={carryNext("/sign-in", next)}>{t("auth.common.startOver")}</Link>
      </p>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

12. `frontend/src/modules/auth/RecoveryCodesPage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/sign-in/recovery-codes` — the ten recovery codes, shown once (own-auth
 * design §2.2, Q5).
 *
 * They arrive from the step that made them in memory (`./flow`), never in the
 * URL or the router's state, and are dropped when this page goes: a reload
 * shows the "nothing to show" state, which is the truth -- the server keeps
 * only their hashes, so nobody can show them again. New ones are made in
 * Sign-in and security.
 *
 * THE CONSOLE OPENS ONLY AFTER THE PERSON SAYS THEY SAVED THEM. Without the
 * codes, losing a passkey or a phone means another administrator, or the
 * server's recovery command for the only one (§7); the tick costs a second
 * and is the one moment that outcome is still cheap to avoid.
 *
 * Copying does not fail in silence (the enrollment token's rule): a browser
 * that refuses the clipboard says so, and the codes stay on screen to select.
 */
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { enterConsole } from "../../lib/session";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard, AuthDone } from "./AuthCard";
import { forgetCodes, heldCodes, useNext } from "./flow";

async function copyToClipboard(text: string): Promise<boolean> {
  try {
    await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export function RecoveryCodesPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const next = useNext();
  const [codes] = useState(heldCodes);
  const [saved, setSaved] = useState(false);
  const [copied, setCopied] = useState<"no" | "yes" | "failed">("no");
  // Gone with the page. (Strict mode runs this cleanup once on purpose; the
  // codes are already in this component's state by then.)
  useEffect(() => () => forgetCodes(), []);

  if (codes.length === 0) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.codes.title")}>
        <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          {t("auth.codes.none")}
        </p>
        <div className="form-actions">
          <Btn variant="primary" icon="arrow-right" label={t("auth.codes.continue")} onClick={() => enterConsole(next)} />
        </div>
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }

  return (
    <AuthCard title={t("auth.codes.title")} intro={t("auth.codes.intro")}>
      <ul
        className="code"
        aria-label={t("auth.codes.list")}
        style={{ listStyle: "none", margin: 0, display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr))", gap: 6 }}
      >
        {codes.map((code) => (
          <li key={code}>{code}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <div>
        <Btn
          icon="copy"
          label={t("auth.codes.copy")}
          onClick={() => void copyToClipboard(codes.join("\n")).then((ok) => setCopied(ok ? "yes" : "failed"))}
        />
      </div>
      {copied === "yes" ? <AuthDone>{t("auth.codes.copied")}</AuthDone> : null}
      <AuthAlert text={copied === "failed" ? t("auth.codes.copyFailed") : null} />
      <label className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <input type="checkbox" checked={saved} onChange={(event) => setSaved(event.target.checked)} />
        {t("auth.codes.saved")}
      </label>
      <div className="form-actions">
        <Btn
          variant="primary"
          icon="arrow-right"
          label={t("auth.codes.continue")}
          disabled={!saved}
          onClick={() => {
            forgetCodes();
            enterConsole(next);
          }}
        />
      </div>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

```tsx
/**
 * `/forgot-password` — ask for a link to choose a new password (own-auth
 * design §2.8).
 *
 * THE SAME ANSWER WHETHER OR NOT THE ADDRESS HAS AN ACCOUNT. The server
 * answers 202 either way (OWASP Forgot Password, [S8]); this page says
 * "if that address belongs to an account" and nothing more definite, so it
 * cannot be used to learn who has one. The link works once, for 30 minutes,
 * and the second factor is still asked for afterwards: a mailbox alone never
 * gets anyone past it (§2.8).
 */
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Link } from "react-router-dom";

import { Form } from "../../components/form";
import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard, AuthDone } from "./AuthCard";
import { describeAuthError } from "./errors";
import { carryNext, useNext } from "./flow";

export function ForgotPasswordPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const next = useNext();
  const [email, setEmail] = useState("");
  const [sent, setSent] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function submit() {
    if (inFlight.current || !email.trim()) return;
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await api.forgotPassword({ email: email.trim() });
      setSent(true);
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      setError(describeAuthError(cause, { canTimeOut: false }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  return (
    <AuthCard title={t("auth.forgot.title")} intro={sent ? undefined : t("auth.forgot.intro")}>
      {sent ? (
        <AuthDone>{t("auth.forgot.sent")}</AuthDone>
      ) : (
        <Form onSubmit={() => void submit()}>
          <Field label={t("auth.common.email")}>
            <input
              className={inputClass}
              type="email"
              autoComplete="username"
              spellCheck={false}
              value={email}
              onChange={(event) => setEmail(event.target.value)}
            />
          </Field>
          <AuthAlert text={error} />
          <div className="form-actions">
            <Btn
              type="submit"
              variant="primary"
              icon="mail"
              label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.forgot.submit")}
              disabled={busy || !email.trim()}
            />
          </div>
        </Form>
      )}
      <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        <Link to={carryNext("/sign-in", next)}>{t("auth.common.backToSignIn")}</Link>
      </p>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

14. `frontend/src/modules/auth/ResetPasswordPage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/reset-password#<token>` — choose a new password from the emailed link
 * (own-auth design §2.8).
 *
 * The token is single-use and lives 30 minutes; the server keeps only its
 * hash. A link it no longer honours (410 `invalid_link`: expired, used, never
 * issued) reads as one state with one way on: ask for a new link. After a change the person
 * signs in, and the second factor is still asked for -- the mailbox alone
 * never gets anyone past it (§2.8). A refused password says which rule
 * refused it (`./NewPasswordFields.tsx`).
 *
 * THE TOKEN IS READ FROM THE FRAGMENT AND SENT IN THE BODY (`./flow.ts`):
 * it never reaches an access log, a `Referer` or a URL of this console's own
 * requests.
 */
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { Link } from "react-router-dom";

import { Form } from "../../components/form";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard, AuthDone } from "./AuthCard";
import { checkNewPassword, describeAuthError, isDeadLink } from "./errors";
import { useLinkToken } from "./flow";
import { NewPasswordFields } from "./NewPasswordFields";

export function ResetPasswordPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const token = useLinkToken();
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [again, setAgain] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [outcome, setOutcome] = useState<"form" | "done" | "dead">("form");
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function submit() {
    if (inFlight.current) return;
    const problem = checkNewPassword(password, again);
    if (problem) {
      setError(problem);
      return;
    }
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await api.resetPassword({ token, password });
      setOutcome("done");
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      if (isDeadLink(cause)) setOutcome("dead");
      else setError(describeAuthError(cause, { canTimeOut: false }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  if (outcome === "done") {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.reset.title")}>
        <AuthDone>{t("auth.reset.done")}</AuthDone>
        <div className="form-actions">
          <Link className="btn primary" to="/sign-in">
            {t("auth.reset.signIn")}
          </Link>
        </div>
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  if (outcome === "dead") {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.reset.title")}>
        <AuthAlert text={t("auth.reset.invalid")} />
        <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          <Link to="/forgot-password">{t("auth.reset.askAgain")}</Link>
        </p>
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  return (
    <AuthCard title={t("auth.reset.title")}>
      <Form onSubmit={() => void submit()}>
        <NewPasswordFields password={password} again={again} onPassword={setPassword} onAgain={setAgain} />
        <AuthAlert text={error} />
        <div className="form-actions">
          <Btn
            type="submit"
            variant="primary"
            icon="lock"
            label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.reset.submit")}
            disabled={busy || !password || !again}
          />
        </div>
      </Form>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

15. `frontend/src/modules/auth/InvitePage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/invite#<token>` — accept an invitation: choose a password, then the first
 * second factor (own-auth design §7).
 *
 * The invitation is single-use and lives 72 hours; the server keeps only its
 * hash. Accepting it leaves a session with a password and no factor, so the
 * next page is `/sign-in/enroll` and the console opens only after a factor and
 * the recovery codes (§2.2). An invitation the server no longer honours (410
 * `invalid_link`: expired, used, cancelled) reads as one state, and says who
 * can fix it. The token comes from the fragment and travels in bodies only
 * (`./flow.ts`).
 *
 * SAMESITE=STRICT IS WHY THIS IS A PAGE AND NOT A SERVER LINK (plan decision
 * D19). The email link is a cross-site top-level navigation, which carries no
 * Strict cookie; this page's own requests are same-origin and do.
 */
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";

import { Form } from "../../components/form";
import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { Trans } from "../../i18n/Trans";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard } from "./AuthCard";
import { checkNewPassword, describeAuthError, isDeadLink } from "./errors";
import { useLinkToken } from "./flow";
import { NewPasswordFields } from "./NewPasswordFields";

export function InvitePage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const token = useLinkToken();
  // Asked even with no token: the server answers an empty one as it answers
  // any unknown link (410), and fixture mode -- which cannot add a fragment --
  // still draws the form for the harmony gate.
  // Asked once: every ask spends the per-IP limit the accept step shares (Task 7, `_LINK`).
  const invite = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["auth", "invite", token],
    queryFn: () => api.getInvite(token),
    retry: false,
    staleTime: Infinity,
    refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
  });
  const [password, setPassword] = useState("");
  const [again, setAgain] = useState("");
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [dead, setDead] = useState(false);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function submit() {
    if (inFlight.current) return;
    const problem = checkNewPassword(password, again);
    if (problem) {
      setError(problem);
      return;
    }
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await api.acceptInvite({ token, password });
      navigate("/sign-in/enroll", { replace: true });
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      if (isDeadLink(cause)) setDead(true);
      else setError(describeAuthError(cause, { canTimeOut: false }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  if (invite.isPending) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.invite.loading")}>
        <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          {t("auth.common.working")}
        </p>
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  if (dead || (invite.isError && isDeadLink(invite.error))) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.invite.heading")}>
        <AuthAlert text={t("auth.invite.invalid")} />
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  if (invite.isError) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.invite.heading")}>
        <AuthAlert text={describeAuthError(invite.error, { canTimeOut: false })} />
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  const { email, display_name } = invite.data;
  return (
    <AuthCard
      title={t("auth.invite.title", { name: display_name })}
      intro={<Trans k="auth.invite.intro" vars={{ email }} components={{ b: <b style={{ color: "var(--ink)" }} /> }} />}
    >
      <Form onSubmit={() => void submit()}>
        {/* For the password manager: the account the new password belongs to. */}
        <Field label={t("auth.common.email")}>
          <input className={inputClass} type="email" autoComplete="username" value={email} readOnly />
        </Field>
        <NewPasswordFields password={password} again={again} onPassword={setPassword} onAgain={setAgain} />
        <AuthAlert text={error} />
        <div className="form-actions">
          <Btn
            type="submit"
            variant="primary"
            icon="arrow-right"
            label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.invite.submit")}
            disabled={busy || !password || !again}
          />
        </div>
      </Form>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

#### Addendum del coordinador (Task 11)

Dos decisiones del coordinador, tras reconciliar las Tasks 7–8 (diseño §7, Q5), que esta tarea construye después
del Step 9 y antes de la verificación del Step 10: **(A)** la página pública del enlace que imprime el comando de
recuperación del servidor (`python -m app.core.auth.recover --email …`), y **(B)** la contraseña del dueño en el
primer arranque. Mismas reglas: pruebas primero, diffs contra el estado que deja el paso anterior (el primero,
contra el que deja el Step 9), generados y comprobados repitiendo los pasos sobre una copia.

**Files:**
- Create: `frontend/src/modules/auth/RecoverPage.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/auth/__tests__/recover.test.tsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/lib/session.ts` (`PUBLIC_PATHS` gana `/recover`) y `frontend/src/lib/session.test.ts` (su lista exacta)
- Modify: `frontend/src/modules/auth/types.ts` (`RecoveryLink`), `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` (`getRecovery`, `acceptRecovery`, tras `acceptInvite`), `frontend/src/lib/api.auth.test.ts`
- Modify: `frontend/src/modules/auth/__tests__/harness.tsx`, `routes.test.ts`, `frontend/src/modules/auth/auth.es.test.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/auth/fixtures.ts`
- Modify: `frontend/src/i18n/en/auth.ts`, `frontend/src/i18n/es/auth.ts` (`auth.recover`)
- Modify: `frontend/src/App.tsx` (la ruta `/recover`), `frontend/scripts/routes.mjs` (`/recover` para harmony)
- Modify: `frontend/src/modules/setup/SetupPage.tsx`, `frontend/src/i18n/en/setup.ts`, `frontend/src/i18n/es/setup.ts`, `frontend/src/modules/setup/__tests__/setup.test.tsx`, `frontend/src/modules/setup/setup.es.test.tsx`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes (Task 8, reconciliado por el coordinador): `POST /api/v1/auth/recover/details {token}` → `{"email"}`;
  `POST /api/v1/auth/recover/accept {token}` → el servidor quita los segundos factores y los códigos de la cuenta y
  deja una sesión sin factor; un enlace usado, caducado o desconocido, 410 `{"code": "invalid_link"}`; el enlace es
  `/recover#<token>`. `POST /api/v1/setup/claim` gana `password` (contraseña de técnico: 12–128, lista de bloqueo y
  contexto en el servidor; `password_rejected` con `detail`).
- Produces: `ApiClient.getRecovery(token: string): Promise<RecoveryLink>`; `ApiClient.acceptRecovery(token: string): Promise<void>`;
  `interface RecoveryLink { email: string }` (`modules/auth/types.ts`); `RecoverPage` en `/recover`; `PUBLIC_PATHS`
  con `/recover`; textos `auth.recover.{heading,loading,title,intro,what,submit,invalid}`. `SetupPage` deja de
  exportar `Claimed` y de tener la pantalla «Configuración completada»; `setup.claim.*` desaparece y
  `setup.page.passwordHint` cambia de texto.

**Decisiones del plan (addendum):**
- *Abrir el enlace de recuperación no cambia nada.* La página dice de quién es la cuenta y qué hará (quitar los
  segundos factores y los códigos; después, un factor y códigos nuevos) y espera un clic: un enlace que alguien
  abre por error, o que un previsualizador de enlaces visita, no deja a nadie sin sus factores.
- *Tras reclamar la instalación, la página va sola a `/sign-in`* (una carga del documento, por `SetupGate`): el dueño
  tiene contraseña y no hay invitación que esperar, así que la pantalla «Configuración completada» y su aviso de
  correo fallido desaparecen, y sus pruebas se re-apuntan (lista abajo).
- *`SetupPage` reutiliza `NewPasswordFields`, `checkNewPassword` y `describeAuthError` de `modules/auth/`*, como pide
  el coordinador: una sola regla de contraseña de técnico en la consola.

**Pruebas existentes que cambian a propósito (B):** `frontend/src/modules/setup/__tests__/setup.test.tsx` — «goes to
this console's sign-in page in one load, with nothing to fail first» (el botón «Go to sign in») → «… once the
installation is claimed» (sin botón); «says plainly when the invitation could not be sent» → «refuses a %s password
before claiming anything» (corta, distinta); «claims once however many times…» espera la navegación en vez del correo
en pantalla; nueva: «shows the server's sentence when it refuses the password». `setup.es.test.tsx` — «shows the
completed screen in Spanish, with a failed invitation…» → «goes to sign in once the installation is claimed»; «says
where to find the invitation when it was sent» → «refuses a short password in Spanish, before claiming anything»; la
pista de `passwordHint` se lee con su texto nuevo.

```tsx
/**
 * `/recover#<token>` — the link the server's recovery command prints (own-auth
 * design §7, Q5; coordinator decision for Task 11).
 *
 * Opening the link changes nothing: the page names the account and waits for
 * one press. The press removes the account's second factors (server side) and
 * goes on to a new first factor. The token comes from the fragment, leaves the
 * address, and travels in bodies only.
 */
import { screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ApiError } from "../../../lib/api";
import { authApi, calls, installDefaults, renderAuth, where } from "./harness";

vi.mock("../../../lib/ApiContext", () => ({ useApi: () => authApi() }));

beforeEach(() => {
  installDefaults();
});

describe("recovering an account from the server's link", () => {
  it("names whose account it is and changes nothing until the person presses", async () => {
    renderAuth("/recover#tok-recover-1");
    expect(await screen.findByRole("heading", { name: "Recover your account" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(calls.getRecovery).toHaveBeenCalledWith("tok-recover-1");
    expect(screen.getByText("owner@example.test", { selector: "b" })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(screen.getByText(/removes this account's second factors and recovery codes/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(calls.acceptRecovery).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.hash).toBe(""));
  });

  it("recovers on the press, with the token in the body, and goes on to a new first factor", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/recover#tok-recover-1");
    await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Recover my account" }));
    expect(calls.acceptRecovery).toHaveBeenCalledWith("tok-recover-1");
    await waitFor(() => expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/sign-in/enroll"));
  });

  it("says a used, expired or unknown link is dead, and who can make another", async () => {
    calls.getRecovery.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(410, '{"code":"invalid_link"}'));
    renderAuth("/recover#tok-gone");
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/This recovery link has expired or was already used/);
    expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: "Recover my account" })).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("says so when the link died between opening it and pressing", async () => {
    calls.acceptRecovery.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(410, '{"code":"invalid_link"}'));
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/recover#tok-recover-1");
    await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Recover my account" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent(/This recovery link has expired or was already used/);
    expect(where.location?.pathname).toBe("/recover");
  });

  it("says a wait for what it is, and stays", async () => {
    calls.acceptRecovery.mockRejectedValue(new ApiError(429, '{"code":"factor_wait","wait_s":30}'));
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    renderAuth("/recover#tok-recover-1");
    await user.click(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Recover my account" }));
    expect(await screen.findByRole("alert")).toHaveTextContent("Too many attempts. Wait 30 seconds and try again.");
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Recover my account" })).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step A2: `RecoverPage`, sus métodos, textos, fixtures y ruta**

1. `frontend/src/modules/auth/RecoverPage.tsx`:

```tsx
/**
 * `/recover#<token>` — the link the server's recovery command prints, for an
 * administrator who lost every second factor and has nobody to reset them
 * (own-auth design §7, Q5: `python -m app.core.auth.recover --email …`, own-auth
 * Task 8). It exists only on the server host: there is no way to ask for one
 * over HTTP, and it lives 15 minutes.
 *
 * WHAT IT DOES, SAID BEFORE IT DOES IT. Accepting removes the account's second
 * factors and recovery codes and leaves a session that has none, so the next
 * page is `/sign-in/enroll`, and the console opens only after a new factor and
 * new codes (§2.2). The page shows whose account the link is for and asks for
 * one deliberate press; opening the link does nothing by itself.
 *
 * A link the server no longer honours (410 `invalid_link`: used, expired or
 * unknown) reads as one state, and says who can make another. The token comes
 * from the fragment and travels in bodies only (`./flow.ts`).
 */
import { useQuery } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";

import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import { Trans } from "../../i18n/Trans";
import { useApi } from "../../lib/ApiContext";
import { Btn } from "../../shell/components";
import { AuthAlert, AuthCard } from "./AuthCard";
import { describeAuthError, isDeadLink } from "./errors";
import { useLinkToken } from "./flow";

export function RecoverPage() {
  const t = useT();
  const api = useApi();
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const token = useLinkToken();
  // Asked even with no token, as `InvitePage` is: the server's 410 decides, and
  // fixture mode still draws the page for the harmony gate.
  const recovery = useQuery({
    queryKey: ["auth", "recover", token],
    queryFn: () => api.getRecovery(token),
    retry: false,
    // Asked once: every ask spends the per-IP limit the accept step shares.
    staleTime: Infinity,
    refetchOnWindowFocus: false,
  });
  const [dead, setDead] = useState(false);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  const inFlight = useRef(false);

  async function recover() {
    if (inFlight.current) return;
    inFlight.current = true;
    setBusy(true);
    setError(null);
    try {
      await api.acceptRecovery(token);
      navigate("/sign-in/enroll", { replace: true });
    } catch (cause: unknown) {
      if (isDeadLink(cause)) setDead(true);
      else setError(describeAuthError(cause, { canTimeOut: false }));
    } finally {
      inFlight.current = false;
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }

  if (recovery.isPending) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.recover.loading")}>
        <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
          {t("auth.common.working")}
        </p>
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  if (dead || (recovery.isError && isDeadLink(recovery.error))) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.recover.heading")}>
        <AuthAlert text={t("auth.recover.invalid")} />
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  if (recovery.isError) {
    return (
      <AuthCard title={t("auth.recover.heading")}>
        <AuthAlert text={describeAuthError(recovery.error, { canTimeOut: false })} />
      </AuthCard>
    );
  }
  return (
    <AuthCard
      title={t("auth.recover.title")}
      intro={
        <Trans
          k="auth.recover.intro"
          vars={{ email: recovery.data.email }}
          components={{ b: <b style={{ color: "var(--ink)" }} /> }}
        />
      }
    >
      <p className="note" style={{ margin: 0 }}>
        {t("auth.recover.what")}
      </p>
      <AuthAlert text={error} />
      <div className="form-actions">
        <Btn
          variant="primary"
          icon="key"
          label={busy ? t("auth.common.working") : t("auth.recover.submit")}
          disabled={busy}
          onClick={() => void recover()}
        />
      </div>
    </AuthCard>
  );
}
```

```diff
+              variant="primary"
+              disabled={!complete || submitting}
+            />
+            <span className="form-hint">
+              {t("setup.page.passwordHint")}
+            </span>
+          </div>
+        </form>
       </div>
     </div>

-/**
- * What happened, said honestly.
- *
- * A fresh installation usually has no email configured, so the invitation is
- * the step most likely to fail — and it fails AFTER the organization and the
- * administrator exist, which is the one outcome a green checkmark would
- * misrepresent. When the mail did not go, this says so and says what to do,
- * rather than sending the operator to a sign-in page that will never let them
- * in.
- */
-function Claim({ claimed }: { claimed: Claimed }) {
-  const t = useT();
-  return (
-    <>
-      <h1 style={HEADLINE}>{t("setup.claim.title")}</h1>
-      <p className="note" style={{ marginTop: 6 }}>
-        <Trans
-          k="setup.claim.belongsTo"
-          vars={{ email: claimed.email }}
-          components={{ b: <b style={{ color: "var(--ink)" }} /> }}
-        />
-      </p>
-      {claimed.invitation_sent ? (
-        <p className="note" style={{ marginTop: 14 }}>
-          {t("setup.claim.checkInbox")}
-        </p>
-      ) : (
-        <p role="alert" className="notice red" style={{ marginTop: 14 }}>
-          <Icon name={KIND_ICON.crit} size={16} />
-          <span>
-            {claimed.invitation_error ?? t("setup.claim.invitationFailed")}
-          </span>
-        </p>
-      )}
-      <div className="form-actions" style={{ marginTop: 20 }}>
-        {/* A WHOLE-DOCUMENT LOAD, NOT A ROUTE CHANGE. `SetupGate` holds
-            `needed: true` for the life of this tab (`staleTime: Infinity`),
-            so a route change would land on this same screen; a fresh page
-            asks again and finds the installation claimed. Nothing is fetched
-            first, so -- unlike the identity provider's discovery document
-            this button used to wait on -- nothing can fail before it goes. */}
-        <Btn
-          label={t("setup.claim.goToSignIn")}
-          icon="lock"
-          variant="primary"
-          onClick={() => navigation.assign(SIGN_IN_PATH)}
-        />
-      </div>
-    </>
-  );
-}
```

**Decisiones del plan (Task 12):**
- *Decisión del plan: añadir una clave de acceso o (re)configurar la app desde Mi seguridad usa las rutas de alta de la
  Task 7 (`/auth/enroll/totp/*`, `/auth/enroll/passkey*`) con la sesión completa.* El Apéndice A da a Mi seguridad solo
  rutas para leer y quitar (`/me/*`), y el diseño quiere «varias por cuenta» (§2.2) y poder cambiar los factores (§2.5).
  Requisito para la Task 7 (se dice en el informe): esas cuatro rutas aceptan también una sesión con `factor_done`,
  exigen la confirmación reciente (403 `step_up_required`) y `totp/confirm` con un TOTP activo lo **reemplaza**.
- *Decisión del plan: el 403 `step_up_required` se reconoce con `code` en la raíz del cuerpo o en `detail.code`.*
  el Apéndice A escribe `{"code": "step_up_required"}`; una `HTTPException(detail={...})` de FastAPI lo sirve como
  `{"detail": {"code": …}}`. Las dos formas valen; cualquier otro 403 pasa tal cual. Tras confirmar el factor la
  petición se repite **una** vez; un segundo 403 se devuelve sin volver a preguntar.
- *Decisión del plan: un factor equivocado en `/auth/step-up/*` no puede ser 401.* Un 401 llama a `onUnauthorized` y la
  consola sale a iniciar sesión. Requisito para la Task 7: 400/422 con `detail` genérico (o 429 con espera).
- *Decisión del plan: las rutas personales (`/me/*`, `/auth/step-up/*`) se piden con `global: true`* (`RequestRoute.global`,
  `api.ts:1587-1596`): son filas de la persona, no de un cliente, y un cliente elegido arriba no tiene nada que decir
  de ellas. Las de administración (`/users/invite`, `/users/{id}/invite[/resend]`, `/users/{id}/factors/reset`,
  `/users/{id}/sessions`) y `PUT /settings/sessions` dependen de `globalRoutes.json`: las Tasks 6 y 8 las añaden a
  `GLOBAL_WRITES` y regeneran el JSON. `src/lib/api.account.test.ts` lo fija y falla si falta alguna.
- *Decisión del plan: campos que la consola lee y el Apéndice A no fijaba* (se dicen a las Tasks 7 y 8):
  `sessions[] = {id, created_at, last_seen_at, expires_at, user_agent, ip, current}`,
  `trusted_devices[] = {id, label, created_at, expires_at, last_used_at, current}`, `UserOut.invite_pending: bool`,
  `POST /users/{id}/invite/resend` → `{invite_link: str | null}` (como la invitación), `SessionSettingsOut.updated_at`
  opcional. La consola trata un `invite_pending` ausente como `false`.
- *Decisión del plan: sin QR.* No se añade ninguna dependencia: Mi seguridad muestra la clave en grupos de cuatro y un
  enlace `otpauth://` (solo si empieza así). Si la Task 11 añadió un componente QR, el coordinador puede usarlo al fusionar.
- *Decisión del plan: la consola deja de ofrecer «Restablecer contraseña» y «Reenviar inscripción» a un administrador.*
  Eran correos de Keycloak; el diseño deja el restablecimiento en manos de la persona (§2.8, «olvidé mi contraseña») y
  da al administrador «restablecer factores» (§7). `createUser`, `resetUserPassword`, `resendUserEnrolment` y sus tipos
  salen de la consola. «Eliminar» se queda: `DELETE /users/{id}` no lo retira ningún documento.
- *Decisión del plan: la pestaña se llama «Sesiones» (clave `sessions`) y va tras «Usuarios».* El diseño dice
  «Configuración → Seguridad → Sesiones», pero Ajustes es una lista plana. Se ofrece con `orgs.manage` (como Correo, cuya
  lectura es el mismo código) y se escribe con `orgs.manage` en todos los clientes (Apéndice A, Task 6).
- *Decisión del plan: la confirmación reciente cubre también retirar una credencial de la bóveda* (`CredentialsPage`):
  §2.5 la exige y el falsificador 5 («la bóveda sigue pidiendo el segundo factor») la necesita en la consola. Si el
  servidor no la pide, `run()` no cambia nada.
- *Decisión del plan: el enlace de invitación, los códigos de recuperación y la clave TOTP viven en el estado del
  componente*, como el secreto retirado de la bóveda (`CredentialsPage.tsx:53-62`): la mutación se vacía (`reset()`)
  en su `onSuccess`, nada pasa por la caché de consultas, y desaparecen cuando la persona dice que los tiene.
- *Decisión del plan (con el contrato de la Task 3): Ajustes → Correo no ofrece ya un campo libre para la
  dirección del token de Microsoft.* La plataforma presenta allí el secreto de cliente, y la Task 3 rechaza con 422 toda
  dirección que no sea `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<directorio>/oauth2/v2.0/token`. La dirección sale del ID de
  directorio (`tokenUrlFor`, como hoy); el cuadro «Advanced» conserva solo el ámbito, y una dirección guardada que no sea
  de Microsoft se lee como «sin directorio» y bloquea el guardado hasta escribirlo. Las nubes gubernamentales o nacionales
  dejan de poder configurarse (el texto de ayuda lo dice).
- *Decisión del plan: la ayuda de la prueba de correo deja de decir que el proveedor rechaza tu dirección tal cual*
  (era una limitación de Keycloak) y dice el límite nuevo de la Task 3 (5 pruebas por minuto y organización); el 429 se
  muestra con las palabras del servidor dentro de «Not sent.». La consola sigue proponiendo `suggested_test_recipient`,
  que la Task 3 conserva igual que la regla de destinatarios.
- *Decisión del plan: quitar el único segundo factor se desactiva en la consola con su motivo*; el servidor lo
  rechaza igualmente (requisito para la Task 7: 409 con `detail`).
- *Decisión del plan: Mi seguridad cierra las otras sesiones una a una*; no ofrece «cerrar sesión en todas partes»
  (`logoutEverywhere` es de la Task 11).
- *Decisión del plan: el aviso `identity_locale_synced` de `ProfilePage.tsx:326-333` se conserva sin cambios*: es el
  espejo de idioma de Keycloak (`me.py:230-284`) y lo retira quien retire ese espejo.

Crear `frontend/src/lib/api.account.test.ts`. Copia la forma de `src/lib/api.clientScope.test.ts:22-40` (`stubFetch`, las
cabeceras del enésimo `fetch`) con el constructor de la Task 10:

```ts
/**
 * The account routes (own authentication design §2, §7) and `X-Client-Id`.
 *
 * YOUR OWN ACCOUNT IS NOT A CLIENT'S. `/me/*` and `/auth/step-up/*` are the
 * person's own rows -- their password, factors, remembered devices and
 * sessions -- and a client chosen in the top bar says nothing about them, so
 * those requests never carry the header (`RequestRoute.global`).
 *
 * THE ADMINISTRATORS' ROUTES ARE CONFIGURATION EVERY CLIENT SHARES. Inviting,
 * resending, cancelling, resetting someone's factors, signing them out and the
 * session settings need their code on every client (`GLOBAL_WRITES`,
 * `backend/tests/test_global_writes.py`), so they are in `globalRoutes.json`:
 * narrowed, the server answers 403 to the very person allowed to act.
 */

import type { AuthenticationResponseJSON } from "@simplewebauthn/browser";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ApiClient } from "./api";
import { isGlobalRoute } from "./globalRoutes";

const ACME = "0b6a2c1e-6d2f-4a51-9c3e-2f4d1a7b8c01";

const ASSERTION: AuthenticationResponseJSON = {
  id: "Y3JlZA",
  rawId: "Y3JlZA",
  response: { clientDataJSON: "e30", authenticatorData: "YXV0aA", signature: "c2ln" },
  clientExtensionResults: {},
  type: "public-key",
};

function stubFetch(): ReturnType<typeof vi.fn> {
  const fetchMock = vi
    .fn()
    .mockImplementation(() => Promise.resolve(new Response("{}", { status: 200 })));
  vi.stubGlobal("fetch", fetchMock);
  return fetchMock;
}

/** The nth `fetch`: its request line, its headers and its body. */
function sent(fetchMock: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>, call: number): { line: string; headers: Headers; body: unknown } {
  const [url, init] = fetchMock.mock.calls[call] as [string, RequestInit];
  return {
    line: `${init.method ?? "GET"} ${url}`,
    headers: new Headers(init.headers),
    body: typeof init.body === "string" ? JSON.parse(init.body) : undefined,
  };
}

/** A console with Acme chosen in the top bar. */
function narrowed(): ApiClient {
  return new ApiClient(vi.fn(), "/api/v1", () => ACME);
}

afterEach(() => {
  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
});

describe("your own account is never narrowed to a client", () => {
  it("asks each route by its own method and path, and none of them carries X-Client-Id", async () => {
    const fetchMock = stubFetch();
    const api = narrowed();
    await api.getMySecurity();
    await api.changePassword({ current: "old phrase here", new: "a much longer phrase" });
    await api.removePasskey("pk 1");
    await api.removeTotp();
    await api.regenerateRecoveryCodes();
    await api.revokeTrustedDevice("td-1");
    await api.endMySession("s-1");
    await api.stepUpTotp("123456");
    await api.stepUpPasskeyOptions();
    await api.stepUpPasskey(ASSERTION);
    await api.stepUpRecovery("7KQ2M-X9D4P");

    const requests = fetchMock.mock.calls.map((_, at) => sent(fetchMock, at));
    expect(requests.map((request) => request.line)).toEqual([
      "GET /api/v1/me/security",
      "PUT /api/v1/me/password",
      // An id is one path segment, whatever it holds.
      "DELETE /api/v1/me/passkeys/pk%201",
      "DELETE /api/v1/me/totp",
      "POST /api/v1/me/recovery-codes",
      "DELETE /api/v1/me/trusted-devices/td-1",
      "DELETE /api/v1/me/sessions/s-1",
      "POST /api/v1/auth/step-up/totp",
      "POST /api/v1/auth/step-up/passkey/options",
      "POST /api/v1/auth/step-up/passkey",
      "POST /api/v1/auth/step-up/recovery",
    ]);
    for (const request of requests) expect(request.headers.has("X-Client-Id"), request.line).toBe(false);
  });

  it("sends each body as the server reads it", async () => {
    const fetchMock = stubFetch();
    const api = narrowed();
    await api.changePassword({ current: "old phrase here", new: "a much longer phrase" });
    await api.stepUpTotp("123456");
    await api.stepUpPasskey(ASSERTION);
    await api.stepUpRecovery("7KQ2M-X9D4P");
    expect([0, 1, 2, 3].map((at) => sent(fetchMock, at).body)).toEqual([
      { current: "old phrase here", new: "a much longer phrase" },
      { code: "123456" },
      { credential: ASSERTION },
      { code: "7KQ2M-X9D4P" },
    ]);
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Los tipos y los métodos**

Crear `frontend/src/modules/profile/types.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Your own sign-in security, as `GET /api/v1/me/security` serves it (own
 * authentication design §2.2, §2.4, §2.6). NOTHING SECRET IS IN IT, by the
 * server's construction and by this file's: a passkey is its name and dates, a
 * remembered device and a session are where and when. The values a person sees
 * once -- the authenticator key, new recovery codes -- come in the answer to
 * their own write and are never part of this read.
 */

export interface MyPasskey {
  id: string;
  /** The name the person gave it when they added it. Recorded text. */
  name: string;
  created_at: string;
  last_used_at: string | null;
  /** Synced by a password manager or a platform account (WebAuthn backup state). */
  backup_state: boolean;
}

/** A device that skips the second factor until `expires_at` (design §2.6). */
export interface MyTrustedDevice {
  id: string;
  /** What the server called it when it was remembered ("Firefox on Windows"). Recorded text. */
  label: string;
  created_at: string;
  expires_at: string;
  last_used_at: string | null;
  /** This browser is that device. */
  current: boolean;
}

/** One signed-in session (design §2.4). */
export interface MySession {
  id: string;
  created_at: string;
  last_seen_at: string;
  expires_at: string;
  /** As the browser sent it. Recorded text. */
  user_agent: string;
  ip: string;
  /** The session this console is using: it ends by signing out, not from this list. */
  current: boolean;
}

export interface MySecurity {
  has_totp: boolean;
  passkeys: MyPasskey[];
  recovery_codes_left: number;
  trusted_devices: MyTrustedDevice[];
  sessions: MySession[];
}

/** `PUT /me/password`. `new` is the server's key; TypeScript allows it as a property name. */
export interface PasswordChange {
  current: string;
  new: string;
}

/** `POST /me/recovery-codes`: ten new codes, shown once (design §2.2). */
export interface RecoveryCodesOut {
  recovery_codes: string[];
}

/**
 * The server's password bounds for a technician (design §2.1), restated only
 * to say so before the round trip: the blocklist, the context words and these
 * very bounds are the server's, and its refusal is what counts. Each code
 * point counts as one, so the console counts with `[...value].length`.
 */
export const PASSWORD_MIN = 12;
export const PASSWORD_MAX = 128;

/** How many codes a set holds (design §2.2). */
export const RECOVERY_CODE_COUNT = 10;
```

hasta el Step 19, que retira su último uso):

```ts
/**
 * One grant an invitation carries: a role on one client, or on every client
 * (`client_id: null`, MSP clients spec §2.1) -- the same pair `RoleAssign` sends.
 */
export interface InviteGrant {
  role_id: string;
  client_id: string | null;
}

/** `POST /users/invite` (own authentication design §7). No password: the person chooses it from the link. */
export interface UserInvite {
  email: string;
  display_name: string;
  grants: InviteGrant[];
}

/**
 * What came of an invitation. `invite_link` is `null` when the server emailed
 * it; the link itself when no mail is configured, in THIS answer only -- the
 * server keeps its hash, never the link, so the console shows it once and
 * keeps it nowhere but the screen.
 */
export interface InviteOut {
  user_id: string;
  invite_link: string | null;
}

/** `POST /users/{id}/invite/resend`: a fresh link, emailed or shown once like the first. */
export interface InviteLinkOut {
  invite_link: string | null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sessions -- `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/sessions` (own authentication design §2.4, §2.6, §3)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** How long a sign-in lasts, for the whole organization (`auth_org_settings`). */
export interface SessionSettingsOut {
  staff_idle_minutes: number;
  staff_max_hours: number;
  remember_device_enabled: boolean;
  remember_device_days: number;
  remembered_max_hours: number;
  contact_idle_minutes: number;
  contact_max_days: number;
  /** When it was last saved. Absent until the first save. */
  updated_at?: string | null;
}

/** The PUT carries all seven, never a part: the form shows all seven. */
export type SessionSettingsUpdate = Omit<SessionSettingsOut, "updated_at">;

export type SessionNumberKey = Exclude<keyof SessionSettingsUpdate, "remember_device_enabled">;

/**
 * The CHECK bounds of `auth_org_settings` (migration 0245, Task 1 of the
 * P2 phase 1 plan), restated so a value out of range is refused before the round trip. The
 * server's constraint is what holds.
 */
export const SESSION_BOUNDS: Readonly<Record<SessionNumberKey, readonly [number, number]>> = {
  staff_idle_minutes: [5, 480],
  staff_max_hours: [1, 24],
  remember_device_days: [1, 30],
  remembered_max_hours: [1, 720],
  contact_idle_minutes: [5, 480],
  contact_max_days: [1, 30],
};
```

   `SessionSettingsOut`, `SessionSettingsUpdate` y `UserInvite`. Justo debajo de esa declaración:

```ts

```

   (`AuthenticationResponseJSON` y `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON` ya los importa la Task 11 en este archivo,
   desde `../modules/auth/types`: no se añade otra declaración, que sería un identificador duplicado para `tsc`.)

2. Tras `updateMe` (`:1888-1890`), la sección nueva:

```ts
  // ----------------------------------------------------------- your security

  /**
   * Your own sign-in security (`GET /me/security`, own authentication design
   * §2.2-§2.6): the factors you have, the recovery codes left, your
   * remembered devices and your sessions. No secret is in it.
   *
   * EVERY REQUEST IN THIS SECTION GOES WITHOUT `X-Client-Id` (`global`):
   * these are the person's own rows, not a client's, and a client chosen in
   * the top bar says nothing about them. Like `updateMe`, none takes a user
   * id: the server answers for the session's own person.
   *
   * THE ONES THAT CHANGE A FACTOR may answer 403 `step_up_required` (§2.5);
   * callers send them through `useStepUp().run` (`components/stepUp.tsx`),
   * which asks for the second factor and sends the request once more.
   */
  getMySecurity(): Promise<MySecurity> {
    return this.request<MySecurity>("/me/security", {}, { global: true });
  }

  /** `PUT /me/password`. Both passwords travel once, in the body, and come back in nothing. */
  changePassword(body: PasswordChange): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>("/me/password", { method: "PUT", body: JSON.stringify(body) }, { global: true });
  }

  removePasskey(passkeyId: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(
      `/me/passkeys/${encodeURIComponent(passkeyId)}`,
      { method: "DELETE" },
      { global: true },
    );
  }

  removeTotp(): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>("/me/totp", { method: "DELETE" }, { global: true });
  }

  /**
   * Ten new codes; the old ones stop working. This answer is the one place
   * they exist in the clear: show it once and keep it nowhere.
   */
  regenerateRecoveryCodes(): Promise<RecoveryCodesOut> {
    return this.request<RecoveryCodesOut>("/me/recovery-codes", { method: "POST" }, { global: true });
  }

  revokeTrustedDevice(deviceId: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(
      `/me/trusted-devices/${encodeURIComponent(deviceId)}`,
      { method: "DELETE" },
      { global: true },
    );
  }

  /** Another of your sessions. The current one ends by signing out. */
  endMySession(sessionId: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(
      `/me/sessions/${encodeURIComponent(sessionId)}`,
      { method: "DELETE" },
      { global: true },
    );
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------- the recent confirmation

  /** `POST /auth/step-up/totp` (design §2.5): a code from your app confirms your second factor for 10 minutes. */
  stepUpTotp(code: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>("/auth/step-up/totp", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ code }) }, { global: true });
  }

  /** A single-use challenge for `startAuthentication`, as W3C JSON (py_webauthn's `options_to_json`). */
  stepUpPasskeyOptions(): Promise<PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON> {
    return this.request<PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON>(
      "/auth/step-up/passkey/options",
      { method: "POST" },
      { global: true },
    );
  }

  /** The browser's signed answer to that challenge, exactly as `startAuthentication` returned it. */
  stepUpPasskey(credential: AuthenticationResponseJSON): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(
      "/auth/step-up/passkey",
      { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ credential }) },
      { global: true },
    );
  }

  /** A recovery code. It works once: the server spends it. */
  stepUpRecovery(code: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>("/auth/step-up/recovery", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ code }) }, { global: true });
  }
```

```ts
  /**
   * Two routes, one method: `/disable` and `/enable` differ only in
   * direction. Disabling ends the person's sessions and forgets their
   * remembered devices at once (own authentication design §2.4).
   */
  setUserEnabled(userId: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<UserOut> {
    return this.request<UserOut>(`/users/${userId}/${enabled ? "enable" : "disable"}`, {
      method: "POST",
    });
  }

  /**
   * Invite a technician (`POST /users/invite`, own authentication design §7):
   * the address, the name and what they may reach on which client. NO
   * PASSWORD: the person chooses one from a single-use link that expires
   * after 72 hours. `invite_link` is that link only when no mail is
   * configured, in this answer only -- the caller shows it once and keeps it
   * nowhere else.
   */
  inviteUser(body: UserInvite): Promise<InviteOut> {
    return this.request<InviteOut>("/users/invite", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body) });
  }

  /** A fresh link (the old one stops working), emailed -- or, without mail, in `invite_link`, once. */
  resendInvite(userId: string): Promise<InviteLinkOut> {
    return this.request<InviteLinkOut>(`/users/${encodeURIComponent(userId)}/invite/resend`, { method: "POST" });
  }

  /** The invitation's link stops working at once. */
  cancelInvite(userId: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(`/users/${encodeURIComponent(userId)}/invite`, { method: "DELETE" });
  }

  /**
   * Reset another technician's second factors (design §7): their passkeys,
   * app and recovery codes stop working and their remembered devices are
   * forgotten; they register a new factor at their next sign-in. The server
   * answers 403 `step_up_required` unless YOUR OWN second factor was
   * confirmed in the last 10 minutes (§2.5): send it through `useStepUp().run`.
   */
  resetUserFactors(userId: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(`/users/${encodeURIComponent(userId)}/factors/reset`, { method: "POST" });
  }

  /** End every session the person has open. Their account stays active. */
  endUserSessions(userId: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.request<void>(`/users/${encodeURIComponent(userId)}/sessions`, { method: "DELETE" });
  }
```

```tsx
/**
 * The recent confirmation of the second factor (own authentication design
 * §2.5), as `useStepUp` answers the server's 403 `step_up_required`.
 *
 * THE SERVER DECIDES; THIS ONLY ANSWERS. Nothing here checks a clock or skips
 * a request: `run` sends it, and only that one refusal opens the dialog. What
 * is pinned is what a regression would turn into a security defect IN THE
 * CONSOLE: the request is sent again only after the server ACCEPTED the
 * factor, at most once, and never when the person closed the dialog; and
 * nothing typed survives the dialog.

import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from "@tanstack/react-query";
import { render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { useState } from "react";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { ApiError } from "../lib/api";
import { StepUpCancelled, isStepUpRequired, useStepUp } from "./stepUp";

const api = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  getMySecurity: vi.fn(),
  stepUpTotp: vi.fn(),
  stepUpPasskeyOptions: vi.fn(),
  stepUpPasskey: vi.fn(),
  stepUpRecovery: vi.fn(),
}));
vi.mock("../lib/ApiContext", () => ({ useApi: () => api }));

const { startAuthentication } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ startAuthentication: vi.fn() }));
vi.mock("@simplewebauthn/browser", () => ({ startAuthentication, startRegistration: vi.fn() }));

/** The server's answer to a change whose second factor is not fresh (Task 6). */
const REFUSED = () => new ApiError(403, JSON.stringify({ detail: { code: "step_up_required" } }));
const WRONG_CODE = () =>
  new ApiError(400, JSON.stringify({ detail: "That code is not right, or it was already used." }));
const OPTIONS = { challenge: "Y2hhbGxlbmdl", rpId: "itms.example.test", allowCredentials: [], userVerification: "required" };
const ASSERTION = {
  id: "Y3JlZA",
  rawId: "Y3JlZA",
  response: { clientDataJSON: "e30", authenticatorData: "YXV0aA", signature: "c2ln" },
  clientExtensionResults: {},
  type: "public-key",
};
/** A person with all three: a passkey, the app and three recovery codes. */
const EVERYTHING = {
  has_totp: true,
  passkeys: [{ id: "pk-1", name: "Laptop", created_at: "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z", last_used_at: null, backup_state: false }],
  recovery_codes_left: 3,
  trusted_devices: [],
  sessions: [],
};

/** A page that sends `action` through the hook and prints what came of it. */
function Probe({ action }: { action: () => Promise<string> }) {
  const stepUp = useStepUp();
  const [outcome, setOutcome] = useState("");
  return (
    <>
      <button
        type="button"
        onClick={() =>
          void stepUp.run(action).then(
            (value) => setOutcome(`done: ${value}`),
            (error: unknown) =>
              setOutcome(
                error instanceof StepUpCancelled
                  ? "cancelled"
                  : `failed: ${error instanceof ApiError ? error.status : "?"}`,
              ),
          )
        }
      >
        Go
      </button>
      <output>{outcome}</output>
      {stepUp.dialog}
    </>
  );
}

function renderProbe(action: () => Promise<string>) {
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({ defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } } });
  render(
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Probe action={action} />
    </QueryClientProvider>,
  );
  return userEvent.setup();
}

async function openConfirmation(user: ReturnType<typeof userEvent.setup>): Promise<HTMLElement> {
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Go" }));
  return screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Confirm it's you" });
}

describe("isStepUpRequired", () => {
  it("is the server's 403 step_up_required, in either body shape", () => {

    expect(isStepUpRequired(new ApiError(403, JSON.stringify({ code: "csrf" })))).toBe(false);
    expect(isStepUpRequired(new ApiError(401, JSON.stringify({ code: "step_up_required" })))).toBe(false);
    expect(isStepUpRequired(new ApiError(403, "<html>Forbidden</html>"))).toBe(false);
    expect(isStepUpRequired(new Error("step_up_required"))).toBe(false);

describe("useStepUp", () => {
```

Qué protege cada prueba (Step 7):

| Protección | Si se quita | Falla |
|---|---|---|
| `if (!isStepUpRequired(error)) throw error;` en `run` | todo fallo abriría el diálogo | «passes any other refusal…» |
| `await new Promise(...)` antes de `return action()` | se reenviaría sin la confirmación del servidor | «asks for a code…» (`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` antes de confirmar) |
| `onConfirmed()` solo tras `await confirm()` | un código rechazado dejaría pasar la escritura | «says a code the server refused…» |
| un solo `return action()`, sin recursión | bucle de confirmaciones | «returns a second refusal…» |
| `reject(new StepUpCancelled())` en `settle(false)` | la mutación quedaría colgada o reenviada | «rejects with StepUpCancelled…» |
| el `useEffect([open])` que vacía los campos | un código tecleado sobrevive al diálogo | «keeps nothing it was given…» |
| los métodos salen de `GET /me/security` | ofrecería lo que la persona no tiene | «offers only the second factors…» |
| `code.replace(/\s+/g, "")` y `recovery.trim()` | el servidor recibe espacios | «asks for a code…», «confirms with a recovery code» |
