- [ ] **Step 24: `SessionsTab.tsx`, la pestaña y sus textos**

Crear `frontend/src/modules/settings/SessionsTab.tsx`:

```tsx
// Sessions -- `GET /settings/sessions` (`orgs.manage`), `PUT /settings/sessions`
// (`orgs.manage` on EVERY client): how long a sign-in lasts (own
// authentication design §2.4, §2.6, §3). One setting for the whole
// organization, so the write needs the code on every client, like Email.
//
// SEVEN VALUES, AND THE BOUNDS ARE THE SERVER'S. The table's CHECK constraints
// (migration 0245) are restated in `SESSION_BOUNDS` only so a value out of
// range is refused before the round trip, with the range under its field;
// the server refuses it anyway. A save sends all seven.
//
// AFTER THE INACTIVITY TIME ONLY THE PASSWORD IS ASKED AGAIN; after the longest
// session, the second factor too (§2.4, what NIST allows at AAL2). The note
// under the technicians' two values says so in the operator's words.
//
// "REMEMBER THIS DEVICE" IS A TRADE THE OPERATOR MADE KNOWINGLY (design §0,
// S2b): on a remembered device the second factor is not asked until it
// expires, which is below AAL2. The warning under the switch says what that
// means, and the limits that bound it -- the person or an administrator can
// forget a device; a password change, a factor reset or a disable forgets
// them all -- are the server's.

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

import { Field, inputClass } from "../../components/ui";
import { useT } from "../../i18n/context";
import type { MessageKey } from "../../i18n/core";
import { FieldGroup, KIND_ICON, Panel, Toggle } from "../../shell/components";
import { Icon } from "../../shell/icons";
import { useGlobalWriteReason, useSessionSettings, useUpdateSessionSettingsMutation } from "./api";
import { FOLDING_FORM_GRID } from "./formGrid";
import { LoadFailure } from "./LoadFailure";
import { SaveBar } from "./SaveBar";
import { isDirty, isForbidden, parseIntegerField } from "./settingsState";
import {
  SESSION_BOUNDS,
  type SessionNumberKey,
  type SessionSettingsOut,
  type SessionSettingsUpdate,
} from "./types";

/** Read and write are the same code, as on the Email tab. */
export const SESSIONS_MANAGE = "orgs.manage";

type SessionsForm = Record<SessionNumberKey, string> & { remember_device_enabled: boolean };

const NUMBER_KEYS: readonly SessionNumberKey[] = [
  "staff_idle_minutes",
  "staff_max_hours",
  "remember_device_days",
  "remembered_max_hours",
  "contact_idle_minutes",
  "contact_max_days",
];

/** Each value's caption, and the unit its range is said in. */
const FIELD: Readonly<Record<SessionNumberKey, { label: MessageKey; range: MessageKey }>> = {
  staff_idle_minutes: { label: "settings.sessions.staffIdle", range: "settings.sessions.rangeMinutes" },
  staff_max_hours: { label: "settings.sessions.staffMax", range: "settings.sessions.rangeHours" },
  remember_device_days: { label: "settings.sessions.rememberDays", range: "settings.sessions.rangeDays" },
  remembered_max_hours: { label: "settings.sessions.rememberedMax", range: "settings.sessions.rangeHours" },
  contact_idle_minutes: { label: "settings.sessions.contactIdle", range: "settings.sessions.rangeMinutes" },
  contact_max_days: { label: "settings.sessions.contactMax", range: "settings.sessions.rangeDays" },
};

function seedFrom(data: SessionSettingsOut | undefined): SessionsForm {
  const text = (key: SessionNumberKey): string => (data ? String(data[key]) : "");
  return {
    staff_idle_minutes: text("staff_idle_minutes"),
    staff_max_hours: text("staff_max_hours"),
    remember_device_days: text("remember_device_days"),
    remembered_max_hours: text("remembered_max_hours"),
    contact_idle_minutes: text("contact_idle_minutes"),
    contact_max_days: text("contact_max_days"),
    remember_device_enabled: data?.remember_device_enabled ?? true,
  };
}

function inRange(key: SessionNumberKey, raw: string): boolean {
  const value = parseIntegerField(raw);
  const [min, max] = SESSION_BOUNDS[key];
  return value != null && value >= min && value <= max;
}

/** `canRead` reads the tab (`orgs.manage`); `canEdit` writes it: `orgs.manage` on every client. */
export function SessionsTab({ canRead, canEdit }: { canRead: boolean; canEdit: boolean }) {
  const t = useT();
  const reason = useGlobalWriteReason(SESSIONS_MANAGE);
  const settings = useSessionSettings(canRead);
  const update = useUpdateSessionSettingsMutation();

  const seed = seedFrom(settings.data);
  const [form, setForm] = useState<SessionsForm>(seed);
  const seedSignature = JSON.stringify(seed);
  useEffect(() => {
    setForm(JSON.parse(seedSignature) as SessionsForm);
  }, [seedSignature]);

  const forbidden = isForbidden(settings.error);
  const failed = settings.error != null && !forbidden;
  const dirty = isDirty(form, seed);
  const invalid = NUMBER_KEYS.filter((key) => !inRange(key, form[key]));
  const editable = canEdit && settings.data != null;

  function set<K extends keyof SessionsForm>(key: K, value: SessionsForm[K]) {
    setForm((current) => ({ ...current, [key]: value }));
  }

  function submit() {
    if (invalid.length > 0) return;
    const number = (key: SessionNumberKey): number => parseIntegerField(form[key]) as number;
    const body: SessionSettingsUpdate = {
      staff_idle_minutes: number("staff_idle_minutes"),
      staff_max_hours: number("staff_max_hours"),
      remember_device_enabled: form.remember_device_enabled,
      remember_device_days: number("remember_device_days"),
      remembered_max_hours: number("remembered_max_hours"),
      contact_idle_minutes: number("contact_idle_minutes"),
      contact_max_days: number("contact_max_days"),
    };
    update.mutate(body);
  }

  function numberField(key: SessionNumberKey, off = false) {
    const [min, max] = SESSION_BOUNDS[key];
    return (
      <Field key={key} label={t(FIELD[key].label)} help={t(FIELD[key].range, { min, max })}>
        <input
          className={inputClass}
          type="number"
          inputMode="numeric"
          min={min}
          max={max}
          value={form[key]}
          disabled={!editable || off}
          onChange={(event) => set(key, event.target.value)}
        />
      </Field>
    );
  }

  return (
    <Panel title={t("settings.sessions.title")} subtitle={t("settings.sessions.subtitle")}>
      {settings.isLoading ? (
        <p className="note">{t("settings.sessions.loading")}</p>
      ) : forbidden ? (
        <p className="note">{t("settings.sessions.forbidden", { code: SESSIONS_MANAGE })}</p>
      ) : failed ? (
        <LoadFailure error={settings.error} />
      ) : (
        <>
          <FieldGroup title={t("settings.sessions.groups.staff")} icon="users">
            <div className="form-grid" style={FOLDING_FORM_GRID}>
              {numberField("staff_idle_minutes")}
              {numberField("staff_max_hours")}
            </div>
            <p className="note" style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>
              {t("settings.sessions.staffNote")}
            </p>
          </FieldGroup>
          <FieldGroup title={t("settings.sessions.groups.remember")} icon="devices">
            <Toggle
              checked={form.remember_device_enabled}
              disabled={!editable}
              label={t("settings.sessions.rememberEnabled")}
              onChange={(next) => set("remember_device_enabled", next)}
            />
            <div className="form-grid" style={{ ...FOLDING_FORM_GRID, marginTop: 10 }}>
              {numberField("remember_device_days", !form.remember_device_enabled)}
              {numberField("remembered_max_hours", !form.remember_device_enabled)}
            </div>
            <p className="notice gold" style={{ marginTop: 10 }}>
              <Icon name={KIND_ICON.warn} size={16} />
              <span>{t("settings.sessions.rememberRisk")}</span>
            </p>
          </FieldGroup>
          <FieldGroup title={t("settings.sessions.groups.contacts")} icon="portal">
            <div className="form-grid" style={FOLDING_FORM_GRID}>
              {numberField("contact_idle_minutes")}
              {numberField("contact_max_days")}
            </div>
            <p className="note" style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>
              {t("settings.sessions.contactsNote")}
            </p>
          </FieldGroup>

          {invalid.length > 0 ? (
            <p className="form-error" style={{ marginTop: 10 }}>
              <Icon name={KIND_ICON.crit} size={13} /> {t("settings.sessions.outOfRange")}
            </p>
          ) : null}

          <SaveBar
            canEdit={editable && invalid.length === 0}
            disabledReason={canEdit ? t("settings.sessions.correct") : reason}
            dirty={dirty}
            pending={update.isPending}
            error={update.error}
            saved={update.isSuccess && !dirty}
            onSave={submit}
          />
        </>
      )}
    </Panel>
  );
}
```

`frontend/src/modules/settings/EmailTab.tsx`:

1. La cabecera `:1-43` entera pasa a:

```tsx
// Email — `GET /settings/email`, `PUT /settings/email`, `POST /settings/email/test`.
// Read and write are both `orgs.manage` (the write on every client).
//
// THE MAIL SERVER FOR INVITATIONS, PASSWORD RESETS AND ACCOUNT NOTICES (own
// authentication design §7). The platform sends them itself now; this used to
// be the identity provider's realm setting. Everything that matters about this
// form follows from the one thing that makes it awkward: THE SERVER NEVER
// RETURNS THE PASSWORD, and it is right not to -- it keeps it encrypted in the
// vault (invariant 3) and opens it only to send.
//
// So the box is always empty, and "Password: set" is the honest way to report a
// stored credential — a masked value would imply this console received
// something, and it did not. An untouched box sends NOTHING: the server reads an
// absent field as "keep what is stored". A form that sent `password: ""` would
// blank a working credential the first time somebody corrected the port, and the
// only symptom would be invitations that quietly stop arriving.
//
// THE TEST BUTTON REPORTS WHAT HAPPENED AND NOT MORE. The mail server accepting
// a message is not it delivering it — a relay that takes mail from an unknown
// sender and drops it silently is the common case, and this platform's own
// runbook already warns about it. So: "Sent to <mailbox> — check that mailbox",
// never a green tick. Each test opens a real conversation with the mail server,
// so the server allows five a minute per organization and says so in its own
// words when they are spent.
//
// THE TEST GOES WHERE THE OPERATOR SAYS, WITHIN THEIR OWN DOMAINS. The box is
// pre-filled with the operator's own address tagged `+itms-test`, which lands
// in the same inbox on Microsoft 365 and Gmail and is easy to find there. The
// server refuses any address other than the sending address, the operator's
// own mailbox, or the organization's sign-in domain (`app/core/mail.py`), so
// this box is not a way to mail strangers.
//
// TLS IS ONE CHOICE OF THREE, not two independent switches. A configuration
// carrying both StartTLS and SSL leaves the relay to decide what was meant.
//
// AUTHENTICATION FOLLOWS THE USERNAME. There is no separate "authenticate"
// toggle, because "authenticate, as nobody" is not a state worth being able to
// save.
//
// SIGN-IN IS A PASSWORD OR A MICROSOFT 365 APPLICATION. For Microsoft the
// platform fetches a token for each message at Microsoft's own address,
// `login.microsoftonline.com/<directory>`, built from the directory ID and
// nowhere else -- the server refuses any other address with 422, because it is
// where the client secret is presented -- so there is no field for it. The
// client secret follows the password's rule exactly (never shown, sent only
// when typed). Switching modes replaces the other credential server-side, so
// the console says so before the save. Design:
// docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-11-mail-oauth-design.md §3.
```

```tsx
/**
 * THE VAULT ASKS FOR THE SECOND FACTOR AGAIN (own authentication design §2.5,
 * falsifier 5). A checkout whose second factor was not confirmed in the last
 * 10 minutes is the server's 403 `step_up_required`; the page asks for it and
 * sends the checkout once more only after the server accepted it. The secret
 * appears only in the answer to that second, accepted checkout.
 */
describe("CredentialsPage — a checkout asks for the second factor again when the server says so", () => {
  const SECURITY = { has_totp: true, passkeys: [], recovery_codes_left: 0, trusted_devices: [], sessions: [] };
  const STALE = () => new ApiError(403, JSON.stringify({ detail: { code: "step_up_required" } }));

  async function askToReveal(user: ReturnType<typeof userEvent.setup>) {
    await screen.findByText("Domain support admin");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: /check out/i }));
    await user.type(screen.getByPlaceholderText(/helpdesk ticket/i), "helpdesk ticket 4821");
    await user.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Reveal" }));
  }

  it("confirms the factor, then reveals", async () => {

    const checkoutCredential = vi
      .fn()
      .mockRejectedValueOnce(STALE())
      .mockResolvedValueOnce({ secret: "sup3r-s3cr3t-value" });
    const stepUpTotp = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    renderPage({
      listCredentials: () => Promise.resolve([credential()]),
      checkoutCredential,
      getMySecurity: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(SECURITY),
      stepUpTotp,
    });
    await askToReveal(user);

    const confirm = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Confirm it's you" });
    expect(screen.queryByText("sup3r-s3cr3t-value")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
    await user.type(await within(confirm).findByLabelText("Code from your authenticator app"), "123456");
    await user.click(within(confirm).getByRole("button", { name: "Confirm" }));

    expect(await screen.findByText("sup3r-s3cr3t-value")).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(stepUpTotp).toHaveBeenCalledExactlyOnceWith("123456");
    expect(checkoutCredential).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    expect(checkoutCredential).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(credential().id, "helpdesk ticket 4821", null);
  });

  it("reveals nothing when the confirmation is closed, and says nothing changed", async () => {
    const user = userEvent.setup();
    const checkoutCredential = vi.fn().mockRejectedValue(STALE());
    renderPage({
      listCredentials: () => Promise.resolve([credential()]),
      checkoutCredential,
      getMySecurity: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(SECURITY),
      stepUpTotp: vi.fn(),
    });
    await askToReveal(user);

    const confirm = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: "Confirm it's you" });
    await user.click(within(confirm).getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" }));

    const checkout = screen.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Check out Domain support admin" });
    expect(await within(checkout).findByText(/Nothing was changed: the confirmation was closed\./)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(checkoutCredential).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
    expect(screen.queryByText("sup3r-s3cr3t-value")).not.toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});
```

**Decisión del plan (1): el Bearer de la consola sale de las tres puertas, no solo de `admit()`.** La interfaz habla
de `admit()`, pero `/ws` (`ws.py:132-138`) y la pantalla remota (`tunnel.py:114-115`) validan el mismo token de la
consola con `require_console_token`: `tests/test_token_origin.py:14-18` lo llama «every non-MCP door». Dejarlo en
los sockets sería dejar Keycloak en el camino de la consola, contra el Goal del plan. `require_console_token` y
`app/core/ws_auth.py` quedan sin llamadas y se borran; `validate_token`, `JwksCache`, `require_person_mcp_token`,
`oidc_console_client_id` y el rechazo de doble audiencia (`deps.py:211-215`) se quedan para MCP.

**Decisión del plan (2): en el canal MCP la puerta no lee la cookie ni el token interno.** 1c(a): «The session is
the person, and only OAuth makes one». La Task 6 ya lee la cookie solo dentro de `if call is None:`; esta tarea lo
fija con una prueba y añade la otra mitad: en el canal, una petición que diga ser el asistente es un 401. Las dos
pruebas están en `test_auth_falsifiers.py`.

**Decisión del plan (2b): `require_step_up` deja de dejar pasar a quien no tiene sesión.** La Task 6 lo dejó así
para el Bearer de la consola (su decisión (10)) y pidió que esta tarea lo hiciera estricto. Desde aquí solo MCP
entra sin sesión, y MCP nunca llega a una acción de §2.5 (`MCP_FORBIDDEN_CODES`, `NEVER_EXPOSED`); si llegara, un
403 `step_up_required` es la dirección correcta del error.

**Decisión del plan (3): el `Origin` de las pruebas sigue a la consola configurada.** Muchas pruebas cambian
`public_console_url` a mitad de camino (`tests/test_install_link_msi.py:166` a `https://10.0.0.5`,
`tests/email_oauth_env.py:157` a `https://itms.example`, `tests/test_email_intake_oauth_app.py:32`, …). Un
navegador manda el origen de la página que tiene abierta, y la página está en la consola configurada. Por eso el
cliente de `api_env` lleva un *event hook* de httpx que cambia un `Origin` igual a `CONSOLE` (Task 6,
`https://itms.test`) por el origen actual de `settings.public_console_url`. Un `Origin` distinto (`null`, otro sitio) o ausente no se toca: las
pruebas del falsificador 7 los mandan a propósito. Con `public_console_url` en `None` no hay origen al que
seguir, y la regla CSRF (Task 6) rechaza: es lo que pasa en producción.

**Decisión del plan (4): tres pruebas que ejercían la negativa de una ruta con `ITS_PUBLIC_CONSOLE_URL` sin fijar
pasan a quitarle la dirección solo a la ruta.** Con la cookie, una escritura sin consola configurada la rechaza la
regla CSRF antes de llegar a la ruta, así que la negativa propia de la ruta ya no se alcanza poniendo `None` en los
Settings. Las tres siguen probando lo mismo cambiando solo la costura: se envuelve la función de servicio que la
ruta llama para que reciba `None` (Step 10). La consola configurada solo la ven la ruta CSRF y el navegador.

**Decisión del plan (5): los falsificadores van en un archivo propio, por HTTP.** Las Tasks 4-8 ya prueban cada
pieza por separado; `tests/test_auth_falsifiers.py` los prueba como los ve un navegador, después del cambio a la
cookie, y cada prueba dice qué protección sostiene. Falsificador 2, «en el mismo tiempo»: medir tiempos en CI es
ruidoso; se prueba el mecanismo que lo garantiza — exista o no la cuenta, el servidor hace exactamente una
verificación argon2 —, que falla si alguien quita el hash de relleno. Falsificador 4: la mitad del servidor (la
plataforma pasa `require_user_verification=True` siempre, D22) en pytest; la mitad del navegador en el job
`webauthn-uv`. Ese job usa py_webauthn con los mismos argumentos, no las rutas, porque una sesión de navegador
contra el servidor completo necesita una base de datos que el job no tiene.

**Pruebas que cambian a propósito** (la Step 6 a la Step 10 dan cada una, antiguo → nuevo): las que afirmaban que
la consola admite un Bearer pasan a afirmar que no lo admite; las que probaban propiedades del Bearer de consola
que siguen existiendo en MCP (refresco del correo desde el claim, auto-alta por `sub`, orden org/dominio) pasan al
canal MCP; las que solo usaban un Bearer para entrar pasan a la cookie. Ninguna se borra ni se salta.

```python
(`frontend/scripts/webauthn-uv.mjs`).

PASSWORD = "correct horse battery staple 12"
NEW_PASSWORD = "a different passphrase for 2026"
APP = Path(app_package.__file__).resolve().parent


class _Browser:
    """One browser on the console: it keeps the cookies the platform sets and
    sends them back, with the console's CSRF header and Origin."""

    def __init__(self, env: Any) -> None:
        self.env = env
        self.jar: dict[str, str] = {}

    async def send(self, method: str, path: str, body: Any = None) -> httpx.Response:
        headers = console_headers()
        if self.jar:
            headers["Cookie"] = "; ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in self.jar.items())
        response = await self.env.client.request(method, path, json=body, headers=headers)
        for line in response.headers.get_list("set-cookie"):
            name, _, rest = line.partition("=")
            value, _, attributes = rest.partition(";")
            if value == "" or "max-age=0" in attributes.lower().replace(" ", ""):
                self.jar.pop(name.strip(), None)
            else:
                self.jar[name.strip()] = value.strip()
        return response

    async def post(self, path: str, body: Any = None) -> httpx.Response:
        return await self.send("POST", path, body)

    async def login(self, email: str, password: str) -> httpx.Response:
        return await self.post("/api/v1/auth/login", {"email": email, "password": password})


async def _staff(env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> tuple[UUID, UUID, str]:
    """`(org, user, email)` of an org-admin with a password and no factor yet.
    Sign-in looks the person up in the deployment's org (D2), so the test org
    becomes it."""
    org_id = await env.create_org("falsifier")
    monkeypatch.setattr(env.settings, "default_org_slug", await env.org_slug(org_id))
    sub = await env.create_user(org_id, "org-admin")
    stored, version = await hash_password(org_id, PASSWORD)
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        user = (
            await session.execute(select(User).where(User.external_subject == sub))
        ).scalar_one()
        session.add(
            AuthPassword(
                user_id=user.id,
                org_id=org_id,
                hash=stored,
                pepper_version=version,
                changed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
            )
        )
        await session.commit()
        return org_id, user.id, user.email


async def _enrol(browser: _Browser, email: str) -> tuple[Any, list[str]]:
    """The first sign-in: password, TOTP enrolment, recovery codes. Returns the
    TOTP generator and the codes; the browser holds a complete session."""
    first = await browser.login(email, PASSWORD)
    assert first.json() == {"state": "enroll_required"}, first.text
    started = await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/enroll/totp/start")
    assert started.status_code == 200, started.text
    totp = pyotp.parse_uri(started.json()["otpauth_uri"])
    confirmed = await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/enroll/totp/confirm", {"code": totp.now()})
    assert confirmed.status_code < 300, confirmed.text
    finished = await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/enroll/finish")
    assert finished.status_code == 200, finished.text
    codes: list[str] = finished.json()["recovery_codes"]
    assert len(codes) == 10
    return totp, codes


def _next_code(totp: Any) -> str:
    """The code of the NEXT 30-second step: enrolment consumed the current one,
    and ±1 step is accepted (design §2.2)."""
    return str(totp.at(int(time.time()) + 30))


async def _mark_step_up(env: Any, user_id: UUID) -> None:
    async with AsyncSession(env.admin_engine) as session:
        await session.execute(
            update(AuthSession)
            .where(AuthSession.user_id == user_id, AuthSession.ended_at.is_(None))
            .values(step_up_at=datetime.now(UTC))
        )
        await session.commit()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Falsifier 1: one org's session reads nothing of another's; a contact's
# session never passes the console's door.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def test_falsifier_1_a_session_of_one_org_reads_nothing_of_another(api_env: Any) -> None:
    """Holds the session -> org binding (`its_auth_session` returns the
    session's own org) and RLS on `auth_sessions`."""
    mine, theirs = await seed_org(api_env, "f1-mine"), await seed_org(api_env, "f1-theirs")
    sub = await api_env.create_user(mine.org_id, "org-admin")
    headers = await api_env.headers(mine.org_id, sub)
    other = await api_env.create_user(theirs.org_id, "org-admin")
    await sign_in(api_env, theirs.org_id, other)

    listed = await api_env.client.get("/api/v1/devices", headers=headers)
    one = await api_env.client.get(f"/api/v1/devices/{theirs.device_id}", headers=headers)

    assert listed.status_code == 200, listed.text
    assert str(mine.device_id) in listed.text
    assert str(theirs.device_id) not in listed.text
    assert one.status_code == 404
    async with org_session(
        mine.org_id, engine=api_env.app_engine, clients=ClientScope.all()
    ) as session:
        seen = set((await session.execute(select(AuthSession.org_id))).scalars())
    assert seen == {mine.org_id}


async def test_falsifier_1_a_contact_session_does_not_pass_the_console_door(api_env: Any) -> None:
    """Holds `contact_refusal` on the session path of `admit(contacts=False)`."""
    org_id = await api_env.create_org("f1-contact")
    sub = f"contact-pending:{uuid4()}"
    async with AsyncSession(api_env.admin_engine) as session:
        client = Client(org_id=org_id, name="Acme", kind="customer")
        session.add(client)
        await session.flush()
        session.add(
            User(
                org_id=org_id,
                external_subject=sub,
                email=f"cam-{uuid4().hex[:6]}@acme.example",
                kind="contact",
                client_id=client.id,
            )
        )
        await session.commit()
    signed = await sign_in(api_env, org_id, sub)

    me = await api_env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=signed.headers)

    assert me.status_code == 403

) -> None:
    """Holds the dummy verification for an unknown address: without it the
    unknown account is answered faster -- zero argon2 verifications against
    one -- which is the timing oracle §2.3 forbids."""
    _, _, email = await _staff(api_env, monkeypatch)
    verifications: list[int] = []
    real = argon2.PasswordHasher.verify

    def counted(self: argon2.PasswordHasher, hash: str | bytes, password: str | bytes) -> Any:
        verifications.append(1)
        return real(self, hash, password)

    monkeypatch.setattr(argon2.PasswordHasher, "verify", counted)
    browser = _Browser(api_env)

    wrong = "a wrong but long enough password"
    known = await browser.login(email, wrong)
    after_known = len(verifications)
    unknown = await browser.login(f"nobody-{uuid4().hex[:6]}@test.local", wrong)

    assert known.status_code == unknown.status_code
    assert known.status_code >= 400
    assert known.json() == unknown.json()
    assert after_known == 1
    assert len(verifications) == 2


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Falsifier 3: at 100 failures the factor is disabled; a TOTP code is never
# accepted twice.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def test_falsifier_3_the_hundredth_failure_disables_the_factor(
    api_env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Holds `DISABLE_AT = 100` and the check that a disabled factor refuses a
    RIGHT code too (`failures.check_allowed`)."""
    org_id, user_id, email = await _staff(api_env, monkeypatch)
    browser = _Browser(api_env)
    totp, _ = await _enrol(browser, email)
    await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/logout")
    assert (await browser.login(email, PASSWORD)).json()["state"] == "factor_required"
    async with AsyncSession(api_env.admin_engine) as session:
        await session.merge(
            AuthFailure(
                org_id=org_id,
                user_id=user_id,
                factor="totp",
                consecutive=99,
                last_failed_at=datetime.now(UTC) - timedelta(days=1),
                disabled_at=None,
            )
        )
        await session.commit()
    valid = {str(totp.at(int(time.time()) + 30 * k)) for k in (-1, 0, 1, 2)}
    wrong = next(code for code in ("000000", "111111", "222222", "333333") if code not in valid)

    refused = await browser.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/factor/totp", {"code": wrong, "remember_device": False}
    )
    right = await browser.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/factor/totp", {"code": _next_code(totp), "remember_device": False}
    )

    assert refused.status_code >= 400
    assert right.status_code >= 400 and right.json().get("state") != "signed_in"
    async with AsyncSession(api_env.admin_engine) as session:
        row = await session.get(AuthFailure, (user_id, "totp"))
        assert row is not None and row.consecutive >= 100 and row.disabled_at is not None
        disabled = (
            await session.execute(
                select(func.count())
                .select_from(AuditEvent)
                .where(AuditEvent.org_id == org_id, AuditEvent.action == "auth.factor_disabled")
            )
        ).scalar_one()
    assert disabled == 1


async def test_falsifier_3_a_totp_code_is_not_accepted_twice(
    api_env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Holds `last_step` (design §2.2: pyotp 2.10.0 does not refuse a replay)."""
    _, _, email = await _staff(api_env, monkeypatch)
    browser = _Browser(api_env)
    totp, _ = await _enrol(browser, email)
    code = _next_code(totp)

    await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/logout")
    await browser.login(email, PASSWORD)
    first = await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/factor/totp", {"code": code, "remember_device": False})
    await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/logout")
    await browser.login(email, PASSWORD)
    again = await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/factor/totp", {"code": code, "remember_device": False})

    assert first.json() == {"state": "signed_in"}, first.text
    assert again.status_code >= 400 and again.json().get("state") != "signed_in"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Falsifier 4 (server half): every passkey check requires user verification.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def test_falsifier_4_every_passkey_check_requires_user_verification(
    api_env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Holds D22: py_webauthn's `require_user_verification` defaults to False,
    and the platform passes True on BOTH ceremonies; the options ask for it too.
    The verifier is replaced by a spy that records what it was given."""
    seen: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}

    def spy(name: str) -> Any:
        def recorded(**kwargs: Any) -> Any:
            seen[name] = kwargs
            raise ValueError("stopped by the spy")

        return recorded

    for name in ("verify_registration_response", "verify_authentication_response"):
        monkeypatch.setattr(webauthn, name, spy(name))
        monkeypatch.setattr(passkeys, name, spy(name), raising=False)
    org_id = await api_env.create_org("f4")
    sub = await api_env.create_user(org_id, "org-admin")
    rp_id = "itms.test"

    def b64(data: bytes) -> str:
        return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).rstrip(b"=").decode()

    async with AsyncSession(api_env.admin_engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:
        user = (
            await session.execute(select(User).where(User.external_subject == sub))
        ).scalar_one()
        created = await passkeys.registration_options(session, user, rp_id=rp_id, rp_name="ITMS")
        assert created["authenticatorSelection"]["userVerification"] == "required"
        client_data = b64(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "type": "webauthn.create",
                    "challenge": created["challenge"],
                    "origin": CONSOLE,
                }
            ).encode()
        )
        # The spy stops the ceremony; whatever the platform turns that into is
        # beside the point -- what it HANDED the verifier is the assertion.
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
            await passkeys.verify_registration(
                session,
                user,
                {
                    "id": b64(b"\x01" * 16),
                    "rawId": b64(b"\x01" * 16),
                    "type": "public-key",
                    "response": {"clientDataJSON": client_data, "attestationObject": b64(b"\x00")},
                    "clientExtensionResults": {},
                },
                name="spy",
                expected_origin=CONSOLE,
                rp_id=rp_id,
            )
        session.add(
            AuthPasskey(
                org_id=org_id,
                user_id=user.id,
                credential_id=b"\x02" * 16,
                public_key=b"\x00",
                sign_count=0,
                transports=["internal"],
                backup_eligible=False,
                backup_state=False,
                name="spy",
                created_at=datetime.now(UTC),
            )
        )
        await session.flush()
        asked = await passkeys.authentication_options(
            session, user.id, org_id=org_id, rp_id=rp_id, purpose="authenticate"
        )
        assert asked["userVerification"] == "required"
        assertion = b64(
            json.dumps(
                {"type": "webauthn.get", "challenge": asked["challenge"], "origin": CONSOLE}
            ).encode()
        )
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
            await passkeys.verify_authentication(
                session,
                {
                    "id": b64(b"\x02" * 16),
                    "rawId": b64(b"\x02" * 16),
                    "type": "public-key",
                    "response": {
                        "clientDataJSON": assertion,
                        "authenticatorData": b64(b"\x00" * 37),
                        "signature": b64(b"\x00"),
                        "userHandle": None,
                    },
                    "clientExtensionResults": {},
                },
                expected_origin=CONSOLE,
                rp_id=rp_id,
                purpose="authenticate",
            )

    assert seen["verify_registration_response"]["require_user_verification"] is True
    assert seen["verify_authentication_response"]["require_user_verification"] is True


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Falsifier 5: a remembered device stops counting when the password changes;
# the vault still asks for the second factor.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


async def test_falsifier_5_the_vault_asks_and_the_device_forgets(
    api_env: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Holds two lines: the step-up gate on `POST /credentials/{id}/checkout`
    (design §2.5, §2.6: a remembered device skips the factor at sign-in, never
    at the vault) and the device revocation in `PUT /me/password`."""
    _, user_id, email = await _staff(api_env, monkeypatch)
    browser = _Browser(api_env)
    _, codes = await _enrol(browser, email)
    made = await browser.post(
        "/api/v1/credentials", {"name": "f5", "type": "password", "secret": "s3cret-value"}
    )
    assert made.status_code == 201, made.text
    credential = made.json()["id"]
    await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/logout")
    await browser.login(email, PASSWORD)
    remembered = await browser.post(
        "/api/v1/auth/factor/recovery", {"code": codes[0], "remember_device": True}
    )
    assert remembered.json() == {"state": "signed_in"}, remembered.text
    device = browser.jar[DEVICE_COOKIE]
    await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/logout")
    browser.jar[DEVICE_COOKIE] = device

    # The device counts: no second factor at sign-in...
    assert (await browser.login(email, PASSWORD)).json() == {"state": "signed_in"}
    # ...and still none at the vault.
    asked = await browser.post(f"/api/v1/credentials/{credential}/checkout", {"reason": "f5"})
    assert asked.status_code == 403
    assert refusal_code(asked) == "step_up_required"
    await _mark_step_up(api_env, user_id)
    opened = await browser.post(f"/api/v1/credentials/{credential}/checkout", {"reason": "f5"})
    assert opened.status_code == 200, opened.text

    changed = await browser.send(
        "PUT", "/api/v1/me/password", {"current": PASSWORD, "new": NEW_PASSWORD}
    )
    assert changed.status_code < 300, changed.text
    await browser.post("/api/v1/auth/logout")
    browser.jar[DEVICE_COOKIE] = device

    after = await browser.login(email, NEW_PASSWORD)

    assert after.json()["state"] == "factor_required", after.text


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Falsifier 7: a cookie write without the custom header, or with Origin null,
# is refused.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "spoil",
    [
        pytest.param(lambda h: h.pop("X-ITMS-Request"), id="no-custom-header"),
        pytest.param(lambda h: h.update({"Origin": "null"}), id="origin-null"),
        pytest.param(lambda h: h.pop("Origin"), id="no-origin"),
        pytest.param(lambda h: h.update({"Origin": "https://evil.example"}), id="foreign-origin"),
    ],
)
async def test_falsifier_7_a_cookie_write_without_its_proof_of_origin_is_refused(
    api_env: Any, spoil: Any
) -> None:
    """Holds `RequireConsoleRequestHeader` (Task 6). The control is the same
    write with the headers a console sends."""
    org_id = await api_env.create_org("f7")
    sub = await api_env.create_user(org_id, "read-only")
    headers = await api_env.headers(org_id, sub)
    spoiled = dict(headers)
    spoil(spoiled)

    refused = await api_env.client.patch("/api/v1/me", headers=spoiled, json={"phone": "+57 1"})
    allowed = await api_env.client.patch("/api/v1/me", headers=headers, json={"phone": "+57 2"})

    assert refused.status_code == 403
    assert refusal_code(refused) == "csrf"
    assert allowed.status_code == 200, allowed.text
    assert allowed.json()["phone"] == "+57 2"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Falsifier 9: the recovery command does not exist over HTTP.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #


def test_falsifier_9_the_recovery_command_has_no_http_route(api_env: Any) -> None:
    """Holds design §7: `python -m app.core.auth.recover` only. A route that
    imported it, or a path that named it, would turn shell access into an
    HTTP request."""
    recover = APP / "core" / "auth" / "recover.py"
    assert recover.exists()
    assert "APIRouter" not in recover.read_text()
    # Word-bounded: `from app.core.auth import recovery` (the recovery CODES,
    # Task 4) is not the recovery COMMAND.
    names_it = re.compile(r"app\.core\.auth\.recover\b|\bimport recover\b")
    importers = [
        str(path.relative_to(APP))
        for path in sorted(APP.rglob("*.py"))
        if path != recover and names_it.search(path.read_text())
    ]
    assert importers == []
    routes = _flatten(api_env.app)
    assert routes, "the router walk found nothing; the next assertion would be vacuous"
    assert [
        path for _, path in routes if "recover" in path and "recovery" not in path
    ] == []

async def test_the_console_bearer_opens_no_console_door(api_env: Any) -> None:
    """The token the console used to send -- issued to `it-suite-web` -- is no
    credential at /api/v1 any more; the same person by cookie is the control."""
    org_id = await api_env.create_org("door")
    sub = await api_env.create_user(org_id, "org-admin")
    token = api_env.idp.token(sub, await api_env.org_slug(org_id), email=f"{sub}@test.local")

    by_bearer = await api_env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
    by_cookie = await api_env.client.get("/api/v1/me", headers=await api_env.headers(org_id, sub))

    assert by_bearer.status_code == 401
    assert refusal_code(by_bearer) == "auth_required"
    assert by_cookie.status_code == 200, by_cookie.text


async def test_the_mcp_channel_takes_no_cookie(api_env: Any) -> None:
    """1c(a): on the MCP channel only an OAuth token makes a session."""
    org_id = await api_env.create_org("door-mcp")
    sub = await api_env.create_user(org_id, "org-admin")
    signed = await sign_in(api_env, org_id, sub)

    async with marked_client(api_env) as client:
        me = await client.get("/api/v1/me", headers={"Cookie": cookie_header(signed.token)})

    assert me.status_code == 401


def test_require_step_up_admits_no_request_without_a_session() -> None:
    """Decision (2b): the Bearer pass Task 6 left in `require_step_up` is gone.
    The control is a session confirmed a moment ago."""
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    fresh = SessionPrincipal(
        session_id=uuid4(),
        user_id=uuid4(),
        org_id=uuid4(),
        kind="staff",
        factor_done=True,
        step_up_at=now,
        email="ada@test.local",
        display_name="Ada",
        expires_at=now + timedelta(hours=1),
    )

    def ctx(principal: SessionPrincipal | None) -> AuthContext:
        claims = None if principal else TokenClaims(sub="s", email="", name="", org_slug="o")
        return AuthContext(
            org_id=uuid4(),
            user_id=uuid4(),
            claims=claims,
            clients=ClientScope.all(),
            principal=principal,
        )

    require_step_up(ctx(fresh), now=now)
    with pytest.raises(AuthRefusal) as refused:
        require_step_up(ctx(None), now=now)
    assert (refused.value.status_code, refused.value.code) == (403, "step_up_required")
```

```python
async def session_screen(websocket: WebSocket, session_id: UUID) -> None:
    """Browser-facing rsp/1 stream for a screen session.

    Admission: the console's session cookie with the console's ``Origin``
    (P2 design §6.5), then ``remote.control`` and owner-or-admin, all
    server-side. The browser sends and receives rsp/1 frames as binary
    messages; text messages are ignored.
    """
    state = websocket.app.state
    if SESSION_COOKIE not in websocket.cookies:
        # No credential at all: 4401, as on the live socket.
        await websocket.close(code=4401)
        return
    try:
        # The person admitted is the viewer, whose closing the viewer is
        # their own act (phase 3 design §5.3): the owner, or a supervisor.
        org_id, viewer_id, _clients = await authorize_tunnel_session(
            connection=websocket,
            session_id=session_id,
            settings=state.settings,
            app_engine=state.app_engine,
        )
```

```python
async def loopback_authorization(request: Request) -> str:
    """The `Authorization` value an assistant turn's loopback calls carry: a
    token minted from the session that admitted the turn's own request
    (`admit()` leaves it on `request.state`). The assistant's routes are not
    MCP tools (`app/mcp/exclusions.py:144-151`), so that request always came
    with a session."""
    principal: SessionPrincipal | None = getattr(request.state, "session_principal", None)
    if principal is None:
        raise _refused("an assistant turn with no session")
    if getattr(request.state, "via_loopback", False):
        raise _refused("a loopback call mints no loopback token")
    return f"Bearer {await mint_loopback(principal)}"
```

```python
    async def headers(self, org_id: UUID, sub: str) -> dict[str, str]:
        """What a browser signed in to the console sends, for a user `create_user`

        A NEW, COMPLETE SESSION PER CALL, with a recent confirmation of the second
        factor, made by the real `start_session` (`tests/session_support.py::sign_in`):
        the cookie as an explicit `Cookie` header -- httpx's jar will not send a
        `Secure` / `__Host-` cookie to `http://api.test` --, `X-ITMS-Request: 1`
        and the console's `Origin`, which the CSRF rule requires on every write.
        The client of `api_env` keeps that Origin pointed at whatever console the
        test has configured (`_browser_origin` below).

        Until own authentication phase 1 this minted a Keycloak token whose email
        claim had to match the seeded row (see git history); the session carries
        no claim, so the row is the only address there is.
        """
        from tests.session_support import sign_in

        return (await sign_in(self, org_id, sub, step_up=True)).headers

    async def loopback_bearer(self, org_id: UUID, sub: str) -> str:
        """The `Authorization` an assistant turn of this person carries: a token
        minted from a new session of theirs (design §5.6). For tests that build a
        `TurnContext` or call an executor directly."""
        from app.core.auth.loopback import mint_loopback
        from tests.session_support import principal_for, sign_in

        signed = await sign_in(self, org_id, sub)
        return f"Bearer {await mint_loopback(await principal_for(self, signed.session_id))}"
```

En el fixture `api_env` (`:314-336`): importar `from urllib.parse import urlsplit` y
`from tests.session_support import CONSOLE`; añadir `public_console_url=CONSOLE` a `Settings(...)` (el valor de
`use_console`, que las pruebas de las Tasks 6-9 siguen llamando sin efecto nuevo); y construir el cliente con el
*hook*:

```python
    async def _browser_origin(request: httpx.Request) -> None:
        """A browser sends the origin of the page it is on, and the page is the
        console the deployment is configured at. So an `Origin` the harness put
        there (`CONSOLE`) follows `settings.public_console_url` when a test
        changes it; a different one (`null`, another site) or none at all is
        left exactly as the test wrote it. With no console configured there is
        no origin to follow, and the CSRF rule refuses -- as in production."""
        if request.headers.get("Origin") != CONSOLE:
            return
        parts = urlsplit((settings.public_console_url or "").strip())
        if parts.scheme and parts.netloc:
            request.headers["Origin"] = f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}"

    app = create_app(settings, jwks_http_client=jwks_client(idp))
    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(
            transport=httpx.ASGITransport(app=app),
            base_url="http://api.test",
            event_hooks={"request": [_browser_origin]},
        ) as client:
            yield ApiEnv(app, client, idp, settings, admin_engine, app_engine)
```

- [ ] **Step 13: Falsificador 4 en el navegador**

Crear `backend/tests/webauthn_uv_probe.py`:

```python
"""py_webauthn's half of falsifier 4's browser check (`frontend/scripts/webauthn-uv.mjs`).

Not a test module (no `test_` prefix); the `webauthn-uv` CI job runs it. Two
commands, JSON on stdout:

    python -m tests.webauthn_uv_probe options <rp_id> <required|discouraged>
    python -m tests.webauthn_uv_probe verify <origin> <rp_id>     # stdin: {"options", "credential"}

`verify` passes `require_user_verification=True`, which is what
`app.core.auth.passkeys` passes on every ceremony (D22) --
`tests/test_auth_falsifiers.py::test_falsifier_4_every_passkey_check_requires_user_verification`
holds that half.
"""

import json
import sys
from typing import Any

from webauthn import (
    base64url_to_bytes,
    generate_registration_options,
    options_to_json,
    verify_registration_response,
)
from webauthn.helpers.structs import (
    AttestationConveyancePreference,
    AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria,
    ResidentKeyRequirement,
    UserVerificationRequirement,
)


def _options(rp_id: str, user_verification: str) -> str:
    options = generate_registration_options(
        rp_id=rp_id,
        rp_name="ITMS",
        user_name="uv@itms.test",
        user_display_name="UV probe",
        attestation=AttestationConveyancePreference.NONE,
        authenticator_selection=AuthenticatorSelectionCriteria(
            resident_key=ResidentKeyRequirement.PREFERRED,
            user_verification=UserVerificationRequirement(user_verification),
        ),
    )
    return options_to_json(options)


def _verify(origin: str, rp_id: str, body: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    try:
        verify_registration_response(
            credential=body["credential"],
            expected_challenge=base64url_to_bytes(body["options"]["challenge"]),
            expected_origin=origin,
            expected_rp_id=rp_id,
            require_user_verification=True,
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - the refusal IS the output
        return {"accepted": False, "error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}
    return {"accepted": True}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) == 3 and argv[0] == "options":
        print(_options(argv[1], argv[2]))
        return 0
    if len(argv) == 3 and argv[0] == "verify":
        print(json.dumps(_verify(argv[1], argv[2], json.load(sys.stdin))))
        return 0
    print(__doc__, file=sys.stderr)
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

Crear `frontend/scripts/webauthn-uv.mjs`:

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Falsifier 4 of the own-authentication design (§10), in a real browser:
 * "Una llave de acceso sin verificación del usuario se rechaza. En la CI, con
 * el autenticador virtual de Chromium."
 *
 * Two ceremonies, each against options py_webauthn generates and judged by
 * py_webauthn with `require_user_verification=True`
 * (`backend/tests/webauthn_uv_probe.py`), the argument the platform passes:
 *
 *   1. CONTROL. An authenticator that verifies the user, options asking for it:
 *      the response carries UV=1 and must be ACCEPTED. Without it, step 2
 *      could pass because nothing verifies at all.
 *   2. FALSIFIER. An authenticator that cannot verify the user, and a client
 *      that rewrote the options to `userVerification: "discouraged"` -- what a
 *      hostile page or extension can do, since the server never sees the
 *      options the browser used. The response carries UV=0 and must be
 *      REFUSED, for that reason and no other.
 *
 * The page is http://localhost:<port>/, a secure context (WebAuthn requires
 * one) whose RP ID is "localhost". Playwright is resolved from a global
 * install, as scripts/a11y-browser.mjs resolves it, and for the same reason.
 *
 * Two authenticators rather than `WebAuthn.setUserVerified` on one: with UV
 * required and verification failing, Chromium rejects the ceremony in the
 * browser, so no UV=0 response would ever reach the verifier.
 */
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";
import { dirname, join, resolve } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const FRONTEND = resolve(HERE, "..");
const BACKEND = resolve(FRONTEND, "..", "backend");
const PYTHON = process.env.ITS_PYTHON ?? join(BACKEND, ".venv", "bin", "python");
const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const GLOBAL_MODULES = join(dirname(dirname(process.execPath)), "lib/node_modules");

async function loadPlaywright() {
  for (const spec of [
    "playwright",
    join(GLOBAL_MODULES, "playwright/index.mjs"),
    "/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs",
    "/usr/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs",
    "/usr/local/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs",
  ]) {
    try {
      const mod = await import(spec.startsWith("/") ? spec : require.resolve(spec, { paths: [FRONTEND] }));
      return mod.chromium ? mod : mod.default;
    } catch {
      /* try the next one */
    }
  }
  throw new Error("playwright is not installed: `npm i -g playwright && npx playwright install chromium`");
}

function probe(args, input) {
  const run = spawnSync(PYTHON, ["-m", "tests.webauthn_uv_probe", ...args], {
    cwd: BACKEND,
    input: input === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(input),
    encoding: "utf8",
  });
  if (run.status !== 0) throw new Error(`probe ${args[0]} exited ${run.status}: ${run.stderr}`);
  return JSON.parse(run.stdout);
}

/** Runs IN THE PAGE: W3C options JSON in, the registration response JSON out. */
async function register(optionsJSON) {
  const toBuffer = (text) => {
    const padded = text.replace(/-/g, "+").replace(/_/g, "/") + "=".repeat((4 - (text.length % 4)) % 4);
    return Uint8Array.from(atob(padded), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0)).buffer;
  };
  const toText = (buffer) =>
    btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(buffer))).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
  const publicKey = {
    ...optionsJSON,
    challenge: toBuffer(optionsJSON.challenge),
    user: { ...optionsJSON.user, id: toBuffer(optionsJSON.user.id) },
    excludeCredentials: (optionsJSON.excludeCredentials ?? []).map((c) => ({ ...c, id: toBuffer(c.id) })),
  };
  const credential = await navigator.credentials.create({ publicKey });
  return {
    id: credential.id,
    rawId: toText(credential.rawId),
    type: credential.type,
    response: {
      clientDataJSON: toText(credential.response.clientDataJSON),
      attestationObject: toText(credential.response.attestationObject),
      transports: credential.response.getTransports ? credential.response.getTransports() : [],
    },
    clientExtensionResults: credential.getClientExtensionResults(),
  };
}

const AUTHENTICATOR = {
  protocol: "ctap2",
  ctap2Version: "ctap2_1",
  transport: "internal",
  hasResidentKey: true,
  automaticPresenceSimulation: true,
};

async function main() {
  const server = createServer((_, response) => {
    response.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "text/html; charset=utf-8" });
    response.end("<!doctype html><title>webauthn-uv</title>");
  });
  await new Promise((done) => server.listen(0, done));
  const origin = `http://localhost:${server.address().port}`;
  const { chromium } = await loadPlaywright();
  const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: ["--no-sandbox", "--disable-dev-shm-usage"] });
  const failures = [];
  try {
    const page = await browser.newPage();
    await page.goto(`${origin}/`);
    const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
    await cdp.send("WebAuthn.enable", { enableUI: false });

    const verifying = await cdp.send("WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator", {
      options: { ...AUTHENTICATOR, hasUserVerification: true, isUserVerified: true },
    });
    const asked = probe(["options", "localhost", "required"]);
    const control = probe(["verify", origin, "localhost"], {
      options: asked,
      credential: await page.evaluate(register, asked),
    });
    if (!control.accepted) failures.push(`control: a user-verified passkey was refused (${control.error})`);
    await cdp.send("WebAuthn.removeVirtualAuthenticator", { authenticatorId: verifying.authenticatorId });

    await cdp.send("WebAuthn.addVirtualAuthenticator", {
      options: { ...AUTHENTICATOR, hasUserVerification: false },
    });
    const issued = probe(["options", "localhost", "required"]);
    const downgraded = {
      ...issued,
      authenticatorSelection: { ...issued.authenticatorSelection, userVerification: "discouraged" },
    };
    const outcome = probe(["verify", origin, "localhost"], {
      options: issued,
      credential: await page.evaluate(register, downgraded),
    });
    if (outcome.accepted) {
      failures.push("falsifier: a passkey created WITHOUT user verification was accepted");
    } else if (!/User verification is required/.test(outcome.error)) {
      failures.push(`falsifier: refused, but not for user verification (${outcome.error}); it proves nothing`);
    }
  } finally {
    await browser.close();
    server.close();
  }
  for (const line of failures) console.log(`FAIL  ${line}`);
  if (failures.length > 0) process.exit(1);
  console.log("ok    a user-verified passkey is accepted; one without user verification is refused");
}

await main();
```

- Al final de §1 (después de `:62`, antes del `---`):

```markdown
### §1 as amended on 2026-11-04 (own authentication, phase 1)

This section said the password field must not live in ITMS. From own
authentication phase 1 it does: passwords enter the platform and are verified
here. The prohibition it quoted is still kept -- the platform does not use the
OAuth password grant, and a correct password alone admits nothing: it yields a
session without its second factor, which reaches only the second-factor and
enrolment routes (design §2.2). The balance, stated rather than implied:

- **What the platform now holds.** Password verifiers (argon2id with the
  `argon2-cffi` defaults, a 16-byte salt and an HMAC with a versioned pepper
  that never leaves OpenBao) and TOTP secrets (sealed by the vault, bound to
  their row). A compromise of the platform exposes those verifiers and
  secrets; the pepper makes an offline attack on a stolen database need
  OpenBao as well, and passkeys expose no secret at all.
- **What it no longer runs.** A second service with its own administration
  console, its own database, its own upgrade path and its own audit trail
  outside the hash chain. Every sign-in, factor change and lockout is now an
  event in the platform's own chain (invariant 4).

MCP keeps signing in at Keycloak until own authentication phase 3, and the
realm is removed in phase 4.
```

```markdown
  own authentication (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-autenticacion-propia-design.md`):
  a password of 12 to 128 characters, checked against a shipped blocklist and
  stored as argon2id with a pepper held in OpenBao, plus a **mandatory second
  factor** -- a passkey with user verification required, or a TOTP app --
  with ten single-use recovery codes. Failures are counted per account and per
  factor, with an increasing wait from the fifth and the factor disabled at
  the hundredth. Sessions are server-side, carried in a `__Host-` cookie that
  holds only a random identifier, with a 30-minute idle timeout and a 12-hour
  maximum by default; every write needs a custom header and a matching
  `Origin`. "Remember this device" (15 days by default) skips the second
  factor at sign-in only, never for a recent-confirmation action, and **does
  not meet AAL2** on that device -- the operator accepted this knowingly
  (design §0, S2b). Not built: SAML and on-premises Active Directory
  federation (out of scope); sign-in with Microsoft and the contacts' portal
  are phase 2. MCP clients still authenticate through Keycloak until phase 3.
```

- La tabla de amenazas (`:165-178`) gana dos filas después de «Operator abuse / over-privilege»:

```markdown
| Stolen or guessed operator password | Mandatory second factor; shipped blocklist; per-account and per-factor failure counters with backoff and a 100-failure disable; generic answers that take the same work whether or not the account exists |
| Theft of the platform database | Passwords stored only as peppered argon2id (pepper in OpenBao), TOTP secrets sealed by the vault, session and device identifiers stored only as SHA-256 |
```

`CLAUDE.md` 1c(a) **no cambia** (diseño §9: ya está redactada sin nombrar proveedor). No se edita.

`deploy/README.md:424-429`, el párrafo «This creates the Ed25519 `job-signing` transit key, …» gana, al final:

```markdown
Since own authentication phase 1 it also creates two transit keys for sign-in:
`auth-pepper` (HMAC, the versioned pepper every password verifier is
computed with) and `auth-signing` (ECDSA P-256, which signs the assistant's
internal tokens and, from phase 3, MCP access tokens). Neither key ever leaves
OpenBao. **On an install that ran `openbao-init` before, re-run it and re-load
the policy** (`bao policy write its-app /bao/its-app.hcl`, as in 3.3), or the
API cannot verify a password.
```

(Si la Task 2 ya dejó un texto equivalente en este párrafo, se conserva el suyo y se comprueba que diga las dos
claves y el paso de la política.) El despliegue completo lo absorbe el proyecto 4 (diseño §9); esta tarea no toca
`deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `.env.example` ni los scripts.
